Fix a named positively oriented inertial laboratory chart with coordinates
$(x,y,z,t)$, spatial domain $\mathbb R^3$, and time domain $\mathbb R$. Adopt SI
units, a vacuum speed $c>0$, an angular frequency $\omega>0$, and
$k_0:=\omega/c$ (so $[k_0]=\mathrm{m}^{-1}$). Let
$\mathbf x_\perp:=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$. Use the unitary two-dimensional
Fourier transform $\mathcal F_2$ whose Schwartz-space convention is
$$\widehat f(\boldsymbol\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}f(\mathbf x_\perp) e^{-2\pi i\mathbf x_\perp\cdot\boldsymbol\xi}\,d^2\mathbf x_\perp,$$
and whose inverse is its unitary $L^2$ extension. The variable
$\boldsymbol\xi$ is in cycles per metre; its associated angular spatial
wavevector is $\mathbf q:=2\pi\boldsymbol\xi$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, with
$|\mathbf q|^2:=q_x^2+q_y^2$.

Choose $0<\delta<1$ and $u_0\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ with
$\mathcal F_2u_0$ supported, up to null sets, in
$D_\delta:=\{\boldsymbol\xi:|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|\le\delta k_0\}$.
For $z\in\mathbb R$ put
$$k_z(\boldsymbol\xi):=\sqrt{k_0^2-|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|^2},$$
which is real and strictly positive on $D_\delta$, and define the exact scalar
and paraxial scalar propagators as the $L^2$ equivalence classes
$$u_{\mathrm{exact}}(z):=\mathcal F_2^{-1}\!\left[ e^{izk_z(\boldsymbol\xi)}\,\mathcal F_2u_0(\boldsymbol\xi)\right],\qquad u_{\mathrm{par}}(z):=e^{ik_0z}\mathcal F_2^{-1}\!\left[ e^{-iz|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|^2/(2k_0)}\,\mathcal F_2u_0(\boldsymbol\xi)\right].$$
The associated real scalar fields are the real parts of these phasors multiplied
by $e^{-i\omega t}$. If $u_0$ carries $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, both propagated
fields carry the same unit. “Exact” here names the exact positive axial
dispersion multiplier inside this scalar model; it does not assert exact
Maxwell validity. Forward propagation is $z\ge0$; the formulas also define the
mathematical continuation to negative $z$.

At a fixed $\boldsymbol\xi\in D_\delta$, write
$\mathbf K(\boldsymbol\xi):=(2\pi\xi_x,2\pi\xi_y,k_z(\boldsymbol\xi))$.
A candidate monochromatic vector plane-wave mode at frequency $\omega$ has
complex amplitudes $\mathbf e,\mathbf b\in\mathbb C^3$ in the real-field
encoding $e^{i(\mathbf K\cdot(x,y,z)-\omega t)}$. It is called an exact
source-free vacuum mode only when its associated real fields satisfy the
adopted source-free vacuum Maxwell equations. The longitudinal electric
coefficient is $e_z$, and
$\mathbf e_\perp:=(e_x,e_y)$ has norm
$|\mathbf e_\perp|^2:=|e_x|^2+|e_y|^2$. No scalar/vector polarization
factorization is part of this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator whose spectral projection valued measure $E$ is supported on $(0,\infty)$. For $\xi\in H$, put $\mu_\xi(B)=\langle E(B)\xi,\xi\rangle$. Define
$$D(A^{1/2})=\left\{\xi\in H:\int_{(0,\infty)}\lambda\,d\mu_\xi(\lambda)<\infty\right\}.$$
For $z\in\mathbb C$ and $\xi\in D(A^{1/2})$, define $A^{-iz/2}\xi$ by the unbounded Borel functional calculus for the function $\lambda\mapsto \exp(-iz\log(\lambda)/2)$. On the closed strip $S=\{z:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq1\}$, this vector is defined, strongly continuous in $z$, and satisfies
$$\|A^{-iz/2}\xi\|^2\leq\|\xi\|^2+\|A^{1/2}\xi\|^2.$$
The map $z\mapsto A^{-iz/2}\xi$ is norm-holomorphic on the open strip $S^\circ$.

A closed surface here is a compact, connected topological $2$-manifold without boundary: each point has a neighborhood homeomorphic to an open disk in $\mathbb R^2$. It is orientable when the local integer-homology system with fiber $H_2(S,S\setminus\{x\};\mathbb Z)$ has a continuous section that generates each fiber; this is the $R$-orientation definition with coefficient ring $R=\mathbb Z$.

A finite cellulation $K$ of $S$ is a finite $2$-dimensional CW decomposition whose open $2$-cells are disks. Write $V,E,F$ for its finite vertex, edge, and face sets. The primal graph has vertices $V$ and edges $E$. The dual graph has one vertex for each face and one dual edge crossing each primal edge, joining the two incident face sides; loops and multiple edges are allowed. Assume both graphs are connected. Let $\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo two. Incidence multiplicities are reduced modulo two: $\partial_1:\mathbb F_2^E\to\mathbb F_2^V$ sends each edge to the sum of its endpoint incidences, and $\partial_2:\mathbb F_2^F\to\mathbb F_2^E$ sends each face to its boundary-edge incidence vector. These cellular boundary maps satisfy $\partial_1\partial_2=0$. Since $S$ has no boundary, each edge has two incident face sides, counted with multiplicity, so $\partial_2(\sum_{f\in F}f)=0$.

Identify $E$ with a finite region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z$ and use the finite local spin matrix algebra on $\Lambda$ with spin dimension $q=2$. The edge Hilbert space is $\mathcal H_K=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes E}$, so $\dim\mathcal H_K=2^{|E|}$. Let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. For $a,b\in\mathbb F_2^E$, define $X(a)=\bigotimes_{e\in E}X^{a_e}$, $Z(b)=\bigotimes_{e\in E}Z^{b_e}$, and $P(a,b)=X(a)Z(b)$. For a vertex $v$ and face $f$, put $A_v=X(\partial_1^T v)$ and $B_f=Z(\partial_2 f)$, where $v$ and $f$ also denote the corresponding basis vectors. Thus $A_v$ is the product of $X$ over incident edges with odd incidence, and $B_f$ is the product of $Z$ over boundary edges with odd incidence. The identity $\partial_1\partial_2=0$ makes every $A_v$ commute with every $B_f$; each is a self-adjoint involution.

For positive real coefficients $J_v,K_f$, define the toric-code Hamiltonian

$$H_K=\sum_{v\in V}J_v\frac{I-A_v}{2}+\sum_{f\in F}K_f\frac{I-B_f}{2}.$$

The Pauli operators are dimensionless. In a physical interpretation, $J_v,K_f$ have energy units (joules in SI); here they are positive mathematical coefficients and no measured values are asserted. A simultaneous $+1$ eigenvector of all $A_v,B_f$ is called a ground vector. The ground space is their common $+1$ eigenspace, equivalently $\ker H_K$.

For the square $L\times L$ torus, $L\ge3$, use vertices $\mathbb Z_L^2$, horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbor edges, and the $L^2$ square faces, with periodic boundary conditions. A coordinate cycle is a closed edge path winding once around one coordinate direction. Let $p_1,p_2$ be the horizontal and vertical coordinate cycles in the primal graph, and let $q_1,q_2$ be the corresponding vertical and horizontal coordinate cycles in the dual graph, chosen so that $I(p_i,q_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The mod-two intersection number is the parity of primal edges crossed by a dual cycle. A topological disk is a subset homeomorphic to the closed unit disk. A finite edge support is disk-local with full complement cycles if it is contained in a topological disk whose complement contains representatives of these two primal and two dual coordinate cycles. The phrase “both independent homology cycles” below refers to these two primal cycles and their dual crossing representatives.

An open primal path is a path in the vertex-edge graph; its $Z$ string is $Z(b)$ for its edge chain $b$. An open dual path is a path in the face-adjacency graph; its $X$ string is $X(a)$ for the primal edges crossed by that dual path. A closed string has zero endpoint boundary in the corresponding primal or dual graph. The support of an operator is a finite edge set $S$ such that the operator is a matrix on $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes S}$ tensored with the identity on $E\setminus S$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited through the cited Hall supplier. Let
$V=\mathbb C^2$ with ordered orthonormal basis $|\uparrow\rangle,|\downarrow\rangle$.
On $V$ define
$$ E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}. $$
They satisfy $[H,E]=2E$, $[H,F]=-2F$, and $[E,F]=H$, and therefore define
the standard two-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$.
Write $S^+=E$, $S^-=F$, and $S^z=H/2$.

For each integer $N\geq1$, the spin space is
$\mathcal H_N=V^{\otimes N}$ with its tensor-product inner product. If $A$ is
an endomorphism of $V$, let $A_j$ act as $A$ on factor $j$ and as the identity
on the other factors. Define the diagonal generators
$$ S_N^+=\sum_{j=1}^N E_j,\qquad S_N^-=\sum_{j=1}^N F_j,\qquad S_N^z=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^N H_j. $$
For $m\in\{-N/2,-N/2+1,\ldots,N/2\}$, its weight space is
$\mathcal H_{N,m}=\ker(S_N^z-mI)$. These are dimensionless matrices in the
algebraic spin convention.

For each integer $r\geq0$, define $V(r)$ to be the vector space
$\mathbb C[x,y]_r$ of homogeneous polynomials of degree $r$, with
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action
$$ E=x\partial_y,\qquad F=y\partial_x,\qquad H=x\partial_x-y\partial_y. $$
The ordered monomials $x^{r-k}y^k$ for $0\leq k\leq r$ form its basis.
Under $x\mapsto|\uparrow\rangle$ and $y\mapsto|\downarrow\rangle$,
$V(1)$ is the representation on $V$ above. A tensor power $V(1)^{\otimes N}$
uses the diagonal action defined by the sums $S_N^+,S_N^-,2S_N^z$.

Let $q_H>1$ be a prime power and fix a finite field $\mathbb F_{q_H}$ of that
cardinality. Put $\nu=\sqrt{q_H}>1$ and $K=\mathbb Q(\nu)$. The representation category of
the one-vertex, no-arrow quiver over $\mathbb F_{q_H}$ is the category of
finite-dimensional $\mathbb F_{q_H}$-vector spaces, with unique simple object
$S=\mathbb F_{q_H}$. Its Hall composition algebra is the subalgebra generated
by the class $[S]$ in the twisted Hall algebra with the normalization of the
Ringel supplier. The rank-one positive quantum half is
$U_\nu^+(\mathfrak{sl}_2)=K[E]$. The canonical Ringel map $E\mapsto[S]$
identifies this positive half with the composition algebra; the finite-Dynkin
criterion identifies it with the full Hall algebra in this one-vertex case.

$\nu=\sqrt{q_H}>1$ and $K=\mathbb Q(\nu)$. The representation category
$\mathcal A=\mathrm{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\mathbb F_{q_H}}$ of the one-vertex,
no-arrow quiver has one simple isomorphism class, represented by
$S=\mathbb F_{q_H}$. For objects $M,N$, write
$\chi_0(M,N)=\dim_{\mathbb F_{q_H}}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)-
\dim_{\mathbb F_{q_H}}\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)$. In the Hall convention of
[[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]], the Hall space is
$H_{\mathcal A,\nu}=\bigoplus_{[M]}K[M]$, with basis $[M]$ indexed by
isomorphism classes and product
$$[M]\star[N]=\nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}\sum_{[L]}g^L_{M,N}[L],$$
where $g^L_{M,N}$ counts subspaces $N'\subseteq L$ with $N'\cong N$ and
$L/N'\cong M$, or equivalently short exact sequences
$0\to N\to L\to M\to0$. Thus the twist is part of the multiplication.
For $M\cong\mathbb F_{q_H}^{m}$ and $N\cong\mathbb F_{q_H}^{n}$,
$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)=mn$ and every short exact sequence splits, so
$\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)=0$ and $\chi_0(M,N)=mn$.

By [[def-extended-hall-algebra-and-composition-subalgebra]], the composition
subalgebra is the subalgebra of this Hall algebra generated by the classes of
simple objects; its torus extension is the distinct extended composition
subalgebra. Denote the former by $\mathcal C$ here, so
$\mathcal C=K\langle[S]\rangle\subseteq H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$. The rank-one
positive quantum half is $U_\nu^+(\mathfrak{sl}_2)=K[E]$, the polynomial
algebra on one generator. The Ringel map $E\mapsto[S]$ embeds this positive
half with image $\mathcal C$; since the one-vertex graph is finite Dynkin type
$A_1$, the finite-Dynkin criterion identifies $\mathcal C$ with the full Hall
algebra in this case. The simple object is unique up to isomorphism, not as a
chosen representative. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the cited
Ringel supplier.

diagonal spin generators $S_N^+,S_N^-,S_N^z$ be the sums of the one-site
matrices $E,F,H/2$ defined in the spin convention. For any distinct sites
$i,j$, let $P_{ij}$ exchange tensor factors $i$ and $j$. Then
$$ [P_{ij},S_N^+]=[P_{ij},S_N^-]=[P_{ij},S_N^z]=0. $$

For $N\geq3$, take an auxiliary copy $V_a=\mathbb C^2$ and define
$P_{aj}$ as the flip of $V_a$ and site $j$. With
$$ R_{aj}(u)=uI+iP_{aj},\qquad T_a(u)=R_{aN}(u)\cdots R_{a1}(u),\qquad t(u)=\operatorname{tr}_a T_a(u)\quad(u\in\mathbb C), $$
where products act rightmost first and the trace is the ordinary finite
trace over $V_a$, every transfer matrix preserves the diagonal spin action:
$$ [t(u),S_N^+]=[t(u),S_N^-]=[t(u),S_N^z]=0. $$
Use the periodic convention $P_{N,N+1}=P_{N,1}$. For real $J,c$, the
periodic XXX matrix
$$ H_N=J\sum_{j=1}^N P_{j,j+1}+cI $$
is Hermitian and commutes with all three generators. When $H_N$ is interpreted as a
physical energy, $J$ and $c$ have joule units; $u$ is dimensionless.

For $m\in\{-N/2,-N/2+1,\ldots,N/2\}$, set
$\mathcal H_{N,m}=\ker(S_N^z-mI)$. For real $\beta$, define the finite
matrix exponential by its norm-convergent power series and put
$Z_N(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_N}e^{-\beta H_N}$. Then
$$ Z_N(\beta)=\sum_m \operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_{N,m}} \left(e^{-\beta H_N}\big|_{\mathcal H_{N,m}}\right). $$
In a physical Gibbs interpretation, $\beta$ has inverse-joule units.

are its matrix units and $X_{rs}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_N)$, and
define the partial trace by $\operatorname{tr}_aX:=X_{11}+X_{22}$. With

Let $D$ be a KLR datum on a symmetrizable Cartan datum with no imaginary
simple roots, over a field $k$, in the conventions of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Let $R_D$
be the resulting graded KLR algebra, and let $K_0(R_D)$ be the Grothendieck
group of its graded projectives. Put
$\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[q_{\mathrm{gr}},q_{\mathrm{gr}}^{-1}]$, where
$q_{\mathrm{gr}}$ is the Laurent grading variable denoted by $q$ in the
divided-power integral form, and let $\mathcal A f_D$ be the integral
negative quantum half. The canonical map
$\gamma_D:\mathcal A f_D\to K_0(R_D)$ is an isomorphism of
$\mathcal A$-algebras and graded twisted bialgebras; $q_{\mathrm{gr}}$ records
the grading shift. Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited through this supplier.

For each integer $n\geq1$, the irreducible highest-weight-$n$ module $V(n)$
defined by homogeneous polynomials of degree $n$ has $H$-weights
$n,n-2,\ldots,-n$, each with multiplicity one. The diagonal
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module
$V(1)^{\otimes n}$ has $H$-weight $n-2k$ with multiplicity
$\binom nk$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Here $H=2S^z$.

For real $h$ and $\beta$, define the zero-exchange finite matrix
$H_n^{(0)}=-hS_n^z$ on $V(1)^{\otimes n}$ and its partition trace
$Z_n(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}\exp(-\beta H_n^{(0)})$. Then
$$ Z_n(\beta)=\bigl(2\cosh(\beta h/2)\bigr)^n, \qquad \cosh x:=\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2. $$
For a Gibbs interpretation, $h$ is an energy coefficient, $S_n^z$ is
dimensionless, and $\beta$ has inverse-energy units. The KLR isomorphism
supplies the negative-half categorification stated above; it supplies no
identification with either finite-dimensional spin module, no
tensor-product categorical realization, and no spin-chain energy spectrum.

statement.before:
On a fixed two-site spin-half space, a rank-one Hall realization, a KLR
negative-half Grothendieck isomorphism, and the diagonal
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module decomposition determine the spectrum and Gibbs
partition trace of every Hamiltonian commuting with that action.
statement.proposed:
Fix $W=V(1)\otimes V(1)$ with its tensor-product inner product and its diagonal
representation $\rho:\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(W)$
from the spin convention, together with the rank-one Hall data at $q_H=2$ and
the type-$A_1$ KLR negative-half Grothendieck isomorphism over $\mathbb Q$.
Let
$$\mathscr H_\rho=\{A\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(W):A=A^*,\ [A,\rho(X)]=0\text{ for every }X\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\},$$
where $A^*$ is the adjoint for the stated inner product. For an endomorphism
$D$ of $W$, set $\exp(D)=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}D^r/r!$, convergent in operator
norm, and let $\operatorname{Tr}_W$ denote the basis-independent trace on
endomorphisms of $W$. For
$C\in\mathscr H_\rho$ and $\beta\geq0$, define its partition trace by
$$Z_C(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_W(\exp(-\beta C)).$$
The claim that the fixed algebraic data
uniquely determine the spectrum and partition trace of every member of
$\mathscr H_\rho$ means that any $A,B\in\mathscr H_\rho$ have the same
eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity and satisfy
$$Z_A(\beta)=Z_B(\beta)\quad\text{for every }\beta\geq0.$$
This uniqueness claim is false. If the endomorphisms are interpreted as
energies, $\beta$ has inverse-energy units.

statement.before: For a finite-dimensional completely positive trace-preserving semigroup, nonincrease of relative entropy to a faithful stationary Gibbs density is sufficient to guarantee that the Gibbs density is the unique stationary density and that every initial density converges to it.
statement.proposed: Let $d\geq1$ and let $(T_t)_{t\geq0}$ be complex-linear maps on $M_d(\mathbb C)$ that are completely positive (each finite ancilla amplification preserves positive matrices) and trace-preserving ($\operatorname{Tr}(T_t(X))=\operatorname{Tr}X$ for every $X$), with $T_0=\operatorname{id}$ and $T_{t+s}=T_t\circ T_s$ for all $s,t\geq0$. A density matrix $\rho$ means $\rho=\rho^*$, $v^*\rho v\geq0$ for every $v\in\mathbb C^d$, and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$; it is faithful when $v^*\rho v>0$ for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb C^d$. For a Hermitian matrix $H\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ and $\beta\in\mathbb R$, define $Z_\beta:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})>0$ and the Gibbs density $\sigma_\beta:=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$. A density matrix $\sigma$ is stationary for $(T_t)$ when $T_t(\sigma)=\sigma$ for every $t\geq0$. For a density matrix $\rho$ and faithful density $\sigma$, let $D(\rho\|\sigma):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\sigma)$, using the natural logarithm, the finite spectral logarithm on the support of $\rho$, and $0\log0:=0$. The claim refuted here is that nonincrease of relative entropy to a faithful stationary Gibbs density is sufficient to guarantee that the Gibbs density is the unique stationary density and that every initial density converges to it.

Let $\mathcal H$ have finite dimension, let $H=H^*$ have energy unit joules, let $\hbar>0$ have unit joule-seconds, and let $\rho$ be a positive-definite trace-one matrix satisfying $[\rho,H]=0$. Define $\omega(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ and $\alpha_t(A):=e^{iHt/\hbar}Ae^{-iHt/\hbar}$. Let $J_L$ be the total lattice current of the finite-volume current definition and center it with respect to this same $\rho$, setting $J:=J_L-\omega(J_L)I$. In particular, one may take the finite-temperature Gibbs density in the definition. Then $J=J^*$, as established by the local continuity result. For $m\ge1$, let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$ be linearly independent conserved matrices, $[H,Q_a]=0$. Put
$$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*Q_b),\qquad v_a:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*J).$$
Then $G$ is positive definite, the finite Cesàro limit exists, and
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}\,\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(J)J\right)\,dt\;\ge\;v^*G^{-1}v\;\ge0.$$
This is a finite-dimensional persistent-correlation bound. It does not identify a thermodynamic Drude weight or assert that either volume/time order of limits exists.
statement.proposed:
Take the finite-chain data of the current definition on $\mathcal H_L$ and identify $\mathcal H:=\mathcal H_L$. Let $H=H^*$ have energy unit joules, let $\hbar>0$ have unit joule-seconds, and let $\rho$ be a positive-definite trace-one matrix satisfying $[\rho,H]=0$. Define $\omega(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ and $\alpha_t(A):=e^{iHt/\hbar}Ae^{-iHt/\hbar}$. Let $J_L$ be the total lattice current of the finite-volume current definition and center it with respect to this same $\rho$, setting $J:=J_L-\omega(J_L)I$. With no identification of $H$ and $H_L$, the estimate below is an abstract bound for this observable under $\alpha_t$. Its lattice-transport specialization further takes $H=H_L$; then the Gibbs density $\rho_{\beta,L}$ in that definition is stationary and is an admissible choice of $\rho$. More generally, $\rho_{\beta,L}$ can be used with another $H$ exactly when it also satisfies $[\rho_{\beta,L},H]=0$. Then $J=J^*$, as established by the local continuity result. For $m\ge1$, let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$ be linearly independent conserved matrices, $[H,Q_a]=0$. Put
$$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*Q_b),\qquad v_a:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*J).$$
Then $G$ is positive definite, the finite Cesàro limit exists, and
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}\,\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(J)J\right)\,dt\;\ge\;v^*G^{-1}v\;\ge0.$$
This is a finite-dimensional persistent-correlation bound. It does not identify a thermodynamic Drude weight or assert that either volume/time order of limits exists.

statement.before:
For every integer $N\ge1$ and real skew-symmetric matrix $A\in M_{2N}(\mathbb R)$, there are an orthogonal real matrix $O$ and numbers $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_N\ge0$ such that
$$OAO^{\mathsf T}=\bigoplus_{r=1}^N\begin{pmatrix}0&\epsilon_r\\-\epsilon_r&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
The positive $\epsilon_r$ are the positive singular values of $A$, each listed once for its two-dimensional invariant plane; zero values pair the kernel directions.
statement.proposed:
For every integer $N\ge1$ and real skew-symmetric matrix $A\in M_{2N}(\mathbb R)$, there are an orthogonal real matrix $O$ and numbers $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_N\ge0$ such that
$$OAO^{\mathsf T}=\bigoplus_{r=1}^N\begin{pmatrix}0&\epsilon_r\\-\epsilon_r&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
For a real square matrix $A$, $A^{\mathsf T}A$ is positive semidefinite because $v^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}Av=\sum_j(Av)_j^2\ge0$ for every real column vector $v$. Its singular-value multiset is the multiset of nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of $A^{\mathsf T}A$, each eigenvalue repeated according to its eigenspace dimension. In the displayed form, the positive $\epsilon_r$ are precisely the positive singular values of $A$: each block with $\epsilon_r>0$ contributes two entries equal to $\epsilon_r$, counting repeated block values separately. Every zero block pairs two kernel directions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ with normalized measure $dk/(2\pi)$, and let $\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)$ have inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\langle x_j,y_j\rangle_{\mathbb C^2}$, linear in the first argument. For a finitely supported sequence $x=(x_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}$ define
$$\mathcal F_0x(k)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}x_j e^{ijk},\qquad k\in\mathbb T,$$
componentwise. Then $\mathcal F_0$ preserves inner products on finitely supported sequences and has a unique extension to a unitary $\mathcal F:\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)\to L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$.
statement.proposed:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and let $m_{\mathbb T}$ be its normalized Borel probability measure, so in the angle coordinate its integral is $\int_{\mathbb T}F\,dm_{\mathbb T}=\int_0^{2\pi}F(k)\,dk/(2\pi)$, obtained from the normalized one-dimensional torus by $k=2\pi x$. On $\mathbb C^2$ use $\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathbb C^2}=u_1\overline{v_1}+u_2\overline{v_2}$ and $\|u\|_{\mathbb C^2}^2=|u_1|^2+|u_2|^2$, linear in the first argument. Define
$$\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2):=\left\{x=(x_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}:x_j\in\mathbb C^2,\ \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\|x_j\|_{\mathbb C^2}^2<\infty\right\},\quad \langle x,y\rangle_{\ell^2}:=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\langle x_j,y_j\rangle_{\mathbb C^2}.$$
Define $L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$ to be the vector space of pairs of Borel-measurable functions $f=(f_1,f_2):\mathbb T\to\mathbb C^2$ with $\int_{\mathbb T}(|f_1|^2+|f_2|^2)\,dm_{\mathbb T}<\infty$, modulo equality $m_{\mathbb T}$-almost everywhere, with inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_{L^2}:=\int_{\mathbb T}\bigl(f_1\overline{g_1}+f_2\overline{g_2}\bigr)\,dm_{\mathbb T}.$$
These pairings are linear in the first argument. The square-summable-family supplier gives the scalar $\ell^2$ norm and pairing used coordinatewise. The $L^2$ space is the pair of scalar $L^2$ quotient spaces with the displayed sum inner product and completeness convention. Let $c_{00}(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2):=\{x\in\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2):\{j:x_j\ne0\}\text{ is finite}\}$. Define the linear map
$$\mathcal F_0x(k)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}x_j e^{ijk},\qquad k\in\mathbb T,$$
componentwise, from $c_{00}(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)$ to $L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$. Its values are continuous finite sums and therefore belong to this $L^2$ space. Then $\mathcal F_0$ preserves inner products on finitely supported sequences and has a unique extension to a surjective linear isometry (a unitary map) $\mathcal F:\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)\to L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $h,J\in\mathbb R$ be energies in joules, with the finite-chain convention of the open transverse Ising definition. On $\mathcal K=\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)$, write $x_j=(u_j,v_j)$ and define the complex-linear operator
$$ (A_\infty x)_j=\bigl(2h v_j-2Jv_{j-1},\,-2h u_j+2Ju_{j+1}\bigr),\qquad K_\infty=iA_\infty. $$
Let $T^*$ denote the Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]). Use the Fourier unitary $\mathcal F x(k)=\sum_jx_je^{ijk}$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ with normalized measure. Then $\mathcal F K_\infty\mathcal F^{-1}$ is multiplication by the matrix
$$M(k)=\begin{pmatrix}0&2i(h-Je^{ik})\\-2i(h-Je^{-ik})&0\end{pmatrix},$$
whose eigenvalues are $\pm\epsilon(k)$ with
$$\epsilon(k)=2\sqrt{h^2+J^2-2hJ\cos k}.$$
With spectrum defined by failure of a bounded two-sided inverse, its spectrum is exactly $\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb T}\{-\epsilon(k),\epsilon(k)\}$. The bottom of its positive band is
$$\Delta_{\mathrm{bulk}}=\min_k\epsilon(k)=2\bigl||h|-|J|\bigr|,$$
so this one-particle band closes exactly when $|h|=|J|$. This statement does not assert uniqueness of an infinite spin-chain ground state or a thermodynamic-limit singularity.
statement.proposed:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $h,J\in\mathbb R$ be energies in joules, with the convention of the open-chain definition: the field coefficient is $h$ and the adjacent-site bond coefficient is $J$, with no bond joining the final site to the first. On $\mathcal K=\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)$, write $x_j=(u_j,v_j)$ and define the everywhere-defined complex-linear operator $A_\infty:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K$ by
$$ (A_\infty x)_j=\bigl(2h v_j-2Jv_{j-1},\,-2h u_j+2Ju_{j+1}\bigr),\qquad K_\infty=iA_\infty. $$
For any bounded operator $T$ on the Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, let $T^*$ denote its Hilbert adjoint. Use the Fourier unitary $\mathcal F x(k)=\sum_jx_je^{ijk}$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ with normalized measure. Define the continuous matrix symbol
$$M(k)=\begin{pmatrix}0&2i(h-Je^{ik})\\-2i(h-Je^{-ik})&0\end{pmatrix},$$
whose eigenvalues are $\pm\epsilon(k)$, where
$$\epsilon(k)=2\sqrt{h^2+J^2-2hJ\cos k}.$$
For a $2\times2$ matrix $C$ acting on the defined $\mathbb C^2$, write $\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup\{\|Cv\|_{\mathbb C^2}:\|v\|_{\mathbb C^2}=1\}$. Then $\|M(k)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=2|h-Je^{ik}|\le2(|h|+|J|)$. Define $\mathsf M:L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)\to L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$ by $(\mathsf Mf)(k)=M(k)f(k)$ almost everywhere. This is an everywhere-defined bounded multiplication operator, and $\mathcal F K_\infty\mathcal F^{-1}=\mathsf M$.
By the stated resolvent convention, $\lambda\in\sigma(K_\infty)$ exactly when $\lambda I_{\mathcal K}-K_\infty$ has no bounded everywhere-defined two-sided inverse on $\mathcal K$. Its spectrum is exactly $\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb T}\{-\epsilon(k),\epsilon(k)\}$. The nonnegative band is $\epsilon(\mathbb T)$, whose minimum is
$$\Delta_{\mathrm{bulk}}=\min_k\epsilon(k)=2\bigl||h|-|J|\bigr|,$$
so this one-particle band closes exactly when $|h|=|J|$. This statement does not assert uniqueness of an infinite spin-chain ground state or a thermodynamic-limit singularity.

statement.before: For the finite open chain on $N\ge1$ sites with $H_N(h,J)=-h\sum_jZ_j-J\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}X_jX_{j+1}$, when $h=0$ and $J>0$ the ground configurations in the $X$ basis are exactly the two fully aligned configurations. For $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $h,J$ in joules, the trace is $Z_N(\beta,h,J)=\prod_r2\cosh(\beta\epsilon_r/2)$ with the open-chain mode energies $\epsilon_r$, and for every fixed finite $N$ the function $Z_N$ is strictly positive and real-analytic for all real $\beta,h,J$.
statement.proposed:
Let $h,J\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite open chain on $N\ge1$ sites, let $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ and $H_N(h,J)=-h\sum_{j=1}^NZ_j-J\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}X_jX_{j+1}$ as in the open-chain definition. For $s_j\in\{-1,1\}$ set $x_{s_j}=2^{-1/2}(1,s_j)^{\mathsf T}$, $z_{+1}=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}$, and $z_{-1}=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}$, and define the $X$- and $Z$-product basis vectors $|s\rangle_X=\bigotimes_{j=1}^Nx_{s_j}$ and $|s\rangle_Z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^Nz_{s_j}$ for $s=(s_1,\ldots,s_N)\in\{-1,1\}^N$. These are eigenbases with $X_j|s\rangle_X=s_j|s\rangle_X$ and $Z_j|s\rangle_Z=s_j|s\rangle_Z$. When $H_N$ is diagonal in one of these product bases $B\in\{X,Z\}$, let $E_B(s)$ be its diagonal matrix entry at $|s\rangle_B$; a ground configuration in that basis is a label $s$ minimizing $E_B$ over $\{-1,1\}^N$.

When $h=0$ and $J>0$, the ground configurations in the $X$ product basis are exactly $s=(1,\ldots,1)$ and $s=(-1,\ldots,-1)$. When $J=0$ and $h\ne0$, the unique ground configuration in the $Z$ product basis has $s_j=1$ at every site if $h>0$ and $s_j=-1$ at every site if $h<0$; thus the minimizing orientation is specified for both signs of $h$. For $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $h,J$ in joules, the trace is $Z_N(\beta,h,J)=\prod_r2\cosh(\beta\epsilon_r/2)$ with the open-chain mode energies $\epsilon_r$. For each fixed finite $N$, the function $Z_N(\beta,h,J)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_N}(e^{-\beta H_N(h,J)})$ is strictly positive and real-analytic on $\mathbb R^3$; here real-analytic means that near every real triple $(\beta,h,J)$ it is represented by a convergent real power series in those three parameters.

At a piece endpoint, use the corresponding one-sided derivative as the tangent. On each piece, pair this tangent $\dot\gamma(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ with $\omega_{\gamma(t)}\in T^*_{\gamma(t)}M$. $$\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega):=\sum_j\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))\,dt,$$

$0<z<1$, define
$$|\psi_z\rangle=\sqrt{1-z}\sum_{n=0}^\infty z^{n/2} |n\rangle_R\otimes|n\rangle_L.$$
Define its left-traced operator $\rho_R$ by
$$\langle m|\rho_R|n\rangle =\sum_{k=0}^\infty \langle m,k|\psi_z\rangle\overline{\langle n,k|\psi_z\rangle}.$$
This coefficient formula defines the partial trace of this rank-one operator
over the left oscillator. The vector is normalized, and $\rho_R$ is a
positive diagonal operator with eigenvalues $p_n=(1-z)z^n$, whose sum is one.
Its entropy in nats, using the natural logarithm, is
$$S(\rho_R)=-\sum_{n=0}^\infty p_n\ln p_n =-\ln(1-z)-\frac{z\ln z}{1-z}.$$
This explicitly constructed pair of oscillator modes does not construct a
tensor-product factorization of the continuum right-wedge Hilbert space or a
density matrix for its local von Neumann algebra.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$. Let $\rho:I\to\operatorname{End}(H)$ be a path whose real and imaginary matrix entries are twice continuously differentiable, such that each $\rho(\varepsilon)$ is self-adjoint with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one. Suppose $\rho(0)=\sigma$ and every eigenvalue of $\sigma$ is strictly positive. Define $K_\sigma:=-\log\sigma$ by spectral calculus and let $s(\tau):=-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)$ with the finite spectral convention $0\log0:=0$. Then

$$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}s(\rho(\varepsilon))\right|_{\varepsilon=0}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho'(0)K_\sigma).$$

The finite relative entropy $D(\rho(\varepsilon)\|\sigma)$ has zero first derivative at $\varepsilon=0$. These are finite-dimensional mathematical statements and make no continuum or gravitational claim.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the
curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ with
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=g^{ac}R_{abcd}$. Let $(M,g_0)$ be a smooth,
time-oriented, globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, and let
$H_0\subset M$ be a smooth embedded null hypersurface. Its smooth,
nowhere-zero, future null generator $k_0$ is affine, $\nabla_{k_0}k_0=0$,
with screen and expansion conventions as in the smooth null-screen definition.
Fix a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold $C$ and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For each dimensionless $\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, supply a
smooth time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metric $g_\epsilon$, a
smooth null hypersurface $H_\epsilon$, and a smooth map
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon$$
such that $\partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon$,
$k_\epsilon$ is future-directed and affine, and every
$\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ is an embedding with spacelike
image. The family supplies a fixed identification of generator labels and a
fixed affine normalization across $\epsilon$. With $[\lambda]=L$, this
parameterization gives $[k_\epsilon]=1$ in length coordinates.

Write $q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$ for the
positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let $\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be
its Riemannian area density. Call the reference geometry stationary in this
model when its screen deformation form $B_0$ vanishes along every generator;
then its expansion $\theta_0$ and shear $\sigma_0$ vanish by definition. Define
$\theta_\epsilon(\lambda,y)$ as the screen expansion along
$\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)$ and
$\delta\theta:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon\right|_{0}$. Use
the stress tensor $T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}[g_\epsilon,\omega_\epsilon]$
supplied by the chosen Hadamard state family and one fixed local
renormalization prescription in the semiclassical model. No independent
graviton-fluctuation source is included in this perturbative family.
Select its Einstein-Hilbert submodel by setting the curvature-squared
couplings to zero, and define
$\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon
(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\right|_0$.
Here $G_N>0$ is Newton's constant with natural-unit dimension $L^2$;
$[\lambda]=L$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, $[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$, and
$[\delta A]=L^2$.

Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, its tail is absolutely integrable on
each generator, and
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$
where $dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}$ is the reference background area density.
Adopt, only to first order in $\epsilon$, the linearized focusing equation and
future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Terms quadratic in expansion or shear are omitted only at this first
perturbative order: both vanish in the stationary reference geometry and are
of order $\epsilon$ in the supplied family, so their squares are of order
$\epsilon^2$.
This postulate is an adopted model equation; it neither asserts that the model
describes nature nor identifies its null-stress moment with modular energy or
entropy.
statement.proposed:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the
curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ with
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=g^{ac}R_{abcd}$. Let $M$ be a fixed Hausdorff,
second-countable, oriented smooth four-manifold. For each dimensionless
$\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, supply a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g_\epsilon$ on $M$ with the stated signature and a time orientation (a chosen
future timelike cone). Each $(M,g_\epsilon)$ is globally hyperbolic: it is
strongly causal, meaning every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods that
each causal curve meets in a connected parameter interval, and each causal
diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact. Here causal curves are piecewise
$C^1$ with consistently future- or past-directed causal tangent, and
$J^\pm(p)$ denote points reachable from or reaching $p$ by such curves.

For each $\epsilon$, let $H_\epsilon\subset M$ be a smooth embedded
three-dimensional submanifold whose induced metric has a one-dimensional
radical at every point. Its smooth nowhere-zero future null generator field
$k_\epsilon$ spans that radical and is affine,
$\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{k_\epsilon}k_\epsilon=0$. At $p\in H_\epsilon$ define
the screen space $\mathcal S_{\epsilon,p}:=k_\epsilon^\perp/\mathbb R
k_\epsilon$, where $k_\epsilon^\perp$ is taken in $T_pM$. Its positive screen
metric is $\bar g_\epsilon([X],[Y]):=g_\epsilon(X,Y)$, its screen deformation
form is
$$B_\epsilon([X],[Y]):=g_\epsilon(\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_Xk_\epsilon,Y),$$
and its expansion and shear are $\theta_\epsilon:=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar
g_\epsilon}B_\epsilon$ and $\sigma_\epsilon:=B_\epsilon-\frac12\theta_\epsilon
\bar g_\epsilon$, respectively. These are the supplied smooth null-screen
conventions. The word “horizon” below denotes only $H_\epsilon$; no causal- or
event-horizon property is assumed.

Fix a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold $C$ and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For each $\epsilon$, supply a smooth map
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon$$
such that $\partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon$, and
every $\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ is an embedding with spacelike
image. The family supplies a fixed identification of generator labels and
affine normalization across $\epsilon$. With $[\lambda]=L$, this
parameterization gives $[k_\epsilon]=1$ in length coordinates.

Write $q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$ for the
positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let $\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be
its Riemannian area density. On each finite parameter slab, the pulled-back
metric, area density, screen deformation form, expansion, and shear are jointly
$C^1$ in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$ and smooth in $y$; the underlying metric and
embedding family has the corresponding $\epsilon$-regularity and spatial
derivatives needed to define them. Call the reference geometry stationary in
this model when $B_0=0$ along every generator; then $\theta_0=\sigma_0=0$.
Define $\delta\theta:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon\right|_0$.

For each $\epsilon$, supply a positive normalized state $\omega_\epsilon$ on
the selected free scalar-field algebra. Its two-point distribution $W_\epsilon$
is a bisolution of the selected Klein–Gordon operator and has the supplied
Hadamard wavefront relation $\mathcal C^+_{g_\epsilon}$: pairs of future-null
covectors related by parallel propagation along a future-directed null
geodesic with common positive scale and opposite sign in the second slot,
including the coincident-point case. Supply a state-independent Hadamard
singular bidistribution
$H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ such that $W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ is smooth, and one
fixed local stress prescription across the family,
$$T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}(x)=\lim_{x'\to x}D^{\epsilon}_{ab}(x,x')\bigl(W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}\bigr)(x,x')+C_{ab}[g_\epsilon;\mu,\mathbf c](x),$$
where $D^{\epsilon}_{ab}$ is the supplied finite-order bidifferential
operator and $C_{ab}$ the supplied state-independent local curvature
correction with fixed scale $\mu$ and finite renormalization conditions
$\mathbf c$. Thus the coincidence limit acts on a smooth difference, not on
the singular distributions separately. The family
$$F_\epsilon(\lambda,y):=(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\bigl(\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\bigr)$$
is jointly $C^1$ in $\epsilon$ and continuous in $(\lambda,y)$ on each finite
parameter slab. No independent graviton-fluctuation source is included.

Restrict every model input to the admissible domain supplied with its chosen
effective-model instance and to the regime below its supplied cutoff
$E_{\mathrm{cut}}>0$; neither the cutoff value nor its admissible input domain
is chosen here. Keep any prescribed retarded data as supplied inputs, without
imposing a collapse geometry or scattering history. Select the
Einstein-Hilbert submodel by setting the supplier's curvature-squared couplings
to zero. Write $G_N$ for the supplier's Newton's constant $G$ in the natural-unit
convention $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, so $G_N>0$ has dimension $L^2$. Define
$$\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon F_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0.$$
Then $[\lambda]=L$, $[k_\epsilon]=1$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, and
$[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$.
Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, its tail is absolutely integrable on
each generator, and
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$
where $dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}$ is the reference background area density.
Adopt, only to first order in $\epsilon$, the linearized focusing equation and
future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Terms quadratic in expansion or shear are omitted only at this first
perturbative order: both vanish in the stationary reference geometry and are
of order $\epsilon$ in the supplied family, so their squares are of order
$\epsilon^2$.
This postulate is an adopted model equation; it neither asserts that the model
describes nature nor identifies its null-stress moment with modular energy or
entropy.

model, satisfying

$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$

statement.proposed:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and
$[\lambda]=L$. Write $G_N$ for the Newton constant $G$ in the supplied
semiclassical equation after setting $c=\hbar=k_B=1$; then $G_N>0$ and
$[G_N]=L^2$. Take a model instance of the adopted Einstein-Hilbert focusing
postulate, with all its inputs restricted to the model-instance admissible
domain below the supplied effective cutoff $E_{\mathrm{cut}}$. The numerical
cutoff and admissible domain are supplied with that instance.

Let $M$ be the common smooth four-manifold of the family of smooth
time-oriented Lorentzian metrics $g_\epsilon$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and
let $H_\epsilon\subset M$ be smooth embedded null hypersurfaces whose induced
metrics have one-dimensional radicals. Their smooth nowhere-zero future null
generator fields $k_\epsilon$ span those radicals and are affine,
$\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{k_\epsilon}k_\epsilon=0$. Use the postulate's global-hyperbolicity convention: strong causality, meaning
that every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods met by each causal curve
in a connected parameter interval, and compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$.
Let $C$ be a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For dimensionless $\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, take the supplied
family
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon,\qquad \partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon,$$
with every $\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ an embedding with
spacelike image and with fixed generator labels and affine normalization
across $\epsilon$. The metric and embedding families have the postulate's
corresponding $\epsilon$-regularity on their common ambient manifold. The
pulled-back metric, area density, screen deformation form, expansion, and
shear are jointly $C^1$ in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$ and smooth in $y$ on each
finite parameter slab, with the spatial regularity needed to define them.

At $p\in H_\epsilon$, use the screen quotient
$\mathcal S_{\epsilon,p}=k_\epsilon^\perp/\mathbb Rk_\epsilon$ with positive
metric $\bar g_\epsilon([X],[Y])=g_\epsilon(X,Y)$. Its deformation form and
expansion are
$$B_\epsilon([X],[Y])=g_\epsilon(\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_Xk_\epsilon,Y),\qquad \theta_\epsilon=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g_\epsilon}B_\epsilon.$$
Assume the reference geometry is stationary in this model in the specified
sense $B_0=0$ along every generator, so $\theta_0$ and the shear
$\sigma_0=B_0-\frac12\theta_0\bar g_0$ vanish. Put
$$q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$$
for the positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let
$\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be its Riemannian area density. Define
$$A_\epsilon(\lambda):=\int_C\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda},\qquad \delta A(\lambda):=\left.\partial_\epsilon A_\epsilon(\lambda)\right|_0,\qquad dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}.$$

For each $\epsilon$, the supplied state $\omega_\epsilon$ is a positive
normalized linear functional; its two-point distribution $W_\epsilon$ is a
bisolution of the selected Klein-Gordon operator with Hadamard wavefront relation $\mathcal C^+_{g_\epsilon}$: its paired future-null covectors are related by parallel propagation along a future-directed null geodesic, with common positive scale and opposite sign in the second slot, including coincidence.
Use the postulate's single fixed local stress prescription
$$T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}(x)=\lim_{x'\to x}D^\epsilon_{ab}(x,x')\bigl(W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}\bigr)(x,x')+C_{ab}[g_\epsilon;\mu,\mathbf c](x),$$
where $W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ is smooth, $D^\epsilon_{ab}$ is the
supplied finite-order bidifferential operator, and $C_{ab}$ is the fixed
state-independent local curvature correction. Define
$$\delta\theta(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0,\qquad F_\epsilon(\lambda,y):=(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\bigl(\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\bigr),\qquad \delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon F_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0.$$
Assume $F_\epsilon$ has the postulate's joint $C^1$ dependence in $\epsilon$ and
continuous dependence on $(\lambda,y)$ on each finite parameter slab. Then $[k_\epsilon]=1$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, and
$[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$.

each generator, and satisfies the absolute first-moment bound
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty.$$

focusing equation and future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$

$$\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda)=8\pi G_N\int_C dA_0\int_\lambda^{\infty}(v-\lambda)\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv.$$

statement.before:
For a smooth codimension-two cut $\Sigma$ on a stationary null hypersurface,
one proved form of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) bounds the null
stress $\langle T_{kk}\rangle:=\langle T_{ab}k^ak^b\rangle$ below by
$\hbar/(2\pi)$ times $S_{\mathrm{out}}''/\mathcal A$. Here
$S_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the von Neumann entropy of the state restricted to one
side of $\Sigma$, $S_{\mathrm{out}}''$ is its second variation under a null
deformation, and $\mathcal A$ is the infinitesimal transverse area used in the
source limit. The cited proof applies to its stated free or superrenormalizable
bosonic field theories on stationary null hypersurfaces; it is not an
unrestricted assertion for every state, geometry or dimension. The quantum
focusing conjecture (QFC) instead proposes that, for a specified generalized
entropy functional $S_{\mathrm{gen}}=S_{\mathrm{grav}}+S_{\mathrm{out}}$ on a
smooth null cut, its source-defined quantum expansion
$\Theta[V;y]=(4G/\sqrt h)\,\delta S_{\mathrm{gen}}/\delta V(y)$ cannot
increase under a further forward affine deformation $V(y)$ along the null
generators; $h$ is the determinant of the cut's induced transverse metric.
This remains a conjecture in general. Weakly curved
Einstein-Hilbert-Gauss-Bonnet models have QFC counterexamples in dimensions
$d\ge5$, and later tests prove a restricted QFC for a class of two-dimensional
Jackiw-Teitelboim toy models while also reporting QFC counterexamples in a
particular regime of that model. Those theory- and regime-specific results
supply no universal QFC theorem for arbitrary higher-curvature effective
gravity. The linearized horizon model on this page defines no outside entropy,
generalized entropy functional or entropy shape derivative, so it neither
assumes nor derives QNEC or QFC.
statement.proposed:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$. For the cited quantum null energy condition
(QNEC), let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike codimension-two cut splitting a
Cauchy surface, and let $p\in\Sigma$. Let $\mathcal N$ be a smooth null
hypersurface orthogonal to $\Sigma$ near $p$, with smooth future-directed null
generators labelled by transverse coordinates $y$. On each generator use an
affine parameter $\lambda$ increasing toward the future and normalize its
tangent by $k^a=(d/d\lambda)^a$. Deforming $\Sigma$ to $\Sigma[\lambda(y)]$
moves each generator by its indicated affine amount. The source's
$S_{\mathrm{out}}[\lambda(y)]$ is the von Neumann entropy of the quantum-field
state restricted to one side of the deformed cut, equivalently to the
corresponding side of a Cauchy surface; the entropy itself may be divergent,
while the source-defined derivatives in the inequality are finite. In §2,
equation (2.2), the authors call the pointwise formulation the “general
conjecture”; its local geometric condition is that the classical expansion
and shear vanish at $p$. For a transverse patch of area $A$ about $p$,
$S_{\mathrm{out}}''(p)$ is the source-defined second affine variation for
that patch, with the other generators held fixed. The corresponding
pointwise formulation, in the small-area notation of equation (2.3), is
$$\langle T_{kk}(p)\rangle\ge\frac{1}{2\pi}\lim_{A\to0}\frac{S_{\mathrm{out}}''(p)}{A},\qquad \langle T_{kk}(p)\rangle:=\langle T_{ab}(p)k^ak^b\rangle.$$
Separately, the paper's abstract and outline report a proof for free or
superrenormalizable, massive or massless bosonic field theories on stationary
null hypersurfaces, where “stationary” means that the classical null expansion
vanishes everywhere. Its §3.1 sets up the proof for $D>2$ on such a
hypersurface, and §4.5 completes that argument. Section 5 separately derives
the free-scalar $D=2$ inequality $\langle T_{2D}\rangle\ge(2\pi)^{-1}S''_{2D}$
by dimensional reduction and strong subadditivity; it also treats higher-spin
bosonic fields and discusses the superrenormalizable extension under the
stated null-surface quantization and renormalization assumptions, in
particular preservation of the null observable algebra and $T_{kk}$. These
reported proof scopes are distinct from the general pointwise conjectural
formulation of §2; they do not establish that general formulation for every
field theory and background.

For the quantum focusing conjecture (QFC), let $\sigma$ be a smooth
codimension-two initial cut orthogonal to a smooth null hypersurface
$\mathcal N$, and label its null generators by $y$. Choose an affine parameter
$\lambda$ on each generator with $\lambda=0$ at $\sigma$, increasing in the
chosen future direction. An admissible nonnegative function $V(y)$ specifies
the cut that meets generator $y$ at $\lambda=V(y)$. Let $S_{\mathrm{gen}}[V]
=S_{\mathrm{grav}}[V]+S_{\mathrm{out}}[V]$ be the specified generalized
entropy functional of the cut, where $S_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outside-state
entropy, and let $h(y)$ be the determinant of the cut's induced transverse
metric in the chosen generator coordinates. Here $G>0$ is Newton's constant
in the stated natural units. The source-defined quantum
expansion is
$$\Theta[V;y_1]:=\frac{4G}{\sqrt{h(y_1)}}\frac{\delta S_{\mathrm{gen}}[V]}{\delta V(y_1)},$$
with $\hbar=1$. The QFC conjectures, for admissible $V$ and generator labels
$y_1,y_2$, the functional-derivative inequality
$$\frac{\delta\Theta[V;y_1]}{\delta V(y_2)}\le0,$$
understood in the source's distributional sense when the generator points
coincide. This remains a conjecture in general.

Weakly curved Einstein-Hilbert-Gauss-Bonnet models have QFC counterexamples
in spacetime dimensions $d\ge5$. The cited 2026 v3 paper proves a restricted QFC for a
class of two-dimensional Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) toy models and reports
counterexamples to the original and stronger QFC in a regime where matter
quantum effects are comparable to the total dilaton. Its authors state that
this counterexample regime has no known higher-dimensional uplift or
dimensional-reduction interpretation, is confined to the toy model, and is
not strong evidence against the original QFC. These theory- and
regime-specific findings establish no universal QFC theorem for arbitrary
higher-curvature effective gravity. The linearized horizon model discussed
here defines no outside entropy, generalized entropy functional, or entropy
shape derivative; it neither assumes nor derives QNEC or QFC.

statement.before: A **finite fusion transfer count model** consists of a finite nonempty label set $I$, a distinguished label $0\in I$, and an explicitly supplied matrix $N=(N_{ab})_{a,b\in I}$ whose entries lie in $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. The entry $N_{ab}$ is the multiplicity of elementary transitions from label $b$ to label $a$; formally, the transition copies from $b$ to $a$ are the triples $(b,a,j)$ with integer $1\leq j\leq N_{ab}$. A length-$n$ path is a sequence of $n+1$ labels together with a chosen transition copy between each consecutive pair. For each integer $n\geq0$, define the vacuum-return count $D_n:=(N^n)_{00}$. If $D_n>0$, set $H_n:=\mathbb C^{D_n}$ with its standard inner product and define $\rho_n:=D_n^{-1}I_{H_n}$. If $D_n=0$, no normalized operator $\rho_n$ is assigned. The matrix $N$ is model data; no fusion category, quantum group, or representation is presumed to realize it.
statement.proposed: A **finite fusion transfer count model** consists of a finite nonempty label set $I$, a distinguished label $0\in I$, and an explicitly supplied matrix $N=(N_{ab})_{a,b\in I}$ whose entries lie in $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. The entry $N_{ab}$ is the multiplicity of elementary transitions from label $b$ to label $a$; formally, the transition copies from $b$ to $a$ are the triples $(b,a,j)$ with integer $1\leq j\leq N_{ab}$. A length-$n$ path is a sequence of $n+1$ labels together with a chosen transition copy between each consecutive pair. View each natural-number entry as a real number under the usual inclusion $\mathbb N\subset\mathbb R$. For a finite set $J$ and $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, $F^J$ means the functions $J\to F$, with pointwise addition $(x+y)_j=x_j+y_j$ and scalar multiplication $(\lambda x)_j=\lambda x_j$. For real matrices $A,B$ indexed by $I$, define $(A+B)_{ab}:=A_{ab}+B_{ab}$. Their action on $x\in\mathbb R^I$ is $(Ax)_a:=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}x_b$. Matrix multiplication is $(AB)_{ac}:=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}B_{bc}$; it is associative by regrouping finite sums. These definitions are compatible because $((AB)x)_a=\sum_{b,c\in I}A_{ab}B_{bc}x_c=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}(Bx)_b=(A(Bx))_a$, and $((A+B)C)_{ac}=\sum_b(A_{ab}+B_{ab})C_{bc}=(AC)_{ac}+(BC)_{ac}$. Thus the natural-entry powers can also act on real vectors and the addition used below distributes over matrix multiplication. Let $I_I$ be the identity matrix with entries $(I_I)_{ab}=1$ if $a=b$ and $0$ otherwise, and use the power convention $N^0:=I_I$ and $N^{n+1}:=NN^n$ for $n\geq0$. Define the vacuum-return count $D_n:=(N^n)_{00}$. If $D_n>0$, set $H_n:=\mathbb C^{D_n}$, with coordinates $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{D_n})$ and inner product $\langle x,y\rangle:=\sum_{j=1}^{D_n}x_j\overline{y_j}$, linear in the first argument. This pairing satisfies the inner-product axioms of [[def-inner-product-space]]: finite distributivity gives $\langle\alpha x+\beta z,y\rangle=\alpha\langle x,y\rangle+\beta\langle z,y\rangle$, and conjugating the finite sum gives $\overline{\langle y,x\rangle}=\sum_j\overline{y_j}x_j=\langle x,y\rangle$. Writing $x_j=a_j+ib_j$ with real $a_j,b_j$ gives $\langle x,x\rangle=\sum_j(a_j^2+b_j^2)\geq0$; if this sum is zero, each nonnegative summand is zero, hence every $a_j=b_j=0$ and $x=0$. Conversely $x=0$ gives zero. The conjugation identities used here follow directly from $\overline{a+ib}=a-ib$ and finite distributivity. Therefore $H_n$ is a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; its coordinate unit vectors form a basis since every $x$ equals their linear combination with coefficients $x_j$, and a zero combination forces every coefficient to vanish. Let $I_{H_n}$ be its identity endomorphism and define $\rho_n:=D_n^{-1}I_{H_n}$. If $D_n=0$, no normalized operator $\rho_n$ is assigned. The matrix $N$ is model data; no fusion category, quantum group, or representation is presumed to realize it.

statement.before:
Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and a real loop parameter $\delta$. Define $[0]_\delta=0$, $[1]_\delta=1$, and $[r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta$ for $r\geq1$. Assume $[k]_\delta\neq0$ for $2\leq k\leq n$; this list is empty when $n=1$. The abstract generator algebra $P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ is the unital complex algebra with generators $u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}$ and relations $u_i^2=\delta u_i$, $u_i u_{i\pm1}u_i=u_i$, and $u_i u_j=u_j u_i$ when $|i-j|>1$. The diagram algebra $\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ has basis the noncrossing pairings of $n$ ordered bottom and $n$ ordered top points; its product stacks the left factor above the right, deletes each closed loop, and multiplies by $\delta$ per loop. Its elementary diagram $d_i$ has a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical strands elsewhere. The isomorphism $\Phi_n:P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ sends $u_i$ to $d_i$.

For every $1\leq i\leq n-2$, the adjacent relations in the presentation mean both $u_i u_{i+1}u_i=u_i$ and $u_{i+1}u_i u_{i+1}=u_{i+1}$. For matching the imported recursion's notation, write $U_i:=d_i$.

Set $p_1=1_1$. For $1\leq r<n$, put $Q_r=p_r\otimes1_1$ by adjoining one rightmost vertical strand and define

$$p_{r+1}:=Q_r-\frac{[r]_\delta}{[r+1]_\delta}Q_r d_r Q_r.$$

The denominator hypotheses make this recursion defined. For each $1\leq r\leq n$, let $\widehat p_r:=\Phi_r^{-1}(p_r)$. The cited Jones-Wenzl result gives $p_n^2=p_n$ under these unit-denominator hypotheses. For $1\leq r\leq n$, let $\iota_{r,n}:P_r(\mathbb C,\delta)\to P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ send each generator $u_i$ to the same-named generator, and let $\jmath_{r,n}:\mathrm{TL}_r(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ append $n-r$ rightmost vertical strands. The maps commute with $\Phi$: on each generator, both composites send $u_i$ to $d_i$ with those added strands, and both send the unit to the identity diagram. Since generators and unit generate $P_r$, the composites agree on every element.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A unital representation is a unital complex-algebra homomorphism $\pi:P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$, where $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$ is the algebra of complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$. Require each $\pi(u_i)$ to be self-adjoint, meaning $\langle\pi(u_i)x,y\rangle=\langle x,\pi(u_i)y\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$. Define $P:=\pi(\widehat p_n)$, define $\operatorname{rank}P:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{im}P$, and restrict to data with $\operatorname{rank}P>0$. The algebraic representation as a physical boundary state space is an additional model identification and is not part of this definition.

statement.before: Under the finite Hilbert representation data, let $r:=\operatorname{rank}P>0$ and $\rho:=P/r$. Then $P$ is an orthogonal projection, $\rho$ is a density matrix with eigenvalue $1/r$ of multiplicity $r$ and eigenvalue $0$ on $\ker P$, and its entropy is $s(\rho)=\log r$ in nats. Under the published closure convention, the unnormalized diagrammatic closure trace of the algebraic Jones-Wenzl element is $\operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1]_\delta$. The proposition records this separately from the ordinary Hilbert-space trace $\operatorname{tr}_H(P)=r$ and does not assert the two values agree. A sufficient additional hypothesis for equality on this element is that the representation preserve these traces, $\operatorname{tr}_H(\pi(\Phi_n^{-1}(X)))=\operatorname{Tr}_n(X)$ for every $X\in\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$.
statement.proposed: Under the finite Hilbert representation data, let $r:=\operatorname{rank}P>0$ and $\rho:=P/r$. An **orthogonal projection** on $H$ means a complex-linear endomorphism $Q$ satisfying $Q^2=Q$ and $\langle Qx,y\rangle=\langle x,Qy\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$. Then $P$ is an orthogonal projection, $\rho$ is a density matrix with eigenvalue $1/r$ of multiplicity $r$ and eigenvalue $0$ on $\ker P$, and its entropy is $s(\rho)=\log r$ in nats. Under the published closure convention, the unnormalized diagrammatic closure trace of the algebraic Jones-Wenzl element is $\operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1]_\delta$. The proposition records this separately from the ordinary Hilbert-space trace $\operatorname{tr}_H(P)=r$ and does not assert the two values agree. A sufficient additional hypothesis for equality on this element is that the representation preserve these traces, $\operatorname{tr}_H(\pi(\Phi_n^{-1}(X)))=\operatorname{Tr}_n(X)$ for every $X\in\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$.

statement.before: An **ensemble** here is a probability distribution over Hermitian matrices $H$ acting on finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and representing energy operators; its averaged partition function is the average of $\\operatorname{tr}(e^{-\\beta H})$ over that distribution. A **nonperturbative completion** is additional exact model data that select an exact theory beyond the terms fixed by a formal genus expansion. In the selected JT disk model, the continuous genus-zero density is only the one-disk input. The matrix-integral completion treated in the cited literature is an ensemble model and is described as non-unique; therefore the disk density alone specifies neither a unique nonperturbative completion nor the exact energy spectrum of one fixed boundary quantum system. No statement is made about every possible microscopic realization.
statement.proposed:
An **ensemble** here means the following finite-dimensional probability model. Let $N\ge 1$ be an integer, let $\mathcal H_N$ be an $N$-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)$ be the real vector space of self-adjoint linear operators on $\mathcal H_N$, with the operator-norm topology and its Borel sigma algebra. Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)$. Each $H\in\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)$ is an energy operator, with units $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ in the natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$ of the adopted JT disk model. For inverse temperature $\beta>0$, with units seconds, define the finite-matrix partition function $Z_H(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal H_N}(e^{-\beta H})$, where $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal H_N}$ is the ordinary finite-dimensional trace.

Since $H$ is self-adjoint and $\mathcal H_N$ is finite-dimensional, $Z_H(\beta)$ is a positive finite real number. The ensemble average is $\langle Z(\beta)\rangle_\mu:=\int_{\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)}Z_H(\beta)\,d\mu(H)$; it is finite when $\int Z_H(\beta)\,d\mu(H)<\infty$.

A **nonperturbative completion** is additional exact model data that select an exact theory beyond the terms fixed by the formal expansion by spacetime topology, as in the adopted JT disk model. In the SSS construction, an ordinary ensemble of $L\times L$ Hermitian matrices has measure $d\mu_{L,a}(H)=\mathcal Z_{L,a}^{-1}e^{-L\operatorname{tr}V_{L,a}(H)}\,dH$ on $\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^L)$, where $dH$ is Lebesgue measure, $V_{L,a}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is the chosen potential applied to the real eigenvalues of $H$, and $\mathcal Z_{L,a}:=\int e^{-L\operatorname{tr}V_{L,a}(H)}\,dH$ is finite and positive so that $\mu_{L,a}$ is normalized.

If $\lambda_1(H),\ldots,\lambda_L(H)$ are the eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, the ensemble-averaged eigenvalue-counting measure is $\nu_{L,a}(B):=\int\#\{j:\lambda_j(H)\in B\}\,d\mu_{L,a}(H)$ for each Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$; where it has a density, its leading large-$L$ term is the leading eigenvalue density. A **double-scaling limit** here is a limit along such a family in which $L\to\infty$ and $a\to\infty$, with $a$ the upper endpoint of the leading eigenvalue-density support before shifting, while $V_{L,a}$ is tuned and the energy coordinate is shifted by $E\mapsto E-a$ so that the leading density on the shifted energy region has a finite limit, with $e^{S_0}$ fixed.

In this limit the JT disk density is a smooth leading density, not the discrete spectrum of one finite matrix and not, by itself, a specification of a finite-matrix probability measure. The SSS matrix-integral approach matches the JT genus expansion in this double-scaled framework and is described as a non-unique nonperturbative completion. Therefore the disk density alone specifies neither a unique nonperturbative completion nor the exact energy spectrum of one fixed boundary quantum system (one specified boundary Hilbert space with one specified energy operator, rather than an ensemble of operators). No statement is made about every possible microscopic realization.

Let $S^2:=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:n\cdot n=1\}$ with the smooth structure given by the six graph charts solving $n_j=\pm\sqrt{1-\sum_{k\ne j}n_k^2}$ on the hemispheres $\pm n_j>0$. Orient it outward using the ordered spatial basis $x^1,x^2,x^3$. Its tangent plane is $T_nS^2=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:n\cdot X=0\}$. Physically, $n=k/|k|$ for a nonzero spatial wavevector $k$ in the SI Fourier description, where $k$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; hence $n$ is dimensionless and the radial magnitude is discarded. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, set $C_nz:=i\,n\times z$, $P_T(n)z:=z-n(n\cdot z)$, and $P_\sigma(n):=\tfrac12(P_T(n)+\sigma C_n)$ on $\mathbb C^3$, using the complex-linear extension of the right-handed cross product. Define the helicity fibre $L_\sigma(n):=\operatorname{range}P_\sigma(n)$ and the total space $L_\sigma:=\{(n,z):n\in S^2,\ z\in L_\sigma(n)\}$, projected to $S^2$ by $(n,z)\mapsto n$. Use the Hermitian product $\langle u,v\rangle_H:=\sum_{j=1}^3\overline{u_j}v_j$.

On a spherical chart with $0<\theta<\pi$ and a smooth longitude branch $\phi$, write $n=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$, $e_\theta=(\cos\theta\cos\phi,\cos\theta\sin\phi,-\sin\theta)$, and $e_\phi=(-\sin\phi,\cos\phi,0)$. The local unit helicity frame is $v_\sigma:=(e_\theta+i\sigma e_\phi)/\sqrt2$. For any local smooth unit frame $v$ of $L_\sigma$, define its Berry connection one-form by $A:=i v^\dagger d v$, where $d v$ differentiates its three complex components. A smooth phase change $v'=e^{i\chi}v$, with real smooth $\chi$, changes this local form to $A'=A-d\chi$. The local Berry curvature is the two-form $F:=dA$; this definition makes no global gluing assertion.
statement.proposed:
For $u,v\in\mathbb C^3$, extend the real Euclidean dot and right-handed cross products complex-bilinearly, with coordinate formulas
$$u\cdot v:=\sum_{j=1}^3u_jv_j,\qquad u\times v:=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2-u_2v_1).$$
The dot product in these formulas uses no complex conjugation; it differs from the Hermitian product $\langle u,v\rangle_H:=\sum_{j=1}^3\overline{u_j}v_j$. Write $\|z\|_H:=\sqrt{\langle z,z\rangle_H}$ for the associated nonnegative norm on $\mathbb C^3$.

Let $S^2:=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:n\cdot n=1\}$ with the smooth structure given by the six graph charts solving $n_j=\pm\sqrt{1-\sum_{k\ne j}n_k^2}$ on the hemispheres $\pm n_j>0$. Orient it outward using the ordered spatial basis $x^1,x^2,x^3$. Its tangent plane is $T_nS^2=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:n\cdot X=0\}$. Physically, $n=k/|k|$ for a nonzero spatial wavevector $k$ in the SI Fourier description, where $k$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; hence $n$ is dimensionless and the radial magnitude is discarded. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, set $C_nz:=i\,n\times z$, $P_T(n)z:=z-n(n\cdot z)$, and $P_\sigma(n):=\tfrac12(P_T(n)+\sigma C_n)$ on $\mathbb C^3$. Define the helicity fibre $L_\sigma(n):=\operatorname{range}P_\sigma(n)$ and the total space $L_\sigma:=\{(n,z):n\in S^2,\ z\in L_\sigma(n)\}$, projected to $S^2$ by $(n,z)\mapsto n$.

For an open set $U\subseteq S^2$, a unit frame of $L_\sigma$ over $U$ is a smooth map $v:U\to\mathbb C^3$ such that $v(n)\in L_\sigma(n)$ and $\langle v(n),v(n)\rangle_H=1$ for every $n\in U$. Since each fibre is a complex line, this vector spans that fibre. A local unit frame is such a map on an open neighborhood in $S^2$; a global unit frame is one defined on all of $S^2$.

Fibrewise addition and scalar multiplication are inherited from $\mathbb C^3$. A unit frame $v$ gives the local trivialization $(n,a)\mapsto(n,a v(n))$ from $U\times\mathbb C$ to $L_\sigma|_U$, with inverse $(n,z)\mapsto(n,\langle v(n),z\rangle_H)$. The construction in the Proof supplies such a frame near every $n$, so $L_\sigma$ is a smooth rank-one complex vector subbundle of the product bundle $S^2\times\mathbb C^3\to S^2$, whose projection is $(n,z)\mapsto n$.

On a spherical chart with $0<\theta<\pi$ and a smooth longitude branch $\phi$, write $n=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$, $e_\theta=(\cos\theta\cos\phi,\cos\theta\sin\phi,-\sin\theta)$, and $e_\phi=(-\sin\phi,\cos\phi,0)$. The local unit helicity frame is $v_\sigma:=(e_\theta+i\sigma e_\phi)/\sqrt2$. For any unit frame $v$ over an open set $U$, write $v^\dagger d v:=\sum_{j=1}^3\overline{v_j}\,d v_j$, where $d v_j$ is the exterior derivative of its $j$th component. Define its Berry connection one-form by $A:=i v^\dagger d v$. A smooth phase change $v'=e^{i\chi}v$, with real smooth $\chi$, changes this local form to $A'=A-d\chi$. The local Berry curvature is the real two-form $F:=dA$ on $U$; no global gluing assertion is made here.

statement.before: Fix $n\in S^2$ and $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Put $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For the dimensionless angle $\alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, define the proper active rotation fixing $n$ by $R_{n,\alpha}z=(n\cdot z)n+\cos\alpha\,(z-(n\cdot z)n)+\sin\alpha\,(n\times z)$ on $\mathbb C^3$, and set $SO(2)_n:=\{R_{n,\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. It acts on the whole helicity fibre $L_\sigma(n)$ by $R_{n,\alpha}z=e^{-i\sigma\alpha}z$, so the fibre carries the character $\rho_\sigma(R_{n,\alpha})=e^{-i\sigma\alpha}$. For a piecewise $C^1$ closed direction path $\gamma:[0,1]\to S^2$ with a finite subdivision $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1$ and local unit frames $v_j$ on the subpaths, define parallel transport by $\nabla s=P_\sigma ds=0$. If $v_{j+1}(\gamma(t_j))=g_jv_j(\gamma(t_j))$ at each internal join and $v_m(\gamma(1))=g_mv_1(\gamma(0))$, where $g_j,g_m\in U(1)$, then its holonomy, the scalar multiplying an initial fibre vector after transport around $\gamma$, is $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^m\exp(i\int_{\gamma|[t_{j-1},t_j]}A_j)\bigr)\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}g_j^{-1}\bigr)g_m$. In a single periodic frame this reduces to $\exp(i\oint_\gamma A)$. If a finite oriented smooth singular $2$-chain $\Sigma$ lies in one frame patch and $\partial\Sigma=\gamma$, then $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\exp(i\int_\Sigma F_\sigma)$.
statement.proposed:
For $u,v\in\mathbb C^3$, the dot and cross products are the complex-bilinear extensions with coordinate formulas $u\cdot v=\sum_{j=1}^3u_jv_j$ and $u\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,u_3v_1-u_1v_3,u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$, as defined in the helicity line-bundle item.

Fix $n\in S^2$ and $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Put $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For $n\in\mathbb R^3$ and $z\in\mathbb C^3$, the dot in the rotation formula is $n\cdot z=\sum_{j=1}^3n_jz_j$, the complex-bilinear dot product defined in the earlier helicity line-bundle definition. For the dimensionless angle $\alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, define the proper active rotation fixing $n$ by $R_{n,\alpha}z=(n\cdot z)n+\cos\alpha\,(z-(n\cdot z)n)+\sin\alpha\,(n\times z)$ on $\mathbb C^3$, with the complex-linear extension of the real rotation action, and set $SO(2)_n:=\{R_{n,\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. It acts on the whole helicity fibre $L_\sigma(n)$ by $R_{n,\alpha}z=e^{-i\sigma\alpha}z$, so the fibre carries the character $\rho_\sigma(R_{n,\alpha})=e^{-i\sigma\alpha}$. For a piecewise $C^1$ closed direction path $\gamma:[0,1]\to S^2$, choose a finite subdivision $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1$ on whose closed subintervals $\gamma$ is $C^1$. For each segment choose an open set $U_j\subseteq S^2$ containing its image and a unit frame $v_j:U_j\to\mathbb C^3$ as defined in the helicity line-bundle definition; write $A_j:=i\sum_{\ell=1}^3\overline{(v_j)_\ell}\,d(v_j)_\ell$. For a one-form $A_j$ on $U_j$, define its oriented curve integral on this segment by
$$\int_{\gamma|[t_{j-1},t_j]}A_j:=\int_{t_{j-1}}^{t_j}(A_j)_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))\,dt,$$
the ordinary Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on that segment. For a $C^1$ section $s(t)\in L_\sigma(\gamma(t))$, define its projected derivative by $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}s(t):=P_\sigma(\gamma(t))\dot s(t)$, with the derivative taken componentwise in $\mathbb C^3$; parallel transport is the solution of $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}s=0$ on each segment. If $v_{j+1}(\gamma(t_j))=g_jv_j(\gamma(t_j))$ at each internal join and $v_m(\gamma(1))=g_mv_1(\gamma(0))$, where $g_j,g_m\in U(1)$, then its holonomy, the scalar multiplying an initial fibre vector after transport around $\gamma$, is $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^m\exp(i\int_{\gamma|[t_{j-1},t_j]}A_j)\bigr)\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}g_j^{-1}\bigr)g_m$. In one unit frame defined on a neighborhood of the whole loop, write $\oint_\gamma A:=\sum_{j=1}^m\int_{\gamma|[t_{j-1},t_j]}A$; then the formula reduces to $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\exp(i\oint_\gamma A)$. If in addition $\gamma$ is piecewise smooth in the sense that each rescaled segment $\gamma_j(u):=\gamma(t_{j-1}+(t_j-t_{j-1})u)$, $0\le u\le1$, is a smooth singular $1$-simplex, define the finite smooth singular $1$-chain $c_\gamma:=\sum_{j=1}^m\gamma_j$ with its positive path orientation. If a finite oriented smooth singular $2$-chain $\Sigma$ has image in one open frame domain $U$ and $\partial\Sigma=c_\gamma$, then $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\exp(i\int_\Sigma F_\sigma)$.

The piecewise $C^1$ subdivision is understood with one-sided derivatives continuous up to each subinterval endpoint. In the final clause, each rescaled path segment must extend to a smooth map from an open neighborhood of its affine interval into $S^2$; this is the neighborhood-extension condition for a smooth singular $1$-simplex. The open frame domain $U$ is an open subset of $S^2$ carrying one smooth unit frame on all of $U$, and the image of $\Sigma$ lies in $U$.
