statement.before:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the finite port model at a real angular frequency $\omega>0$, period $T=2\pi/\omega$, incoming amplitude $a\in\mathbb C^N$, and unique outgoing amplitude $b=S(\omega)a$. Here $\Omega$ is the bounded $C^1$ device region in that port model. The real fields $E,H,D,B:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ and the material states are jointly $C^\infty$ and $T$-periodic, satisfy the smooth source-free macroscopic Maxwell equations, and have free charge and current $\rho_f=0$ and $J_f=0$. Their units are respectively $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, and $\mathrm T$. Use one of the following two homogeneous material branches with constant coefficients.

**Finite Lorentz branch.** For a finite $M\ge1$, each $P_\ell:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+\sum_{\ell=1}^M P_\ell$, $B=\mu H$, and $\partial_t^2P_\ell+\gamma_\ell\partial_tP_\ell+\omega_\ell^2P_\ell=a_\ell E$, where $\varepsilon_\infty,\mu,a_\ell,\omega_\ell>0$ and $\gamma_\ell\ge0$.

**Drude branch.** $P,V:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ have units $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$ and $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, respectively; $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+P$, $B=\mu H$, $\partial_tP=V$, and $\partial_tV+\gamma V=aE$, where $\varepsilon_\infty,\mu,a>0$ and $\gamma\ge0$.

The constants have the SI units of the respective adopted closure: $\varepsilon_\infty$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$, $\mu$ in $\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, each $a_\ell$ or $a$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and each $\omega_\ell$ or damping rate in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. In the Lorentz branch define $\ell=\sum_{\ell=1}^M(\gamma_\ell/a_\ell)|\partial_tP_\ell|^2$; in the Drude branch define $\ell=(\gamma/a)|V|^2$. These are nonnegative loss densities in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$, and let $P_{\mathrm{mat}}=T^{-1}\int_0^T\int_\Omega\ell\,dV\,dt$. Let $P_\partial\ge0$ be the cycle-averaged outward power of the passive physical walls, and let $P_{\mathrm{other}}\ge0$ be all outgoing radiation or propagating-channel power not represented in $b$, as defined by the port model. Then

$$\|a\|_2^2-\|S(\omega)a\|_2^2=P_{\mathrm{mat}}+P_\partial+P_{\mathrm{other}}\ge0.$$

Consequently $S(\omega)$ is contractive: $\|Sa\|_2\le\|a\|_2$ for every $a$. If all material loss, wall loss, and unlisted outward power vanish for every incoming vector, then $S^\dagger S=I_N$; because the defined map is square, $S$ is unitary. The exact equality and unitarity are conditional deductions of this model, not existence claims about arbitrary scatterers.
statement.proposed:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the finite port model at a real angular frequency $\omega>0$, period $T=2\pi/\omega$, incoming amplitude $a\in\mathbb C^N$, and unique outgoing amplitude $b=S(\omega)a$. Here $\Omega$ is the bounded $C^1$ device region in that port model. The real fields $E,H,D,B:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ and the material states are jointly $C^\infty$ and $T$-periodic, satisfy the smooth source-free macroscopic Maxwell equations, and have free charge and current $\rho_f=0$ and $J_f=0$. Their units are respectively $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, and $\mathrm T$. Use one of the following two homogeneous material branches with constant coefficients.

For real vectors $v,w\in\mathbb R^3$, the Euclidean product is $v\cdot w:=\sum_{r=1}^3v_rw_r$ and $|v|^2:=v\cdot v$.

The port model uses incoming and outgoing vectors $a,b\in\mathbb C^N$ with amplitude units $\mathrm{W^{1/2}}$; for either vector $z$, $\|z\|_2^2:=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N|z_\alpha|^2$ is its power in W, and the net outward port power is $\|b\|_2^2-\|a\|_2^2$.

**Finite Lorentz branch.** For a finite $M\ge1$, each $P_\ell:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+\sum_{\ell=1}^M P_\ell$, $B=\mu H$, and $\partial_t^2P_\ell+\gamma_\ell\partial_tP_\ell+\omega_\ell^2P_\ell=a_\ell E$, where $\varepsilon_\infty,\mu,a_\ell,\omega_\ell>0$ and $\gamma_\ell\ge0$.

**Drude branch.** $P,V:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ have units $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$ and $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, respectively; $D=\varepsilon_\infty E+P$, $B=\mu H$, $\partial_tP=V$, and $\partial_tV+\gamma V=aE$, where $\varepsilon_\infty,\mu,a>0$ and $\gamma\ge0$.

The constants have the SI units of the respective adopted closure: $\varepsilon_\infty$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$, $\mu$ in $\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, each $a_\ell$ or $a$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and each $\omega_\ell$ or damping rate in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. In the Lorentz branch define the loss-density map $\ell:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ by $\ell=\sum_{\ell=1}^M(\gamma_\ell/a_\ell)|\partial_tP_\ell|^2$; in the Drude branch define it by $\ell=(\gamma/a)|V|^2$. These have units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$. For the solution with the fixed input $a$, set $P_{\mathrm{mat}}(a):=T^{-1}\int_0^T\int_\Omega\ell\,dV\,dt$. Let $P_\partial(a)\ge0$ be its cycle-averaged outward power at passive physical walls, and let $P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)\ge0$ be all its outgoing radiation or propagating-channel power not represented in $b$, as defined by the port model. For brevity, in the proof write these three quantities as $P_{\mathrm{mat}}$, $P_\partial$, and $P_{\mathrm{other}}$. Then

$$\|a\|_2^2-\|S(\omega)a\|_2^2=P_{\mathrm{mat}}(a)+P_\partial(a)+P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)\ge0.$$

For complex vectors and matrices, an overline denotes componentwise complex conjugation and a superscript ${}^{\mathsf T}$ denotes ordinary transpose; set $z^\dagger:=\overline z^{\,\mathsf T}$ for $z\in\mathbb C^N$ and $A^\dagger:=\overline A^{\,\mathsf T}$ for $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times N}$. A matrix is **Hermitian** when $A^\dagger=A$, and is **unitary** when $A^\dagger A=AA^\dagger=I_N$, where $I_N$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb C^N$.

Consequently $S(\omega)$ is contractive: $\|Sa\|_2\le\|a\|_2$ for every $a$. If $P_{\mathrm{mat}}(a)=P_\partial(a)=P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)=0$ for every incoming vector $a$, then $S^\dagger S=I_N$; because the defined map is square, $S$ is unitary. The exact equality and unitarity are conditional deductions of this model, not existence claims about arbitrary scatterers.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the finite port model at a fixed real $\omega>0$. Let $S(\omega)\in\mathbb C^{N\times N}$ be its unique scattering matrix. Suppose the continuous device phasor coefficient maps obey $\varepsilon(x)^T=\varepsilon(x)$ and $\mu(x)^T=\mu(x)$ pointwise, the two source-free scattering solutions used below lie in $C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb C^3)$, and their reciprocal port modes satisfy the exact bilinear pairing stipulated in the model definition. Then

$$S(\omega)^T=S(\omega).$$

If in addition the material, wall, and unlisted-channel losses vanish for every incoming vector, the lossless clause of the contractivity theorem gives $S^\dagger S=I_N$, so the matrix is symmetric and unitary. statement.proposed:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the finite port model at a fixed real $\omega>0$. Let $S(\omega)\in\mathbb C^{N\times N}$ be its unique scattering matrix. Suppose the continuous device phasor coefficient maps $\varepsilon,\mu:\overline\Omega\to\mathbb C^{3\times3}$ obey $\varepsilon(x)^T=\varepsilon(x)$ and $\mu(x)^T=\mu(x)$ pointwise, and for every pair of incoming vectors the corresponding source-free scattering solutions lie in $C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb C^3)$ and have reciprocal port modes satisfying the exact bilinear pairing stipulated in the model definition. Then

$$S(\omega)^T=S(\omega).$$

For $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times N}$, define its conjugate transpose by $A^\dagger:=\overline A^{\,\mathsf T}$, where the overline is componentwise conjugation and a superscript $\mathsf T$ is ordinary transpose; $A$ is Hermitian when $A^\dagger=A$ and unitary when $A^\dagger A=AA^\dagger=I_N$, with $I_N$ the identity on $\mathbb C^N$. The transpose relation above uses the unconjugated Lorentz pairing; the unitary relation below uses the separate conjugated Hermitian power pairing. No time-reversal claim follows.

For each incoming vector $a$, define the operational net cycle-averaged material power transferred from the fields in this source-free phasor model by

$$P_{\mathrm{bulk}}(a):=\frac{\omega}{2}\int_\Omega\operatorname{Im}\big(\widetilde E^\dagger\varepsilon\widetilde E+\widetilde H^\dagger\mu\widetilde H\big)\,dV.$$

Here $v^\dagger=\overline v^{\,T}$ for a complex column vector, and this power has units W. It is a signed net transfer, not an assumption of local passivity or a definition of a material realization. Let $P_\partial(a)$ and $P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)$ be the nonnegative outward wall and unlisted-channel powers of the same finite-port model, whose total outward boundary power is $\|Sa\|_2^2-\|a\|_2^2+P_\partial(a)+P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)$. Then

$$\|a\|_2^2-\|Sa\|_2^2=P_{\mathrm{bulk}}(a)+P_\partial(a)+P_{\mathrm{other}}(a).$$

Consequently, if all three powers vanish for every incoming vector $a\in\mathbb C^N$, then $S^\dagger S=SS^\dagger=I_N$, so $S$ is symmetric and unitary. Pointwise Hermitian $\varepsilon$ and $\mu$ suffice to make $P_{\mathrm{bulk}}(a)=0$ for every input, since their quadratic forms are real; Hermitian symmetry is distinct from the ordinary transpose symmetry required for reciprocity. No constitutive branch beyond the stated phasor model is required for this operational zero-power conclusion.

The following full finite-port contraction hypotheses give additional Lorentz and Drude sufficient cases on this same port map. For every incoming vector, its real field maps $E,H,D,B:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ and its material-state maps on that domain are jointly $C^\infty$ and $T$-periodic, where $T=2\pi/\omega$, and satisfy the smooth source-free macroscopic Maxwell equations with $\rho_f=J_f=0$.

The material closure is one of these two homogeneous, constant-coefficient branches. In the finite Lorentz branch, choose finite $M\ge1$ and maps $P_\ell:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ for $1\le\ell\le M$. They satisfy

$$D=\varepsilon_\infty E+\sum_{\ell=1}^M P_\ell,\qquad B=\mu H,\qquad \partial_t^2P_\ell+\gamma_\ell\partial_tP_\ell+\omega_\ell^2P_\ell=a_\ell E,$$

with constant $\varepsilon_\infty,\mu,a_\ell,\omega_\ell>0$ and $\gamma_\ell\ge0$. In the Drude branch, take maps $P,V:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$. They satisfy

$$D=\varepsilon_\infty E+P,\qquad B=\mu H,\qquad \partial_tP=V,\qquad \partial_tV+\gamma V=aE,$$

with constant $\varepsilon_\infty,\mu,a>0$ and $\gamma\ge0$. Their SI units are those specified in the finite-port contraction model.

For each input, require the real fields and material states to have only this frequency: let $\widetilde E,\widetilde H,\widetilde D,\widetilde B:\overline\Omega\to\mathbb C^3$ be their phasor amplitudes with $E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and analogously for $H,D,B$. In the Lorentz branch also write $P_\ell(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde P_\ell(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ with $\widetilde P_\ell:\overline\Omega\to\mathbb C^3$; in the Drude branch write $P,V$ in the same form with amplitudes $\widetilde P,\widetilde V:\overline\Omega\to\mathbb C^3$. Substitution into the closure equations gives

$$\varepsilon_{\mathrm L}(\omega)=\left(\varepsilon_\infty+\sum_{\ell=1}^M\frac{a_\ell}{\omega_\ell^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_\ell\omega}\right)I_3,\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm D}(\omega)=\left(\varepsilon_\infty-\frac{a}{\omega^2+i\gamma\omega}\right)I_3,$$

where every Lorentz denominator is required nonzero, $I_3$ is the $3\times3$ identity, and the magnetic coefficient is $\mu I_3$ in either branch. Require these harmonic coefficient maps to be the continuous coefficients of this same reciprocal-phasor port model. The matrices are symmetric under ordinary transpose. The branch loss density is $\ell=\sum_{j=1}^M(\gamma_j/a_j)|\partial_tP_j|^2$ in the Lorentz branch and $\ell=(\gamma/a)|V|^2$ in the Drude branch, using the real vector norm $|v|^2=v\cdot v$. For the solution with incoming vector $a$, define $P_{\mathrm{mat}}(a):=T^{-1}\int_0^T\int_\Omega\ell\,dV\,dt$, and let $P_\partial(a)$ and $P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)$ be its nonnegative passive-wall and unlisted-outgoing powers under the finite-port model's bookkeeping. The field, material-state, and parameter units are exactly those specified in that model.

In either harmonic branch, $P_{\mathrm{bulk}}(a)=P_{\mathrm{mat}}(a)$. Thus $P_{\mathrm{mat}}(a)=P_\partial(a)=P_{\mathrm{other}}(a)=0$ for every incoming vector $a$ is a sufficient case of the operational zero-power criterion, also supplied by the contraction result. These branch hypotheses are sufficient cases, not restrictions on the general phasor power identity above.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty, bounded, connected open set with smooth boundary, meaning each boundary point has Euclidean coordinates in which $\Omega$ is one side of a smooth graph. Use Euclidean coordinates $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $\delta=\sum_{i=1}^3dx^i\otimes dx^i$, write $\partial_i=\partial/\partial x^i$, and set $\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2$. A multi-index is $\beta=(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3)\in\mathbb N_0^3$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$; write $|\beta|=\beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3$ and $D^\beta=\partial_1^{\beta_1}\partial_2^{\beta_2}\partial_3^{\beta_3}$. Fix $0<\alpha<1$, a real function $S\in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $S\geq0$, and a real dimensionless parameter $\varepsilon$. For a real function $g$ on $\overline\Omega$, define

$$[g]_{0,\alpha}:=\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha},\qquad \|g\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}:=\sup_{\overline\Omega}|g|+[g]_{0,\alpha},$$

and let $C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ consist of the continuous functions with finite displayed norm. Define $C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ to consist of functions whose derivatives through order $2$ on $\Omega$ extend continuously to $\overline\Omega$ and whose norm

$$\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}:=\sum_{|\beta|\leq2}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta u|+\sum_{|\beta|=2}[D^\beta u]_{0,\alpha}$$

is finite, where $\beta$ is a multi-index. Write $X:=\{u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):u|_{\partial\Omega}=0\}$, with its inherited norm, and $Y:=C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$. The bounded-domain charged conformal problem is to find $u\in X$ such that $\psi:=1+u>0$ on $\overline\Omega$ and

$$-8\Delta\psi=2\varepsilon^2 S\psi^{-3}\quad\hbox{in }\Omega,\qquad \psi|_{\partial\Omega}=1.$$

In the conformal-seed specialization $\bar h=\delta$, $\bar A=0$, $\tau=0$, and $\Lambda=0$ (so $h=\psi^4\delta$ and $K=0$), the initial data are time-symmetric, meaning their second fundamental form is $K=0$. The scalar equation is the Hamiltonian constraint from the conformal electrovacuum transformation when $S=|\bar E_0|_\delta^2+|\bar B_0|_\delta^2$. Here $\bar E_0,\bar B_0:\overline\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are independently prescribed contravariant Euclidean vector fields, each the restriction of a smooth map on an open neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$, and divergence-free means $\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i\bar E_0^i=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i\bar B_0^i=0$ on $\Omega$ in these Cartesian coordinates. In geometric length coordinates, $\psi,\varepsilon$ are dimensionless, $\bar E_0,\bar B_0$ have units of inverse length, and $S$ has units of inverse length squared. This is a specialization with prescribed fields; the general problem allows any nonnegative $S\in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$. The definition does not assert existence, uniqueness, a momentum constraint, or an asymptotically Euclidean or puncture solution.

Let $U$ be a nonempty, connected, simply connected, second-countable smooth
two-manifold without boundary. Let $q$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric of
signature $(-,+)$ on $U$, with a chosen time orientation and an orientation
whose metric volume form is $\epsilon_2$. Let $r:U\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth.
Take $S^2=\{p\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot p=1\}$ with induced round metric
$\gamma_{S^2,p}(u,v)=u\cdot v$ and outward area form
$(\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v)=\det(p,u,v)$; in polar coordinates it is
$\omega_{S^2}=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. Put
$\mathcal M:=U\times S^2$, let $\pi_U,\pi_S$ be its projections, and define
$$g:=\pi_U^*q+(r\circ\pi_U)^2\pi_S^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$
The fibre over $y\in U$ is $S^2_y:=\pi_U^{-1}(\{y\})=\{y\}\times S^2$.
Choose the four-dimensional orientation so that its metric volume form is
$$\mathrm{vol}_g=-(r\circ\pi_U)^2\,\pi_U^*\epsilon_2\wedge\pi_S^*\omega_{S^2}.$$
In any chart $(x^0,r)$ for which $\epsilon_2=-dx^0\wedge dr$, this gives
$\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dr\wedge r^2\omega_{S^2}$.

For each $R\in SO(3)$ define $\rho_R:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ by
$\rho_R(y,p)=(y,Rp)$. A tensor field $T$ on $\mathcal M$ is called
rotationally invariant if $\rho_R^*T=T$ for every $R\in SO(3)$; a two-form
$\mathcal F$ is rotationally invariant in exactly this sense. This definition
specifies a local warped-product model and a group action. It asserts no global
quotient, global potential, maximal extension, or field equation.
statement.proposed:
Let $U$ be a nonempty, connected, simply connected, second-countable smooth
two-manifold without boundary. Let $q$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $U$ such that $q_y$ is nondegenerate of signature $(-,+)$
for every $y\in U$. Choose a smooth vector field $N$ on $U$ with
$q(N,N)<0$ everywhere; the **time orientation** is the choice of the
connected component containing $N_y$ in each timelike cone
$\{v\in T_yU:q_y(v,v)<0\}$. Choose an orientation of $U$, and let
$\epsilon_2$ be its metric volume form, characterized by
$\epsilon_2(e_0,e_1)=1$ on every positively oriented $q$-orthonormal frame
with $q(e_0,e_0)=-1$ and $q(e_1,e_1)=1$. Let $r:U\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth.
Take $S^2=\{p\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot p=1\}$ with the smooth structure and
induced round metric fixed by the earlier dyonic Reissner–Nordström data
definition cited below. Its tangent plane is
$T_pS^2=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot u=0\}$, its metric is
$\gamma_{S^2,p}(u,v)=u\cdot v$, and its outward area form is
$(\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v)=\det(p,u,v)$. Write $\wedge$ for the exterior
product of alternating forms. In polar coordinates
$\omega_{S^2}=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. Put
$\mathcal M:=U\times S^2$ and define its projections by
$\pi_U(y,p):=y$ and $\pi_S(y,p):=p$. For a smooth map $F:X\to Y$ and a
smooth covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ on $Y$, define its pullback by
$$(F^*h)_x(v,w):=h_{F(x)}(dF_xv,dF_xw),$$
where $x\in X$, $v,w\in T_xX$, and $dF_x:T_xX\to T_{F(x)}Y$ is the
derivative. This formula also defines pullback of a covariant $2$-form.
Define
$$g:=\pi_U^*q+(r\circ\pi_U)^2\pi_S^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$
It has Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$.
The fibre over $y\in U$ is $S^2_y:=\pi_U^{-1}(\{y\})=\{y\}\times S^2$.
Its induced Riemannian metric is $r(y)^2\gamma_{S^2}$ and its area form is
$r(y)^2\omega_{S^2}$; in polar angles $0<\theta<\pi$ and
$0\le\phi<2\pi$, its area is
$\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi r(y)^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi=4\pi r(y)^2$.
Thus $r(y)>0$ is the areal radius of this orbit sphere.
Choose the four-dimensional orientation so that its metric volume form is
$$\mathrm{vol}_g=-(r\circ\pi_U)^2\,\pi_U^*\epsilon_2\wedge\pi_S^*\omega_{S^2}.$$
In any chart $(x^0,r)$ for which $\epsilon_2=-dx^0\wedge dr$, this gives
$\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dr\wedge r^2\omega_{S^2}$.

Define
$$SO(3):=\{R\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}:R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3,\ \det R=1\}.$$
Each $R\in SO(3)$ acts on $S^2$ by $p\mapsto Rp$ and defines the smooth
diffeomorphism $\rho_R:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$,
$\rho_R(y,p)=(y,Rp)$, whose inverse is $\rho_{R^{\mathsf T}}$.
For nonnegative integers $a,b$, a smooth tensor field of type $(a,b)$ on
$\mathcal M$ is a smooth section of
$$T^a_b\mathcal M:=(T\mathcal M)^{\otimes a}\otimes(T^*\mathcal M)^{\otimes b};$$
at each $x\in\mathcal M$ its value is multilinear on $a$ covectors in
$T_x^*\mathcal M$ and $b$ vectors in $T_x\mathcal M$, where
$T_x^*\mathcal M:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(T_x\mathcal M,\mathbb R)$.
Smoothness means that the components of the section in every smooth product
chart are $C^\infty$. For such a field $T$, define its pullback by the
diffeomorphism $\rho_R$ by
$$(\rho_R^*T)_x(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_a;v_1,\ldots,v_b)=T_{\rho_R(x)}(\alpha_1\circ(d\rho_R)_x^{-1},\ldots,\alpha_a\circ(d\rho_R)_x^{-1};(d\rho_R)_xv_1,\ldots,(d\rho_R)_xv_b)$$
where $\alpha_i\in T_x^*\mathcal M$, $v_j\in T_x\mathcal M$, and
$(d\rho_R)_x:T_x\mathcal M\to T_{\rho_R(x)}\mathcal M$ is the derivative
of $\rho_R$ at $x$.
A real two-form is a smooth alternating tensor field of type $(0,2)$.
The field $T$ is **rotationally invariant** if $\rho_R^*T=T$ for every
$R\in SO(3)$; a two-form $\mathcal F$ is rotationally invariant in exactly
this sense. This definition specifies a local warped-product model and a
group action. It asserts no global quotient, global potential, maximal
extension, or field equation.

coordinates $(t,r)$ on the quotient in which

Let $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$, and assume $0\le Q^2<m^2$. Use the asymptotically flat dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric with $M=m$ and $f(r)=1-2m/r+Q^2/r^2$ on the exterior $r>r_+:=m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$. Here $r_-$ denotes the other algebraic horizon root $m-\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$; when $Q^2>0$, $r_\pm$ are the local null Killing horizons of the selected RN model, and when $Q^2=0$, $r_+=2m$ is the larger root. An equatorial circular null geodesic means a smooth nonconstant affinely parametrized geodesic $\gamma(s)=(x^0(s),r_c,\pi/2,\phi(s))$ with $g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=0$ and nonzero angular momentum $\ell=r_c^2\dot\phi$. Its effective radial function is $h(r)=f(r)/r^2$. The outer circular null radius is

$$r_{\mathrm{ph}+}=\frac{3m+\sqrt{9m^2-8Q^2}}{2}.$$

It lies strictly above $r_+$ and is a strict local maximum of $h$. The corresponding circular geodesic is linearly unstable under radial perturbations at fixed energy and angular momentum. The other algebraic stationary radius is $r_{\mathrm{ph}-}=(3m-\sqrt{9m^2-8Q^2})/2$; this proposition assigns it no exterior-orbit interpretation. Coordinates $x^0,r,m,q_e,q_m$ have length units, angular coordinates are dimensionless, and the affine parameter has arbitrary normalization. This is a null-ray calculation for the exact RN metric; it proves no wave-decay or Morawetz estimate.

statement.before: Let $(g,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on an open domain $U$ as in [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]]. If $X$ is a smooth vector field with local flow $\Phi_\epsilon$, then the pure-gauge perturbation $(\dot\Phi_0^*g,\dot\Phi_0^*\mathcal F)$ solves the linearized electrovacuum system on every common flow domain. More generally, the derivative at any parameter value of a smooth one-parameter family of exact backgrounds on a common domain solves the same linearized system. statement.proposed: Let $(g,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on an open domain $U$ as in [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]]. If $X$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ and $\Phi_\epsilon:V\to U$ is an orientation-preserving local flow it generates, where $V\subseteq U$ is open, $\Phi_0$ is the inclusion, and $\partial_\epsilon\Phi_\epsilon=X\circ\Phi_\epsilon$ wherever defined, then the pure-gauge perturbation $(\dot\Phi_0^*g,\dot\Phi_0^*\mathcal F)$ solves the linearized electrovacuum system on every common flow domain. More generally, let $\lambda\mapsto(g_\lambda,\mathcal F_\lambda)$ be a smooth one-parameter family of exact backgrounds on a common domain, with every member satisfying the equations for one fixed value of $\Lambda$. Its derivative at any parameter value solves the linearized system at that member. In the $\Lambda=0$ sector, fixed-domain Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman parameter families provide stationary parameter modes, meaning that their displayed metric and field components are independent of $x^0$, on exterior domains admitted by their verification results, when the parameters vary in an interval on which one such domain remains common. These conclusions do not classify the kernel of the linearized operator or determine which of its solutions arise as derivatives of exact solution families (integrable perturbations).

Let $T>0$ and consider a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on a normal-flow collar $[-T,T]\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, where $x^0=t$ is a length coordinate, $n=\partial_t$, and
$$g=-dt^2+\gamma_{ij}(t,\theta)d\theta^i d\theta^j$$
with $\gamma$ a smooth positive spatial metric. Fix the harmonic reference metric $\bar g$ to equal the background and define $H^a[g_\epsilon]:=g_\epsilon^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}[g_\epsilon]-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$, with $H_b[g_\epsilon]:=g_{\epsilon bc}H^c[g_\epsilon]$. Thus the background gauge vector vanishes and the linearized reduced metric equation is the derivative of $\operatorname{Ric}[g_\epsilon]-\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{(a}H_{b)}[g_\epsilon]-\Lambda g_{\epsilon ab}-2Q_{ab}(g_\epsilon,\mathcal F_\epsilon)=0$, where $Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd}$. Let $L_0>0$ be the fixed spatial length scale and write $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ with dimensionless coordinates $\theta^i$ on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Use the global coordinate frame on $\mathbb T^3$ and the smooth oriented spatial orthonormal triad obtained by Gram–Schmidt from it. The first-order state is the $56$-component periodic array $u=(h_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi},e_i,b_i)$, where $h$ is the metric perturbation, $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0h_{ab}$, $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i h_{ab}$, and $e_i,b_i$ are the six components of the two-form perturbation $f$ in the background triad. For arrays on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, define $H^k$ by the Fourier norm $\|u\|_{H^k}^2=\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|\ell|^2)^k|\widehat u(\ell)|^2$. Write $x=\theta$ in the system below and absorb the fixed factor $L_0^{-1}$ from $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$ into its spatial matrices. For any smooth linearized perturbation state $u$ and smooth source $s$, write the inhomogeneous first-order system in the chosen trivialization as
$$A^0(t,x)\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3 A^i(t,x)\partial_i u+C(t,x)u=s(t,x),$$
where $A^0,A^1,A^2,A^3,C$ are smooth periodic matrices, each $A^i$ and $A^0$ is symmetric, and constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ satisfy $aI\le A^0(t,x)\le bI$ throughout the slab. In the normal-flow chart, the harmonic metric reduction has time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(I,I,\gamma^{ij}I)$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [F1], while the six Maxwell field-strength variables have time matrix $I_6$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [F2]. When the Maxwell equations are linearized, derivatives of the perturbed lapse, frame and spatial metric occur through $p_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}$, which are components of the state and hence contribute to $C u$, not to spatial derivatives of the state. The variation of the Maxwell stress in the metric equation is algebraic in $(h,f)$ by [F3]. Thus the full principal matrices are the direct sums of the metric and Maxwell principal matrices, and the remaining couplings are smooth zeroth-order terms. Compactness of the slab then supplies uniform positive bounds for $A^0$.

For every integer $k\ge0$, define
$$\mathcal E_k(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}(\partial^\alpha u)^T A^0(t,x)\partial^\alpha u\,dx.$$
There is a constant $C_k$, depending only on $a,b,T$ and the coefficient derivatives through order $k+1$, such that
$$\|u(t)\|_{H^k}\le C_k e^{C_k|t|}\left(\|u(0)\|_{H^k}+\int_{\min(0,t)}^{\max(0,t)}\|s(\tau)\|_{H^k}\,d\tau\right),\qquad |t|\le T.$$
This is a finite-time conditional estimate, not an existence theorem or a global decay statement.

For the unforced linearized system, the Maxwell subsidiary constraints are the spatial restrictions of $df$ and $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)$ to a slice. If the normal-slot linearized Maxwell evolution equations hold and both initial restrictions vanish, they remain zero on the slab. Let $\dot H$ be the first variation of the harmonic gauge vector at the exact background. If the linearized reduced Einstein and Maxwell equations hold and $\dot H=\partial_t\dot H=0$ initially, then $\dot H=0$ throughout the slab. These are the Maxwell Gauss and harmonic-gauge subsidiary identities; no decay of the physical perturbation is asserted.

No global null normal pair is asserted.

Here a **smooth null hypersurface** $H\subset M$ means a smooth embedded
three-dimensional submanifold without boundary such that, at every $p\in H$,
the restriction $g_p|_{T_pH}$ is positive semidefinite of rank two. Its radical
is the one-dimensional subspace
$$\operatorname{Rad}(g_p|_{T_pH}):=\{v\in T_pH:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for every }w\in T_pH\}.$$
A **smooth future null normal field** on $H$ is a smooth nowhere-zero section
$\ell$ of this radical line, with $g_p(\ell_p,N_p)<0$. Thus
$$T_pH=\ell_p^\perp,\qquad (T_pH)^\perp=\operatorname{Rad}(g_p|_{T_pH})=\mathbb R\ell_p;$$
in particular, the normal space of a null hypersurface is a null line, not a
Lorentzian two-plane. A **spacelike section** $S$ of $H$ is a smooth embedded
two-manifold $S\subset H$ such that $q:=g|_{TS}$ is positive definite and
$$T_pH=T_pS\oplus\mathbb R\ell_p\qquad(p\in S).$$
The condition says that $S$ is transverse to the null generators.
The **null generator curves** are integral curves $\gamma$ of $\ell$, meaning
$\dot\gamma=\ell\circ\gamma$; when $D_\ell\ell=0$, their parameter is affine.
For fields defined only along $H$ or a surface $S$, covariant derivatives
$\nabla_X\ell$ use the pullback of the metric-selected connection.

For a smooth future null normal field $\ell$ on $H$, the quotient
$$\mathscr S_p:=\ell_p^\perp/\mathbb R\ell_p,\qquad p\in H,$$
is a smooth rank-two bundle with positive metric
$$\bar q_p([X],[Y]):=g_p(X,Y).$$
The normal line is $\mathbb R\ell_p$; the auxiliary null direction used in the
proof below is not a second normal to $H$. If $\ell$ is **affinely geodesic**,
meaning $D_\ell\ell=0$ along its integral curves, the map
$$B_p:\mathscr S_p\to\mathscr S_p,\qquad [X]\mapsto[\nabla_X\ell]$$
is well-defined and self-adjoint with respect to $\bar q$, that is,
$\bar q(Bu,v)=\bar q(u,Bv)$. On a spacelike section $S$ of $H$, the quotient
map $T_pS\to\mathscr S_p$, $X\mapsto[X]$, is an isometry; it is an isomorphism

normal $\ell$ to a spacelike surface $S$, define
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)\qquad(X,Y\in T_pS);$$

$\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$ is independent of the representative and

$$\ell\bigl(\bar q([X],[Y])\bigr)=\bar q(\mathcal D_\ell[X],[Y])+\bar q([X],\mathcal D_\ell[Y]).$$

Require, for every $\lambda\in J$, that its variation directions satisfy
$$g_{F(p,\lambda)}\bigl(\ell(p,\lambda),dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)\bigr)=0\qquad(X\in T_pU).$$
Thus its variation directions are orthogonal to $\ell$. For $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$, the map $F$ has rank three locally near $(p,\lambda)$: its two section directions are spacelike and orthogonal to the nonzero null vector $\ell$. Its local image is a null hypersurface, with tangent space $\ell^\perp$ and induced radical $\mathbb R\ell$, as in [[lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen]]. The parameter $\lambda$ is affine. On each section in $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified isometrically with the tangent plane of that section by projection. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

All screen bundles associated with this congruence are understood as bundles over the parameter domain $U\times J$: the notation $\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ denotes the branch determined by $(p,\lambda)$, so self-intersections do not identify distinct screen fibers. For each $\lambda\in J$, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$; it is invertible for $\lambda\in J_{\mathrm{reg}}(p)$. A **focal instant** is a positive parameter in $J$ where $A_\lambda$ loses rank; the **first focal instant**, if it exists, is the least such parameter after $0$. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. On $J_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$, and the **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$. Its **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and its **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint. Its antisymmetric part $\omega:=(B-B^*)/2$, called the twist, therefore vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

No orientation of $M$, $S$, or the screen is required for these constructions. Indeed, if two orthonormal screen frames are related by a real $2\times2$ matrix $O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}O=I_2$, then the endomorphism matrices obey $\widehat B=O^{-1}BO$ and $\widehat\sigma=O^{-1}\sigma O$. Cyclicity of the matrix trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\widehat B=\operatorname{tr}B$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\sigma^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma^2)=|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2$; the last equality follows by summing the squared entries of the symmetric shear matrix in an orthonormal frame. This includes $\det O=-1$. The screen inner products and the rank of $A_\lambda$ are likewise invariant under changes of frame, so neither the index-form contractions nor the focal condition uses a signed screen area form. The preceding lemma constructs normal pairs using the supplied time orientation and only a local spacelike complement; changing the complement's sign interchanges the two future null rays. No global ordered pair follows. If an orientation is additionally supplied, the same formulas apply on that oriented subclass.

generator and boost the pair by $\ell'=e^f\ell$, $k'=e^{-f}k$. Then

Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty compact smooth three-manifold without boundary. In
this item, “vacuum” means that the stress-energy tensor is zero and the
cosmological constant is fixed at $\Lambda=0$. Let $\widetilde h$ be a smooth
Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $\widetilde\sigma$ be a smooth symmetric
covariant two-tensor field, let $\tau\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and let
$\phi\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\phi(p)>0$ at every $p\in\Sigma$.
Use the positive scalar $\phi$ as a dimensionless conformal factor.

Write $\widetilde D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $\widetilde h$ and
$D$ for that of the metric $h$ defined below. In a chart, $\widetilde h^{ij}$
denotes the inverse matrix to $\widetilde h_{ij}$. It is smooth because
$\det(\widetilde h_{ij})>0$ and the matrix inverse is the adjugate divided by
the determinant. For any smooth Riemannian metric $m$ on $\Sigma$, with
Levi-Civita connection $D^m$, define
$$R^m(X,Y)Z:=D^m_XD^m_YZ-D^m_YD^m_XZ-D^m_{[X,Y]}Z.$$
In a chart, $R[m]^a{}_{bij}$ denotes the components of
$R^m(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_b$. Define
$\operatorname{Ric}(m)_{ij}:=R[m]^k{}_{ikj}$ and
$R(m):=m^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}(m)_{ij}$. In particular,
$\widetilde R:=R(\widetilde h)$, with the same curvature sign convention.
Define the scalar Laplacian by
$$\widetilde\Delta f:=\widetilde h^{ij} (\partial_i\partial_j f-\widetilde\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k f),$$
where $\widetilde\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ are the Christoffel symbols of
$\widetilde D$, given by the Levi-Civita Christoffel formula
[[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]].
The curvature sign is the one displayed above. All traces, norms, raising of
indices and contractions in this item use the metric indicated by the
subscript. In particular,
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\widetilde h}\widetilde\sigma:=\widetilde h^{ij}\widetilde\sigma_{ij},\qquad |\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2:=\widetilde h^{ik}\widetilde h^{j\ell}\widetilde\sigma_{ij}\widetilde\sigma_{k\ell},\qquad (\operatorname{div}_{\widetilde h}\widetilde\sigma)_j:=\widetilde h^{ik}\widetilde D_i\widetilde\sigma_{kj}.$$
The tensor $\widetilde\sigma$ is **transverse-traceless** (TT) when it is
symmetric and both displayed trace and divergence vanish.

Define
$$h:=\phi^4\widetilde h,\qquad K:=\phi^{-2}\widetilde\sigma+\frac{\tau}{3}h.$$
Because $\phi>0$, $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric; because
$\widetilde\sigma$ and $h$ are symmetric, $K$ is a smooth symmetric tensor.
Here $h$ is the candidate induced Riemannian metric and $K$ is the candidate
second fundamental form, with the library convention
$K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X n,Y)$ when the data are induced by a spacelike hypersurface
with future unit normal $n$. The pair is **vacuum conformal constraint data**.
It is abstract data on $\Sigma$; no embedding into a spacetime is part of this
definition. For its embedded Lorentzian interpretation assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the supplied smooth tangent-bundle
convention; the algebraic tensor definitions themselves use no choice
principle. Define the $h$-trace, squared norm and divergence by
$$\operatorname{tr}_hK:=h^{ij}K_{ij},\qquad |K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell},\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)_j:=h^{ik}D_iK_{kj}.$$
With $R(h)$ computed using $h$, define the Hamiltonian and momentum residuals
$$\mathcal H(h,K):=R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2,\qquad \mathcal M_j(h,K):=h^{ik}D_iK_{kj}-D_j(\operatorname{tr}_hK).$$
The data satisfy the vacuum constraint equations when
$\mathcal H(h,K)=0$ and $\mathcal M(h,K)=0$. For an embedded hypersurface,
these are the normal and normal-tangential Einstein constraints in the
specified $K$ convention.

Tensoriality of curvature and basis-independent contraction make these scalar
curvatures independent of the chart.
For dimensional bookkeeping in the SI length convention, $[\tau]=\mathrm m^{-1}$,
$[R(h)]=[\widetilde R]=[|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2]
=[\widetilde\Delta]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[\phi]=1$. Thus all terms in the
scalar constraint equation have units $\mathrm m^{-2}$.

Suppose the conformal metric has $\widetilde R=0$ and
$|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2=A$ is a positive constant, with constant
$\tau\ne0$. Then the Lichnerowicz equation has exactly one positive constant
solution,
$$\phi_0=\left(\frac{3A}{2\tau^2}\right)^{1/12}.$$

dimensionless. Uniqueness is only among positive constant solutions; no
uniqueness claim is made for arbitrary positive functions.

For the geometric initial-data convention, let $(M,g)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth embedded three-manifold whose induced metric $h:=\iota^*g$ is positive definite. The second fundamental form is $K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, with $\nabla$ the Levi-Civita connection of $g$ and the curvature sign convention stated in the Definition references section. The end data below are specified as a Riemannian metric and a symmetric tensor of these types; no embedding or Einstein constraint equation is required.

Let $E=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r>R_0\}$, where $R_0>0$ is a length, $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ are Cartesian coordinates measured in metres, and $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$. Write $\delta:=\delta_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$ for the standard Euclidean metric, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise; repeated spatial indices are summed over $1,2,3$. A **fixed-chart asymptotically Euclidean end** consists of this exterior domain, a $C^2$ symmetric positive-definite covariant $2$-tensor $h=h_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$, and a $C^1$ symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K=K_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$ such that
$$h_{ij}(x)=\delta_{ij}+\frac{a_{ij}}{r}+\rho_{ij}(x),\qquad K_{ij}(x)=O_1(r^{-2}),$$
where $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ is a constant real matrix, $\epsilon>0$, and $\rho=O_2(r^{-1-\epsilon})$. For any tensor components $T_{ij}$, the notation $T=O_k(r^{-q})$ means that for every multi-index $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)$ with $|\alpha|:=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\le k$ there are constants $C_\alpha,R_\alpha$ such that $|\partial^\alpha T_{ij}(x)|\le C_\alpha r^{-q-|\alpha|}$ for $r\ge R_\alpha$, uniformly in angle. Thus the definition requires two Cartesian derivatives of the metric remainder and one of $K$. The coordinates and $r$ have units of metres; $\delta_{ij}$ and $h_{ij}$ are dimensionless, $a_{ij}$ has units of metres, and $K$ has inverse-length units in a spatial orthonormal frame.

$$E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(h;x):=\frac{c^4}{16\pi G_N}\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R}\bigl(\partial_jh_{ij}-\partial_ih_{jj}\bigr)n^i\,dS,\qquad M_{\mathrm{ADM}}:=\frac{E_{\mathrm{ADM}}}{c^2}.$$
Here $c>0$ is the SI speed-of-light conversion constant with units metres per second, and $G_N>0$ is the Newtonian gravitational conversion constant with units metres cubed per kilogram per second squared. The limit has units of metres, $E_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ has units of joules, and $M_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ has units of kilograms. statement.before:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian boundary conventions inherited from [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. On its formal boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$, let $\ell_{\mathcal I}=\partial_u$ be the null-generator direction and let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric on the cuts; the degenerate boundary metric is $q_{AB}dx^A dx^B$ with kernel $\mathbb R\ell_{\mathcal I}$. In a fixed Bondi frame with $q_{AB}$ held fixed, an **infinitesimal supertranslation** is the asymptotic vector field parametrized by a smooth real function $f:S^2\to\mathbb R$ whose leading boundary action is $\delta_fu=f(x)$ and whose leading bulk generator is

$$\xi_f=f\,\partial_u-\frac1rD^Af\,\partial_A+\frac12D^AD_Af\,\partial_r+O(r^{-1})\partial_u+O(r^{-2})\partial_A+O(r^{-1})\partial_r.$$

The displayed leading terms preserve Bondi gauge and the fixed round cut metric to the asymptotic orders used here; the omitted terms are not part of this definition. We use the active convention $\delta_f=\mathcal L_{\xi_f}$. Its action on the shear and news of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]] is

$$\delta_f C_{AB}=fN_{AB}-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf,\qquad \delta_f N_{AB}=f\,\partial_uN_{AB}.$$

The function $f$ carries length units when the retarded coordinate $u$ is read in SI geometric coordinates; the sphere derivatives and angular coordinates are dimensionless. The Hessian term is trace-free because $q^{AB}q_{AB}=2$. When $N_{AB}=0$, an infinitesimal supertranslation therefore changes a time-independent shear by the sphere trace-free Hessian while leaving the news zero.
statement.proposed:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian boundary conventions inherited from [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. On its formal boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$, let $\ell_{\mathcal I}=\partial_u$ be the null-generator direction and let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric on the cuts; the degenerate boundary metric is $q_{AB}dx^A dx^B$ with kernel $\mathbb R\ell_{\mathcal I}$. A **fixed Bondi frame** here means the chosen Bondi-Sachs chart and gauge $(u,r,x^A)$ of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]], including $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$ and $\det\gamma=\det q$, with the round cut metric $q_{AB}$ held fixed. It is a chart/gauge choice, not an observer congruence or tetrad. An **infinitesimal supertranslation** is the asymptotic vector field parametrized by a smooth real function $f:S^2\to\mathbb R$ whose leading boundary action is $\delta_fu=f(x)$ and whose leading bulk generator is

$$\xi_f=f\,\partial_u-\frac1rD^Af\,\partial_A+\frac12D^AD_Af\,\partial_r+O(r^{-1})\partial_u+O(r^{-2})\partial_A+O(r^{-1})\partial_r.$$

The displayed leading terms preserve Bondi gauge and the fixed round cut metric to the asymptotic orders used here; the omitted terms are not part of this definition. We use the active convention $\delta_f=\mathcal L_{\xi_f}$. Its action on the shear and news of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]] is

$$\delta_f C_{AB}=fN_{AB}-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf,\qquad \delta_f N_{AB}=f\,\partial_uN_{AB}.$$

The **finite active boundary supertranslation** with parameter $f$ is the map $\Phi_f(u,x)=(u+f(x),x)$ on
$$\mathcal D_f:=\{(u,x)\in I\times S^2:u+f(x)\in I\}.$$
It is a diffeomorphism from $\mathcal D_f$ onto $\mathcal D_{-f}$, with inverse $\Phi_{-f}$. If $I=\mathbb R$, it is a diffeomorphism of all of $\mathcal I^+$; for a shorter retarded-time interval the action is defined on this overlap only. In the same active convention, its induced action on the boundary shear and news is

$$C^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=C_{AB}(u+f(x),x)-2D_AD_Bf(x)+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf(x),\qquad N^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=N_{AB}(u+f(x),x),\quad (u,x)\in\mathcal D_f.$$

Differentiating these formulas for the parameter $tf$ at $t=0$ recovers the infinitesimal formulas above. This definition gives only the boundary action and induced shear/news; it does not specify the full finite bulk coordinate transformation.

The function $f$ carries length units when the retarded coordinate $u$ is read in SI geometric coordinates; the sphere derivatives and angular coordinates are dimensionless. The Hessian term is trace-free because $q^{AB}q_{AB}=2$. When $N_{AB}=0$, an infinitesimal supertranslation therefore changes a time-independent shear by the sphere trace-free Hessian while leaving the news zero.

statement.before:
Assume Countable Choice and a smooth Bondi expansion as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. For $u_1<u_2$ in its retarded-length interval, define $\Delta C_{AB}:=C_{AB}(u_2)-C_{AB}(u_1)$. Then

$$\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}(u)\,du.$$

For the detector clause, fix an angular point and a large fixed area radius $r$. Use the local flat observer and propagation direction of [[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]] to identify the positive two-dimensional screen. A **linear transverse detector approximation** here means that the dimensionless screen metric perturbation is $H_{AB}(u)=C_{AB}(u,x)/r+\rho_{AB}(u,r,x)$, where the screen-TT remainder and its first two $u$-derivatives are $O(r^{-2})$ uniformly on $[u_1,u_2]$; retain only first order in $H$ and first order in separation. Let $s^A(u)$ be the screen Jacobi field of a smooth timelike geodesic variation, with affine parameter $u$ (equivalently $x^0=ct=u+r$ along the background central geodesic), initial data $s^A(u_1)=s^A$ and $\partial_us^A(u_1)=0$, and assume $N_{AB}(u_1)=N_{AB}(u_2)=0$. Then, at this linear separation order,

$$s^A(u_2)-s^A(u_1)=\frac{1}{2r}\Delta C^A{}_B\,s^B+O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|),\qquad \varepsilon:=\sup_{[u_1,u_2]}|H|_q.$$

Under the same approximation, the endpoint relative screen velocity satisfies $\partial_us^A(u_2)=O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$, so it has no leading $r^{-1}$ contribution when the news vanishes at both cuts.

The error constants depend on the fixed compact interval, angular patch and differentiated remainder bounds in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. No exact finite-radius identity $H_{AB}=C_{AB}/r$ is asserted.
statement.proposed:
Assume Countable Choice and a smooth Bondi expansion as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. For $u_1<u_2$ in its retarded-length interval, define $\Delta C_{AB}:=C_{AB}(u_2)-C_{AB}(u_1)$. Then

$$\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}(u)\,du.$$

For the detector clause, fix an angular point $x\in S^2$ and a large fixed area radius $r>r_0$. In the local flat approximation choose the future unit observer $n=\partial_0$ and outward unit propagation direction $\hat k=\partial_3$ of [[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]], so the positive screen is $\Sigma(n,\hat k)=\operatorname{span}(\partial_1,\partial_2)$. Let $\iota:S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be the unit-sphere inclusion; $d\iota_x$ identifies $T_xS^2$ isometrically, for $q$, with the plane orthogonal to $\iota(x)$. Choose axes with $e_3=\iota(x)$ and a fixed ordered orthonormal screen basis $e_1,e_2$ corresponding to a $q$-orthonormal basis of $T_xS^2$. Use adapted inertial coordinates with $x^0=ct$ and $x^3$ in the $\hat k$ direction. The background central worldline is the restriction to $[u_1,u_2]$ of the smooth future-directed timelike affine geodesic $\gamma_0(u)=(x^0=u+r,x^1=0,x^2=0,x^3=r)$; its affine parameter $u$ is also proper-length parameter, and on it the Bondi retarded coordinate is $u=x^0-r$.

A **linear transverse detector approximation** here is the formal flat first-order model with a dimensionless screen-TT profile $H_{AB}(u)=C_{AB}(u,x)/r+\rho_{AB}(u,r,x)$ in the chosen basis, extended on an open tube $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^4$ around $\gamma_0([u_1,u_2])$ as the planar perturbation $h_{AB}(x^0,x^3)=H_{AB}(x^0-x^3)$ with all other components zero. Take $H$ as the first-order coefficient of a smooth flat linearized metric family on $\Omega$; only this coefficient is used. Assume the profile has a smooth extension outside $[u_1,u_2]$; only its values on this interval enter. For $j=0,1,2$, assume $\sup_{u\in[u_1,u_2]}|\partial_u^j\rho_{AB}(u,r,x)|\le K_jr^{-2}$, where the constants $K_j$ are uniform on the fixed interval and angular patch and have dimensions $\mathrm{length}^{2-j}$. Let $s_0^A$ be any initial screen-separation components in the fixed basis, with zero initial relative velocity. Its **formal first-order response** $\delta s^A$ is the unique solution of the linearized screen Jacobi equation

$$\partial_u^2\delta s^A=\frac12\partial_u^2H^A{}_B\,s_0^B,\qquad \delta s^A(u_1)=0,\qquad \partial_u\delta s^A(u_1)=0,$$

with angular indices raised using $q^{AB}$. Assume $N_{AB}(u_1)=N_{AB}(u_2)=0$. This formal clause is a first-order response coefficient only; its quantitative realization is stated separately below. Then

$$\delta s^A(u_2)=\frac{1}{2r}\Delta C^A{}_B\,s_0^B+O(r^{-2}|s_0|).$$

Under the same approximation, the endpoint relative screen velocity has first-order response $\partial_u\delta s^A(u_2)=O(r^{-2}|s_0|)$, so it has no leading $r^{-1}$ contribution when the news vanishes at both cuts.

The error constants depend on the fixed compact interval, angular patch and the $K_j$ bounds. No exact finite-radius identity $H_{AB}=C_{AB}/r$ is asserted.

A quantitative amplitude statement is also available. Fix $r$, the angular point, and the interval $[u_1,u_2]$, and let $\Omega$ contain a compact coordinate tube around $\gamma_0([u_1,u_2])$. Supply any smooth flat linearized family
$$g_{ab}(\lambda,x)=\eta_{ab}+\lambda h_{ab}(x)+\lambda^2k_{ab}(\lambda,x)$$
on this tube, in the exact sense of [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], with the planar first-order coefficient $h_{AB}=H_{AB}(x^0-x^3)$ above and all other $h_{ab}=0$. The normalized remainder $k$ is smooth jointly in $(\lambda,x)$, and $\lambda$ is a dimensionless amplitude parameter. For small $|\lambda|$, use the future cone containing $\partial_0$ on a smaller tube. Issue the timelike geodesic $\gamma_\lambda$ from $\gamma_0(u_1)$ with unit initial velocity $\partial_0/\sqrt{-g_\lambda(\partial_0,\partial_0)}$. Choose a smooth initial orthonormal spatial frame tending to $(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ at $\lambda=0$, and parallel-transport it along $\gamma_\lambda$. Let $J_\lambda$ be the exact Jacobi field with initial value $s_0^AE_{A,\lambda}(u_1)$ and covariant initial derivative zero, and define $s_\lambda^A(u):=g_\lambda(J_\lambda,E_{A,\lambda})$, $A=1,2$. These are screen components in the transported frame; initial rest is covariant rest, not a coordinate-velocity condition. The geodesics, frames and Jacobi fields exist on the full fixed interval for sufficiently small $|\lambda|$, and $J_\lambda$ is realizable as a smooth timelike geodesic variation. There are constants for this fixed tube, interval and normalized family such that
$$s_\lambda(u_2)-s_0=\frac{\lambda}{2r}\Delta C\,s_0+O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|),\qquad s_\lambda'(u_2)=O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|).$$
More precisely, the actual screen components equal $s_0+\lambda\delta s+O(\lambda^2|s_0|)$, and their derivatives equal $\lambda\delta s'+O(\lambda^2|s_0|)$, uniformly on the interval. The first-order $r^{-2}$ constants are uniform wherever the stated $K_j$ bounds are uniform; the amplitude-squared constants here are for fixed $r$ and the chosen family and tube. No uniformity of those constants as $r\to\infty$ is asserted without uniform family bounds. The parameter $\lambda$ is not identified with $\sup|H|$. This is a local metric-family estimate, not an error estimate comparing a full Bondi spacetime with its detector approximation.

statement.before:
Let $Y(x)=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, and set $T_{AB}=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^CD_CY$. Let $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ be nonnegative, supported on $[-1,1]$, and normalized by $\int g(u)\,du=1$; choose a nonzero length $a$, and put $H(u)=\int_{-\infty}^u g(v)\,dv$, $C_{AB}(u,x)=aH(u)T_{AB}(x)$ and $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}=ag(u)T_{AB}$. With the mass aspect defined by the local vacuum coefficient equation and initial value $m(-1,x)=0$, these data have $\Delta C_{AB}=aT_{AB}$ and

$$m_B(1)-m_B(-1)=-\frac{a^2}{32\pi}\left(\int_{-1}^{1}g(u)^2\,du\right)\left(\int_{S^2}T_{AB}T^{AB}\,d\Omega\right)<0.$$

In the stated leading large-radius linear detector approximation, the same pulse gives $\Delta s^A=\tfrac{a}{2r}T^A{}_Bs^B+O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$ for initially comoving screen separation $s^A$ and $\varepsilon=\sup|C/r|$.
statement.proposed:
Let $\tau>0$ be a pulse length and let $a\ne0$ be a length. On the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric, $D_A$ its Levi-Civita derivative, and $d\Omega$ its area form. Put $Y(x)=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ and $T_{AB}=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^CD_CY$. Define the dimensionless bump $b(z)=e^{-1/(1-z^2)}$ for $|z|<1$ and $b(z)=0$ otherwise, let $Z=\int_{-1}^1b(z)\,dz$, and set $g_\tau(u)=b(u/\tau)/(\tau Z)$ and $\Phi_\tau(u)=\int_{-\infty}^u g_\tau(v)\,dv$. Then $g_\tau$ has units $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, support $[-\tau,\tau]$, and integral one. Set $C_{AB}=a\Phi_\tau T_{AB}$ and $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}=ag_\tau T_{AB}$. Impose the local coefficient constraint $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$ on these formal boundary data, with $m(-\tau,x)=0$, and define $m_B(u)=\tfrac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. It gives $\Delta C_{AB}=aT_{AB}$ and

$$m_B(\tau)-m_B(-\tau)=-\frac{a^2}{32\pi}\left(\int_{-\tau}^{\tau}g_\tau(u)^2\,du\right)\left(\int_{S^2}T_{AB}T^{AB}\,d\Omega\right)<0.$$

Let $r_0>0$ be a fixed inner radial cutoff with units of length. For the formal first-order detector response at a fixed sufficiently large area radius $r>r_0$, take a smooth screen-TT remainder $\rho_{AB}$ with $\sup_{[-\tau,\tau]}|\partial_u^j\rho_{AB}|\le K_jr^{-2}$ for $j=0,1,2$, where $K_j$ has dimensions $\mathrm{length}^{2-j}$, and put $H_{AB}=C_{AB}/r+\rho_{AB}$. In a fixed $q$-orthonormal screen basis, let $s_0^A$ be the initial separation and define $\delta s^A$ on $[-\tau,\tau]$ by $\partial_u^2\delta s^A=\tfrac12\partial_u^2H^A{}_B s_0^B$ with $\delta s(-\tau)=\partial_u\delta s(-\tau)=0$, raising indices with $q^{AB}$. Then $\delta s^A(\tau)=\tfrac{a}{2r}T^A{}_Bs_0^B+O(r^{-2}|s_0|)$; the formal clause alone makes no finite-amplitude error claim.

For any smooth normalized local metric family satisfying the quantitative clause of [[prop-gr-fx-memory-integral]] with this same $H$, use its initially covariantly comoving exact Jacobi field and parallel screen components $s_\lambda$. Then
$$s_\lambda(\tau)-s_0=\frac{\lambda a}{2r}T s_0+O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|),\qquad s_\lambda'(\tau)=O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|).$$
The amplitude-squared constants are for the fixed local family, tube and interval $[-\tau,\tau]$; $\lambda$ is its controlled dimensionless parameter. This does not assert Ricci-flatness of the constructed Bondi-Sachs end or identify that end with the local detector family.

statement.before: Let $Y(x)=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ on $S^2$, set $f=aY$ for a nonzero length $a$, and consider the infinitesimal supertranslation shear $C_{AB}:=\delta_fC_{AB}=-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf$ of flat Bondi data. This shear is time-independent and nonzero, but $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}=0$, so the vacuum mass-loss law gives $dm_B/du=0$ and the classical memory integral gives $\Delta C_{AB}=0$ on every retarded-time interval. A shear value alone is therefore not radiated power or memory.
statement.proposed: Let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric on $S^2$, $D_A$ its Levi-Civita derivative, and $d\Omega$ its area form. On $I=\mathbb R$ and $r>r_0>0$, with $r_0$ a length, the exact flat Bondi metric is $g_0=-du^2-2du\,dr+r^2q_{AB}dx^A dx^B$; its shear, news and mass aspect are $C_{AB}=N_{AB}=m=0$. Let $m_B(u)=\tfrac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. Let $Y(x)=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ on $S^2$, set $f=aY$ for a nonzero length $a$, and use the finite active boundary action $C^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=C_{AB}(u+f(x),x)-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf$, $N^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=N_{AB}(u+f(x),x)$. It gives $C^{(f)}_{AB}=-2aT_{AB}$, where $T_{AB}=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^2Y$, and $N^{(f)}_{AB}=0$. Treat these as formal boundary data with $m=0$ and impose the local coefficient constraint $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$. Then $m_B=0$, $dm_B/du=0$, and $\Delta C_{AB}=0$ on every retarded-time interval, where $\Delta C_{AB}=C_{AB}(u_2,x)-C_{AB}(u_1,x)$ for $u_1<u_2$. No full finite-transformed vacuum metric is asserted. A nonzero shear value alone therefore does not imply nonzero news or a nonzero shear difference.

statement.before:
Let $T=\partial_t$ be the stationary field and let $\Phi$ be the sphere
rotation field, extended to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$. Both are Killing fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.
statement.proposed:
Let $T=\partial_t$ be the stationary field and let $\Phi$ be the sphere
rotation field, extended to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$. Both are Killing fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. In the ingoing product coordinates $(v,r,p)$, the smooth field
$$\overline N:=\partial_v-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\partial_r$$
is timelike on the extension and selects a time orientation agreeing with the
chosen exterior time orientation. On $H^+$ one has $g(\chi,\overline N)=-1$,
so $\chi$ is its future null generator. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.

statement.before:
At an exterior point $p$ where the stationary Killing field $T=\partial_t$ is
spacelike, let $n$ be any observer and consider the canonical real scalar
matter model with $V=0$ and coupling $K>0$. The associated
Killing-multiplier density $\rho_T(p;n)$ takes negative values for suitable
smooth local scalar fields. Thus this stationary current has no pointwise
nonnegative density on all scalar first-derivative data in the ergoregion and,
by itself, cannot be a positive coercive energy density there. If the scalar
equation holds, the current is conserved; this example does not assert
existence of a global solution with any prescribed pointwise derivative.
statement.proposed:
At an exterior point $p$ where the stationary Killing field $T=\partial_t$ is
spacelike, let $U$ be an oriented coordinate neighborhood of $p$, restrict the
real scalar-field model to $U$, set its potential to $V=0$, fix a coupling
$K>0$, and let $n$ be any observer at $p$. There is a smooth scalar field
$\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ for which the associated Killing-multiplier density
$\rho_T(p;n)$ is negative. Thus this stationary current is not pointwise
nonnegative on all scalar first-derivative data in the ergoregion and cannot
itself supply a pointwise positive coercive energy density there; the
nonnegativity on every admissible datum used here is a necessary condition for
such a density. If a scalar field on $U$ satisfies its scalar equation, its
current is conserved. This example does not assert that an on-shell field
exists with the prescribed derivative.

statement.before:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $s>0$ and let $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ be the
regular advanced-chart extension of the Schwarzschild exterior, with
$f(r)=1-s/r$ and stationary field $T=\partial_v$. Let $C$ be a compact finite
smooth singular four-chain in the exterior closure $r\geq s$, with oriented
boundary
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+\mathcal H^++B_{\mathrm{out}}$, where
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$ are spacelike faces with future unit normals $n_1,n_2$,
$\mathcal H^+$ is a future-horizon face, and $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the
remaining signed outer boundary. Let $\psi$ be smooth on a neighborhood of
$C$ and solve $\Box_{g_{\mathrm{ext}}}\psi=0$. Define
$j_T^a:=-Q^{a}{}_{b}[\psi]T^b$. Orient each spacelike face $\Sigma_j$ so
that its adapted unit normal is the future unit normal $n_j$, and define

$$E_j:=\Phi_{j_T}(\Sigma_j)=\int_{\Sigma_j}Q_{ab}[\psi]n_j^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_j}.$$

Define $F_{\mathrm{out}}$ as the signed flux of
$j_T$ through $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ and

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $0<|a|<M$ and let $H^+$ be a regular
future Kerr horizon patch with stationary field $T$, axial field $\Phi$,
future null generator $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, and
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Let $u$ be a nonzero smooth $(\omega,m)$ mode
trace on $H^+$, where $\omega>0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, and suppose that
$\psi=\operatorname{Re}u$ is the trace of a smooth real scalar field near
$H^+$. No wave equation or global extension of the mode is assumed. Define
$\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T$ as the average of the real scalar flux density
$Q_{ab}[\psi]\chi^aT^b$ over one stationary-flow period $2\pi/\omega$.
Then

$$\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T=\frac12\omega(\omega-m\Omega_H)|u|^2.$$

Consequently, when $m\Omega_H>\omega>0$, this stationary horizon-flux density is nonpositive everywhere, is zero at every node $u=0$, and is strictly negative exactly where $u\ne0$.

For a compact smooth spacelike horizon-cut patch $D$ with nonempty interior and smooth boundary, contained in the mode domain, let $d\mu_D$ be the positive area measure of its induced metric. Define the integrated averaged stationary flux by
$$\mathcal F_D:=\int_D\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T\,d\mu_D =\frac12\omega(\omega-m\Omega_H)\int_D|u|^2\,d\mu_D.$$
In the same frequency band, $\mathcal F_D<0$ whenever $u|_D$ is not identically zero. A smooth nonzero mode therefore has strictly negative integrated averaged flux on a sufficiently small compact spacelike cut patch meeting its nonzero set. This is a conditional local mode-trace calculation; it does not assert the existence of a global wave or scattering solution.
statement.proposed:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $0<|a|<M$, and let
$P\subset H^+=\{r=r_+\}$ be the smooth open mode patch, with stationary field $T$, axial field $\Phi$,
future null generator $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, and
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Let $u\in C^\infty(P,\mathbb C)$ be a nonzero
$(\omega,m)$ mode trace, where $\omega>0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, and suppose that
$\psi=\operatorname{Re}u$ is the trace of a smooth real scalar field near
$P$. No wave equation or global extension of the mode is assumed. For each
$p\in P$, let $\gamma_p:I_p\to H^+$ be the unique maximal integral curve of
$T$ through $p$, with $\gamma_p(0)=p$ and maximal open interval domain
$I_p\subseteq\mathbb R$. For
$p$ with $[0,2\pi/\omega]\subset I_p$ and
$\gamma_p([0,2\pi/\omega])\subset P$, define

$$\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T(p):=\frac{\omega}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}Q_{ab}[\psi](\gamma_p(\tau))\chi^aT^b\,d\tau.$$

Write $P_{\omega,T}$ for the set of such points. Then, for every
$p\in P_{\omega,T}$,

$$\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T=\frac12\omega(\omega-m\Omega_H)|u|^2.$$

Consequently, when $m\Omega_H>\omega>0$, this averaged stationary horizon-flux density is nonpositive at every point of $P_{\omega,T}$, is zero at every node $u=0$, and is strictly negative exactly where $u\ne0$.

For a compact smooth spacelike horizon-cut patch $D\subset P_{\omega,T}$ with
nonempty interior and smooth boundary, let $d\mu_D$ be the positive area
measure of its induced metric. Thus the mode domain contains the full
integral-curve segment of length $2\pi/\omega$ from every point of $D$. Define the
integrated averaged stationary flux by
$$\mathcal F_D:=\int_D\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T\,d\mu_D =\frac12\omega(\omega-m\Omega_H)\int_D|u|^2\,d\mu_D.$$
In the same frequency band, $\mathcal F_D<0$ whenever $u|_D$ is not identically zero. At any $p\in P_{\omega,T}$ with $u(p)\ne0$, such an admissible patch can be chosen around $p$. This is a conditional local mode-trace calculation; it does not assert the existence of a global wave or scattering solution.

Fix one evolution problem, its state space and its declared classical solution class. For the general-relativity application here, use one fixed periodic symmetric-hyperbolic system on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ with integer regularity $s\ge5$, a fixed gauge, smooth coefficient maps on an open state domain, symmetric principal matrices and a positive time matrix. On each compact time slab, its normalized state $u$ belongs to $L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$ and has $\partial_tu\in L^\infty H^{s-1}$, with the fixed-gauge data and coefficient bounds specified in the references below.

A forward solution on $[0,T_{\max})$ is **maximal** in this solution class when no solution on $[0,T_{\max}+\rho)$, for any $\rho>0$, agrees with it on $[0,T_{\max})$. Let $E_{\rm raw}$ be a specified nonnegative scalar functional of the solution, continuous on every compact subinterval of $[0,T_{\max})$. If $E_{\rm raw}$ has units, choose a fixed positive scale $E_*$ with the same units and set $E=E_{\rm raw}/E_*$. In the general-relativity convention the time coordinate is $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ in metres; choose a fixed length scale $L_*>0$ and use the dimensionless time $t=x^0/L_*$. Thus $E$ and $t$ are dimensionless. The constants $A$, $\epsilon$ and $\eta$ below are dimensionless as well. In a purely mathematical application, take these variables as real scalars without a physical interpretation.

Specify a finite list of dimensionless margin functions $m_j:[0,T_{\max})\to\mathbb R$ and thresholds $\mu_j>0$. Write $\mathcal M(T)$ when $m_j(t)\ge\mu_j$ for every listed $j$ and every $0\le t<T$. The **continuation criterion** is a separate result for the chosen evolution problem: if a solution has a finite right endpoint $T$ with $E(t)\le\eta$ for every $0\le t<T$ and $\mathcal M(T)$, then it extends past $T$ in the same solution class.

For constants $A>0$, $\epsilon>0$ and $\eta>0$ with $2A\epsilon^2<\eta$, a **bootstrap estimate** is the implication, required on every finite $T<T_{\max}$,

$$\left[ E(t)\le2A\epsilon^2\text{ for all }0\le t\le T\right]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\left[ E(t)\le A\epsilon^2\text{ for all }0\le t\le T\right].$$

This contract records the continuity and continuation inputs needed by an application. It does not itself prove the bootstrap estimate, the margin bounds, or any Einstein evolution estimate.

statement.before: The accessed 2021 Klainerman–Szeftel manuscript describes a nonlinear stability result for the Kerr family at sufficiently small angular momentum, in asymptotically flat solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations, and presents it as a multi-paper proof. This records the authors' stated scope; it is not a local proof or an independent acceptance of every companion paper. The 2008 review's discussion of then-known global constructions of dynamical vacuum black-hole spacetimes is historical and is not used here as current status. This remark makes no claim about whether the full subextremal or extremal Kerr stability problem is open or solved.
statement.proposed:
For the mathematical terms, let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $\iota:\Sigma_0\hookrightarrow M$ a spacelike embedded three-manifold. Vacuum initial data mean $(\Sigma_0,h_0,K_0)$, where $h_0=\iota^*g$ and $K_0(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for tangent vectors $V,W$ and the unique future-directed unit normal $n$; the data satisfy the matter-free, zero-cosmological-constant specialization of the initial-data constraints. Here the vacuum Einstein equation means $\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0$ with the curvature convention defining its Ricci tensor. A Cauchy hypersurface is a spacelike embedded hypersurface met exactly once, in parameter value, by every inextendible causal curve. A future globally hyperbolic development is a time-oriented Lorentzian solution with an embedding of $\Sigma_0$ as a Cauchy hypersurface inducing $h_0$ and $K_0$. The local Kerr definition uses geometric parameters $M>0$ and $|a|<M$ for the subextremal exterior; when a physical interpretation is adopted, $M=G_Nm_{\mathrm{phys}}/c^2$ and $a=J_{\mathrm{phys}}/(m_{\mathrm{phys}}c)$, with $G_N$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $c$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $m_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in $\mathrm{kg}$ and $J_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. Thus $M$ and $a$ have units $\mathrm m$, and $a$ is the specific-angular-momentum length parameter. The paper's notation $\operatorname{Kerr}(a_0,m_0)$ corresponds to $(a,M)=(a_0,m_0)$, and its smallness condition $|a_0|/m_0\ll1$ is dimensionless.

For asymptotic terminology, an end is a component outside a compact subset of $\Sigma_0$, equipped with coordinates $x$ onto $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r=|x|>R\}$. A basic asymptotically flat initial-data convention is $h_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_1(r^{-1})$ and $K_{ij}=O_1(r^{-2})$: $T=O_k(r^{-q})$ means that each component satisfies $|\partial^\alpha T|\le C_\alpha r^{-q-|\alpha|}$ for all multiindices $|\alpha|\le k$, uniformly in direction for sufficiently large $r$. These are the explicit end conditions in Gourgoulhon, §7.2.1, equations (7.1)–(7.4); they describe the asymptotic terminology, not a sufficient stability hypothesis. The local ADM-end definition gives the mass surface integral on its more specialized end class; it does not assert that its special expansion exhausts the data in the Kerr source. In a fixed asymptotically Cartesian chart, the geometric ADM mass is, whenever the finite limit exists,

$$
m_{\rm ADM}=\frac{1}{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|=R}(\partial_jh_{ij}-\partial_ih_{jj})\frac{x^i}{R}\,dS_\delta.
$$

Here $dS_\delta$ is Euclidean sphere area, repeated indices are summed from $1$ to $3$, and the physical energy and mass are $E_{\rm ADM}=c^4m_{\rm ADM}/G_N$ and $M_{\rm ADM}=c^2m_{\rm ADM}/G_N$. For a chosen oriented rotation axis in that chart, let $\varphi=x^1\partial_2-x^2\partial_1$ for the third axis, with cyclic variants for the other axes. With the present convention $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$, its geometric angular-momentum charge is, whenever this finite limit exists,

$$
\mathcal J(\varphi)=-\frac{1}{8\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|=R}\bigl(K_{ij}-(\operatorname{tr}_hK)h_{ij}\bigr)\varphi^i\nu_h^j\,dS_h.
$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$, $\nu_h$ is the outward $h$-unit sphere normal, and $dS_h$ is its induced area. This is Gourgoulhon's equation (7.63) with the sign translated from his $K(V,W)=-g(\nabla_Vn,W)$, equation (2.43). The geometric charge has units $\mathrm{m^2}$ and $J_{\rm phys}=c^3\mathcal J/G_N$; for Kerr about its spin axis, $\mathcal J=Ma$. Thus the source's parameter $a_0$ denotes the spin length, not a total angular momentum with SI units. Neither existence nor coordinate invariance of angular momentum follows just from the displayed basic falloff: a fixed asymptotic frame and the source's charge/admissibility conditions are retained, rather than silently imposing one additional parity or gauge condition on its theorem; see Gourgoulhon §7.5.2 for this distinction.

In this report the stability assertion quantifies over precisely the source's own initial-data class. Definition 3.4.2 takes an initial-data layer $L_0(a_0,m_0)$ in the future of asymptotically flat data on a spacelike $\Sigma_0$, with source parameters $m_0$ and $a_0$, and defines $(\epsilon_0,k)$-admissibility using its initial-layer norm $I_k$ from §3.3.6. The unnumbered Main Theorem (version 2) in §3.4.3 assumes $|a_0|/m_0$ sufficiently small, $k_{\rm large}$ sufficiently large, $\epsilon_0$ sufficiently small, and in particular $I_{k_{\rm large}+10}\le\epsilon_0^2$. Definition 3.4.5 uses “admissible future null complete” for a future development of such a layer with complete $\mathscr I^+$ and its other listed geometric conditions.

For the completeness terminology, a null generator with affine parameter $\lambda$ has nonzero future null tangent $\ell$, $g(\ell,\ell)=0$ and $\nabla_\ell\ell=0$; future completeness means that its maximal future affine parameter is unbounded above. A change $\lambda\mapsto A\lambda+B$, $A>0$, preserves this property; complete future null infinity means that every one of its future generators is complete in this sense. Here the source's future null infinity $\mathscr I^+$ is the asymptotic boundary $r\to\infty$ along its outgoing $u$-foliation, not an additional hypothesis of a smooth conformal completion. Section 3.8.1, pp. 152–153, identifies its limiting null generators and explains completeness using the leaves for all $u\ge1$ and the generator normalization: the limiting generator has $du/d\lambda=2+O(\epsilon_0/u^{1+\delta})$ for the source's $\delta>0$ and small $\epsilon_0$, hence this derivative is bounded above and below by positive constants and unbounded $u$ gives unbounded future affine parameter. This specifies the reported boundary completeness; it does not say that every null geodesic of the black-hole spacetime is future complete.

The arXiv v1 abstract says that the authors prove full unconditional nonlinear stability of this small-angular-momentum Kerr family in asymptotically flat solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations. Its simplified Theorem 1.2.1 states that the future globally hyperbolic development of a general initial-data set in that source class, sufficiently close in a suitable topology to $\operatorname{Kerr}(a_0,m_0)$ initial data and with sufficiently small $|a_0|/m_0$, has complete future null infinity and converges in the source's set $J^{-1}(\mathscr I^+)$ to a nearby $\operatorname{Kerr}(a_\infty,m_\infty)$, with final parameters close to the initial ones. The precise convergence and parameter-closeness conclusions are stated in the authors' norms, including estimate (3.4.8).

This is a report of the authors' stated result and its source-defined scope, not a local proof or independent verification of the full series. The v1 abstract records that three companion papers had been released and the remaining papers were expected; §1.2.1 identifies estimates assigned to forthcoming papers. The 2008 review's discussion of then-known global constructions is historical only. This remark makes no current-status claim about whether the full subextremal or extremal Kerr stability problem is open or solved.

Let $c>0$ be a fixed conversion constant in metres per second. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of physical time in seconds, and let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ have dimensionless angular coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3$. Its quotient charts are local lifts to $\mathbb R^3$; chart changes are translations by elements of $(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$. Give $M=I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the product smooth structure, so $M$ is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Choose positive $C^2$ functions $a_i:I\to(0,\infty)$, $i=1,2,3$, with values in metres. The metric

$$g=-c^2\,dt^2+\sum_{i=1}^3a_i(t)^2\,(dx^i)^2$$

has signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and is $C^2$ on the product manifold. Choose the smooth vector field $N=\partial_t$ as its time orientation: the relevant pointwise condition from the Lorentzian definition is $g(N,N)=-c^2<0$, which is meaningful at this $C^2$ regularity. Let $N\ge3$, $h=2\pi/N$, $k>0$, and $\lambda=k/h$. Complexify the real
linear recurrence of the periodic wave algorithm. For each discrete Fourier
index $\ell\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}$ define the mode
$$
e_\ell(j):=\exp(2\pi i\ell j/N),\qquad j\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z.
$$
If $0<\lambda<1$, every nonconstant mode ($\ell\ne0$) has recurrence
coefficient
$$
c_\ell:=1-2\lambda^2\sin^2(\pi\ell/N)\in(-1,1)
$$
and two distinct amplification roots
$$
z_{\ell,\pm}:=c_\ell\pm i\sqrt{1-c_\ell^2},\qquad |z_{\ell,\pm}|=1.
$$
Consequently, each fixed nonconstant mode has bounded amplitude on every
finite slab. For arbitrary real initial arrays define their spatial means by
$$
\bar u^0:=\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}u^0_j,\qquad \bar v^0:=\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v^0_j.
$$
The constant mode has the repeated root $1$ and evolves exactly as
$\bar u^0+nk\bar v^0$; for any fixed $T\ge0$ it is bounded on the slab
$0\le nk\le T$ but has no uniform-in-time displacement bound when
$\bar v^0\ne0$. This statement
does not assert that the condition $0<\lambda<1$ alone proves convergence of a
numerical relativity scheme. For each fixed $N$, define the nonzero discrete
frequencies $\omega_\ell:=2h^{-1}|\sin(\pi\ell/N)|$, $1\le\ell<N$.

uniform in $N$ is asserted.

the Nyquist mode. At the endpoint $\lambda=1$, if $N$ is even and
$u_j^0=a_0(-1)^j$, $v_j^0=\beta_0(-1)^j$ for real amplitudes $a_0,\beta_0$,
then each output level satisfies
$$
u_j^n=(-1)^j(-1)^n(a_0-nk\beta_0).
$$
The Nyquist amplification root is repeated at $-1$, and a nonzero Nyquist
velocity amplitude $\beta_0$ gives linear growth in the step number.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open, and let $u:I\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$
be six times continuously differentiable and $2\pi$-periodic in its spatial
variable $x$. Assume the nondimensional scalar wave equation
$u_{tt}=u_{xx}$ on $I\times\mathbb R$. For $N\ge3$, $h=2\pi/N$, $k>0$,
$x_j=jh$, and an integer $n$ with $t_n=nk$ and
$[t_n-k,t_n+k]\subset I$, put
$$
U_j^n:=u(x_j,t_n),\qquad \tau_j^n:=\frac{U_j^{n+1}-2U_j^n+U_j^{n-1}}{k^2} -\frac{U_{j+1}^n-2U_j^n+U_{j-1}^n}{h^2}.
$$
Set $M_n$ to be the supremum
$$
M_n:=\sup\{|\partial_x^4u(x,t)|:0\le x\le2\pi,\ t_n-k\le t\le t_n+k\}.
$$
Then for every grid index $j$,
$$
|\tau_j^n|\le\frac{k^2+h^2}{12}M_n.
$$
Thus the normalized local truncation residual is $O(k^2+h^2)$ on each
compact time window where the displayed fourth-derivative bound is uniform.
This consistency estimate alone is not a convergence theorem.
