Assume Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ be an open coordinate chart of a three-dimensional Brillouin torus, let $h:U\to M_r(\mathbb C)$ be the restriction of a $C^2$ Hermitian finite-range Bloch fiber family, and let $\varepsilon:U\to\mathbb R$ be a simple eigenvalue with a positive local gap from the other eigenvalues. On a local chart choose a $C^2$ normalized eigenvector $u(k)$ for $\varepsilon(k)$. Under an adopted slow-force single-band effective description, for position $x\in\mathbb R^3$, crystal wave vector $k\in U$, constant signed charge $q$, constant electric field $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}$, and reduced Planck constant $\hbar>0$, take the effective Lagrangian

$$L=\hbar k\cdot\dot x+i\hbar\,u(k)^*\nabla_k u(k)\cdot\dot k-\varepsilon(k)+q\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot x.$$

Here $k$ is measured in radians per metre, $x$ in metres, $\varepsilon$ in joules, $q$ in coulombs, $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}$ in volts per metre, and $\hbar$ in joule seconds. Let $\mathcal A(k):=i u(k)^*\nabla_k u(k)\in\mathbb R^3$ and $\boldsymbol\Omega(k):=\nabla_k\times\mathcal A(k)$. Every $C^2$ stationary curve of this adopted effective action satisfies

$$\hbar\dot k=q\mathbf E_{\rm ext},\qquad \dot x=\frac{1}{\hbar}\nabla_k\varepsilon-\dot k\times\boldsymbol\Omega.$$

The equations are invariant under a local phase change of $u$. This is the exact Euler–Lagrange consequence of the stated effective Lagrangian; it supplies no error estimate for replacing the underlying quantum dynamics by that Lagrangian.

For a two-band specialization, the normalization of $\boldsymbol\Omega$ agrees with the Chern convention of the two-band degree formula.
statement.proposed:
Assume Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mathbf a_1,\mathbf a_2,\mathbf a_3\in\mathbb R^3$ be a basis of direct-lattice vectors, each measured in metres, and set $\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^3\mathbb Z\mathbf a_j$ and $\Lambda^*:=\{\mathbf G\in\mathbb R^3:\mathbf G\cdot\mathbf R\in2\pi\mathbb Z\text{ for all }\mathbf R\in\Lambda\}$, whose vectors have units of inverse metres. The reciprocal-space torus is $\mathbb R^3/\Lambda^*$; let $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ be an open set on which the quotient map is injective, giving local wave-vector coordinates. For $\delta\in\mathbb Z^3$ put $\mathbf R_\delta=\sum_j\delta_j\mathbf a_j$ and $\theta_j(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a_j\pmod{2\pi}$. Fix finite $S\subset\mathbb Z^3$ with $S=-S$ and hopping matrices $T_\delta\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $T_{-\delta}=T_\delta^*$; assign the entries of $T_\delta$ units of joules. The finite-range physical fiber is

$$h(\mathbf k)=\sum_{\delta\in S}T_\delta e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R_\delta}=\sum_{\delta\in S}T_\delta e^{-i\theta(\mathbf k)\cdot\delta},$$

which is the fiber in [[def-nrqmx-bloch-fiber-model]] written in physical reciprocal coordinates. Its entries and its eigenvalues have energy units (joules). Let $\varepsilon:U\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^2$ simple eigenvalue of $h(\mathbf k)$ and, after shrinking $U$ if needed, assume its distance from the other eigenvalues is at least some $\gamma>0$ throughout $U$. Choose a $C^2$ local normalized eigenvector $u:U\to\mathbb C^r$ with $h(\mathbf k)u(\mathbf k)=\varepsilon(\mathbf k)u(\mathbf k)$ and $u(\mathbf k)^*u(\mathbf k)=1$.

Let $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ denote a position coordinate measured in metres, $\mathbf k\in U$ the physical crystal wave vector measured in inverse metres (radians are dimensionless), $q$ a constant signed charge in coulombs, $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\in\mathbb R^3$ a constant electric field in volts per metre, and $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck constant in joule seconds. Under the adopted single-band effective description, take

$$L=\hbar\mathbf k\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}+i\hbar\,u(\mathbf k)^*\nabla_{\mathbf k}u(\mathbf k)\cdot\dot{\mathbf k}-\varepsilon(\mathbf k)+q\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf x.$$

Here each term of $L$ has units of joules. Define the real Berry connection $\mathcal A_j(\mathbf k):=i u(\mathbf k)^*\partial_{k_j}u(\mathbf k)$, whose components have units of metres, and the Berry-curvature vector $\boldsymbol\Omega(\mathbf k):=\nabla_{\mathbf k}\times\mathcal A(\mathbf k)$, whose components have units of square metres. For time $t$ measured in seconds, a compact interval $I=[t_0,t_1]$ with $t_0<t_1$, and curves $\mathbf x,\mathbf k\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\mathbf k(t)\in U$, define the action $\mathscr S[\mathbf x,\mathbf k]=\int_{t_0}^{t_1}L(\mathbf x(t),\mathbf k(t),\dot{\mathbf x}(t),\dot{\mathbf k}(t))\,dt$. A curve is **stationary** if $\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}\mathscr S[\mathbf x_s,\mathbf k_s]=0$ for every jointly $C^2$ variation $(s,t)\mapsto(\mathbf x_s(t),\mathbf k_s(t))$, $|s|<\eta$, with $(\mathbf x_0,\mathbf k_0)=(\mathbf x,\mathbf k)$, fixed endpoints $\mathbf x_s(t_i)=\mathbf x(t_i)$ and $\mathbf k_s(t_i)=\mathbf k(t_i)$ for $i=0,1$, and $\mathbf k_s(t)\in U$. Every such $C^2$ stationary curve of this adopted effective action satisfies

$$\hbar\dot{\mathbf k}=q\mathbf E_{\rm ext},\qquad \dot{\mathbf x}=\frac{1}{\hbar}\nabla_{\mathbf k}\varepsilon-\dot{\mathbf k}\times\boldsymbol\Omega.$$

The action has units of joule seconds. The equations are invariant under a local phase change of $u$. The words “wave packet” and “slow-force” name only the physical motivation and regime label of this adopted effective model; no wave-packet object is used in the deduction, and no approximation-validity or error-bound claim about underlying quantum dynamics is made. For the two-band specialization, take $r=2$. Let $\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2,\mathbf b_3$ be the reciprocal basis, defined by $\mathbf b_j\cdot\mathbf a_\ell=2\pi\delta_{j\ell}$, so $\Lambda^*=\sum_j\mathbb Z\mathbf b_j$. Fix $\tau\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and the closed reciprocal two-torus

$$\Sigma_\tau=\{[\mathbf k]\in\mathbb R^3/\Lambda^*: \theta_3(\mathbf k)=\tau\},\qquad \kappa_\tau(\theta_1,\theta_2)=\left[\frac{\theta_1\mathbf b_1+\theta_2\mathbf b_2+\tau\mathbf b_3}{2\pi}\right].$$

Here $\kappa_\tau:\mathbb T^2_{2\pi}\to\Sigma_\tau$ is a diffeomorphism and fixes the orientation by $d\theta_1\wedge d\theta_2$. Suppose the restriction has the two-band form $h\circ\kappa_\tau=d_0I+d\cdot\sigma$ of [[thm-nrqmx-two-band-degree-formula]], with $d$ nowhere zero on this entire torus. Put $n=d/|d|$ and $P_s=(I+s n\cdot\sigma)/2$, $s\in\{+1,-1\}$; the chosen local eigenvector belongs to that band wherever its chart meets the slice. Interpret $P_s$ also as the corresponding globally defined projector on $\Sigma_\tau$. Define the global real two-form

$$\mathcal B_s:=i\,\operatorname{tr}\bigl(P_s(dP_s\wedge dP_s)P_s\bigr).$$

On every local normalized eigenvector chart this is $d\mathcal A$ for $\mathcal A=i u^*du$; it does not require a global eigenvector. In physical reciprocal coordinates, the coordinate conversion on every such chart is

$$\kappa_\tau^*\mathcal B_s=\frac{\boldsymbol\Omega(\kappa_\tau(\theta))\cdot(\mathbf b_1\times\mathbf b_2)}{(2\pi)^2}\,d\theta_1\wedge d\theta_2.$$

The coefficient is dimensionless, since $\boldsymbol\Omega$ has units of square metres and each reciprocal basis vector has inverse-metre units. With this orientation and the same band sign,

$$\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\Sigma_\tau}\mathcal B_s=\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb T^2_{2\pi}}\operatorname{tr}\bigl(P_s(dP_s\wedge dP_s)P_s\bigr)=C(P_s)=-s\deg(n).$$

The integrals are over the whole closed torus, and the exterior derivatives in the second integral are in the dimensionless $\theta$ coordinates. This is the Chern convention of [[thm-nrqmx-two-band-degree-formula]].

Let $d\ge1$, let $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ act on $\mathbb C^d$ with its standard complex inner product, and let $z\in\mathbb C$. Define the finite-dimensional matrix exponential by
$$e^{zA}:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^kA^k}{k!},\qquad A^0=I_d.$$
Every matrix $B=(b_{ij})\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ is bounded on $\mathbb C^d$: since $|x_j|\le\|x\|$ for the standard Euclidean norm, $\|Bx\|^2\le\sum_{i=1}^d(\sum_{j=1}^d|b_{ij}|)^2\|x\|^2$. Thus its operator norm is defined by the unit-ball supremum in [[def-operator-norm]]. For $B,C\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ and $\|x\|\le1$, that definition and the bound $\|By\|\le\|B\|\|y\|$ give $\|BCx\|\le\|B\|\|Cx\|\le\|B\|\|C\|$; taking the supremum over the unit ball proves $\|BC\|\le\|B\|\|C\|$. Since $d\ge1$, the standard unit ball contains a unit vector and $\|I_d\|=1$. Hence $\|A^0\|=1$, while induction using submultiplicativity gives $\|A^k\|\le\|A\|^k$ for every $k\ge1$. The terms are therefore dominated by the convergent scalar exponential series $\sum_{k\ge0}(|z|\|A\|)^k/k!$; the displayed series converges absolutely in operator norm. The scalar exponential uses the convention $\exp z=\sum_{k\ge0}z^k/k!$.

This algorithm returns that finite record unchanged and does not certify its residual claims.

The algorithm takes $(d,b,N,\hbar,\omega,(H_k)_{|k|\le b},\tau,S_\tau)$ and returns a matrix $K_N$ and the eigensolver's output record:

1. Order the Fourier indices as $-N,-N+1,\ldots,N$ and allocate a $(2N+1)d$ by $(2N+1)d$ block matrix.

2. For each ordered pair $n,m\in\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, assign the $d$ by $d$ block
$$ (K_N)_{nm}:=H_{n-m}+n\hbar\omega\,\delta_{nm}I_d,$$
where $\delta_{nm}=1$ if $n=m$ and $0$ otherwise.

3. Call $S_\tau(K_N)$ once and return $(K_N,S_\tau(K_N))$.

The block assembly always terminates after $(2N+1)^2$ block assignments; the complete procedure terminates by the assumed totality of $S_\tau$. statement.proposed:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $b,N\ge0$, and real numbers $\hbar>0$, $\omega>0$, and $\tau>0$. Let $H_k\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ for $-b\le k\le b$ satisfy $H_{-k}=H_k^*$; set $H_k=0$ when $|k|>b$. Thus $H(t)=\sum_{k=-b}^{b}H_ke^{ik\omega t}$ is a finite Fourier polynomial with period $T=2\pi/\omega$. Put $q=(2N+1)d$. Let $S_\tau$ be a caller-supplied total classical routine on $\{M\in M_q(\mathbb C):M=M^*\}$ whose declared interface, on input $M$, returns real numbers $\widetilde\lambda_1,\ldots,\widetilde\lambda_q$, an orthonormal basis $x_1,\ldots,x_q$ of standard $\mathbb C^q$, and residuals $r_j=\|Mx_j-\widetilde\lambda_jx_j\|\le\tau$ for $1\le j\le q$. This algorithm returns that finite record unchanged and does not independently certify its residual claims.

The algorithm takes $(d,b,N,\hbar,\omega,(H_k)_{|k|\le b},\tau,S_\tau)$ and returns a matrix $K_N$ and the eigensolver's output record:

1. Order the Fourier indices as $-N,-N+1,\ldots,N$ and allocate a $(2N+1)d$ by $(2N+1)d$ block matrix.

2. For each ordered pair $n,m\in\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, assign the $d$ by $d$ block
$$ (K_N)_{nm}:=H_{n-m}+n\hbar\omega\,\delta_{nm}I_d,$$
where $\delta_{nm}=1$ if $n=m$ and $0$ otherwise.

3. Set $R:=S_\tau(K_N)$ by one call, then return $(K_N,R)$.

**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. The mode operators are dimensionless and on the finite-particle core satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

The assigned dipole interaction core expression is $V_{\mathrm{dip}}=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_jD_j\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)$ in the ordered space $\mathcal H_A\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$; each summand has units joules and acts on the finite-particle core. This clause assigns the finite matrix expression only. It does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generate an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_A\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h))$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a state $\rho$, the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $Q_j$ is the self-adjoint quadrature fixed by [[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on the finite-particle core equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately; the optional finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment has the exact scope of the finite open-system postulate and implies no reservoir limit.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.
statement.proposed:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

statement.before: Assume the finite-mode light–matter assignment and choose one of its modes. Let $\rho$ be a density operator (a positive trace-class operator of trace one) on that mode's one-mode Fock space. Let $\Pi_n:=|n\rangle\langle n|$ be the ideal number-count PVM on that mode, with probabilities $p_n:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_n)$. Suppose $\bar n:=\sum_{n\ge0}np_n$ is finite and strictly positive, and $m_2:=\sum_{n\ge0}n(n-1)p_n$ is finite. Define the model's equal-time second factorial statistic by $g^{(2)}(0;\rho):=m_2/\bar n^2$. This is the number-distribution form of the ideal single-mode normally ordered factorial count statistic; the unambiguous numerator used here is the finite sum $m_2$ defined above. This definition uses the ideal counting outcome model only; it asserts no time-resolved photocurrent law, empirical detection, or detector realization.
statement.proposed: Specialize the finite-mode assignment to $M=1$, identify the coordinate vector $(z)\in\mathbb C^1$ with its single component $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$ for this one-mode Fock space. Write $|n\rangle$ for the occupation vector with $n$ quanta in its unique mode. Let $\rho$ be a density operator (a positive trace-class operator of trace one) on $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. Let $\Pi_n:=|n\rangle\langle n|$ be the ideal number-count PVM, with probabilities $p_n:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_n)$. Suppose $\bar n:=\sum_{n\ge0}np_n$ is finite and strictly positive, and $m_2:=\sum_{n\ge0}n(n-1)p_n$ is finite. Define the model's equal-time second factorial statistic by $g^{(2)}(0;\rho):=m_2/\bar n^2$. On finite-particle number vectors the one-mode maps satisfy $a|0\rangle=0$, $a|n\rangle=\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$ for $n\ge1$, and $a^*|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}|n+1\rangle$ for $n\ge0$. Normal ordering here means placing creation maps to the left of annihilation maps; these actions give $a^*a^*aa|n\rangle=n(n-1)|n\rangle$ for $n\ge0$. Thus $m_2$ is the corresponding number-basis factorial moment, defined here directly by its probability sum rather than by an unqualified expectation of an unbounded operator product. This uses only the ideal counting model; it asserts no time-resolved photocurrent law, empirical detection, or detector realization.

statement.before:
Assume the finite-mode assignment with two modes and its ideal number PVM. Let $t,r\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless amplitudes with $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$, and fix the complete unitary mode matrix $C=\begin{pmatrix}t&-\overline r\\r&\overline t\end{pmatrix}$. Use the state-action convention that the passive unitary $U_C$ satisfies $U_C\Omega=\Omega$, $U_Ca_1^*U_C^*=t a_1^*+r a_2^*$, and $U_Ca_2^*U_C^*=-\overline r\,a_1^*+\overline t\,a_2^*$ on the finite-particle core. Put $\eta:=|t|^2$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and $0\le k\le n$, write $\binom nk:=n!/(k!(n-k)!)$. For input $|n,0\rangle$ and $0<\eta<1$, the joint output count law is
$$\mathbb P(k,\ell)=\begin{cases}\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k},&\ell=n-k,\ 0\le k\le n,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
At $\eta=0$ and $\eta=1$ the joint laws are respectively point masses at $(0,n)$ and $(n,0)$. Thus the first output count is binomial with parameters $(n,\eta)$. For a dimensionless coherent input $|\alpha,0\rangle$ with $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$, the output state is $|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$.

Assume the finite-mode assignment with two modes and its ideal number PVM, with AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the implementer and completed Fock/tensor suppliers. Write $\mathcal F^{(2)}=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^2)$ in the ordered mode basis $(1,0),(0,1)$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. The mode-factorization map is the unitary $\mathcal J:\mathcal F^{(2)}\to\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$ determined by $\mathcal J|m,n\rangle=|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$. Here $\widehat\otimes$ is the completed Hilbert tensor product, and the one-mode occupation vectors and their products use the same vacuum and mode order. Its unitary extension is proved below. Let $t,r\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless amplitudes with $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$, and fix the complete unitary mode matrix $C=\begin{pmatrix}t&-\overline r\\r&\overline t\end{pmatrix}$. Use the state-action convention that the passive unitary $U_C$ satisfies $U_C\Omega=\Omega$, $U_Ca_1^*U_C^*=t a_1^*+r a_2^*$, and $U_Ca_2^*U_C^*=-\overline r\,a_1^*+\overline t\,a_2^*$ on the finite-particle core. Put $\eta:=|t|^2$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and $0\le k\le n$, write $\binom nk:=n!/(k!(n-k)!)$. For input $|n,0\rangle$ and $0<\eta<1$, the joint output count law is
$$\mathbb P(k,\ell)=\begin{cases}\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k},&\ell=n-k,\ 0\le k\le n,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
At $\eta=0$ and $\eta=1$ the joint laws are respectively point masses at $(0,n)$ and $(n,0)$. Thus the first output count is binomial with parameters $(n,\eta)$. For a dimensionless coherent input $|\alpha,0\rangle$ with $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$, define $|\alpha,0\rangle=\mathcal J^*(|\alpha\rangle\otimes|0\rangle)$, equivalently $e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n,0\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$. The output state under this fixed mode factorization is $\mathcal J U_C|\alpha,0\rangle=|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$; on $\mathcal F^{(2)}$ it is $\mathcal J^*(|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle)$.

statement.before:
Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the assigned finite-mode model, a single input mode and a second mode prepared independently in vacuum $|0\rangle\langle0|$. For $0\le\eta\le1$, choose the passive unitary $U_\eta$ of the two-mode beam-splitter model with $t=\sqrt\eta$ and $r=\sqrt{1-\eta}$. For every trace-class operator $\rho$ on the one-mode Fock space, define
$$\Phi_\eta(\rho):=\operatorname{Tr}_2\!\left(U_\eta(\rho\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|)U_\eta^*\right),$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ is the trace-class partial trace over the environment mode. Here CPTP means complex-linear, trace-preserving, and positive after every finite-dimensional ancilla amplification on trace-class operators. The map $\Phi_\eta$ is CPTP. For $0<\eta<1$ and an input number state $|n\rangle$, its output state is
$$\Phi_\eta(|n\rangle\langle n|)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k}|k\rangle\langle k|,$$
so ideal number detection has the binomial-thinning law. At $\eta=0$ this number input is mapped to vacuum, and at $\eta=1$ it is unchanged. For a coherent input $|\alpha\rangle$, its output is $|\sqrt\eta\,\alpha\rangle\langle\sqrt\eta\,\alpha|$ for every $0\le\eta\le1$. On arbitrary input states, $\Phi_0$ maps to vacuum and $\Phi_1$ is the identity.
statement.proposed:
Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the assigned finite-mode model, one input mode and a second mode prepared independently in vacuum $|0\rangle\langle0|$. For a bounded operator, its spectrum $\sigma(B)$ is the set of complex $z$ for which $B-zI$ has no bounded two-sided inverse. Let $E_B$ be the regular projection-valued measure on the Borel subsets of $\sigma(B)$ satisfying $B=\int_{\sigma(B)}b\,dE_B(b)$. A projection-valued measure is a countably additive measure whose values are orthogonal projections and whose value on the whole space is $I$. $$A=\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda),\qquad D(A)=\left\{u\in H:\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda^2\,d\langle E_A(\lambda)u,u\rangle<\infty\right\}.$$

For every bounded Borel function $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$, the integral $f(A):=\int f\,dE_A$ is bounded and satisfies $\|f(A)\|\le\sup_{\lambda\ge0}|f(\lambda)|$. The condition $E_B(\{0\})=0$ does not assert that $0\notin\sigma(B)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Here self-adjoint means equality with the Hilbert-space adjoint, including equality of domains. A projection-valued measure (PVM) on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ is a map $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(H)$ such that every $E(S)$ is a bounded orthogonal projection ($E(S)^2=E(S)=E(S)^*$), $E(\varnothing)=0$, $E(X)=I$, $E(S\cap T)=E(S)E(T)$, and $E(\bigcup_n S_n)u=\sum_nE(S_n)u$ in norm for each disjoint sequence $(S_n)$ and each $u\in H$. On a locally compact Hausdorff Borel space, such a PVM is regular when each finite scalar measure $\mu_u(S):=\langle E(S)u,u\rangle$ is inner regular on Borel sets and outer regular by open supersets. Then $I+A:D(A)\to H$ is bijective. Its inverse $B:=(I+A)^{-1}$ is a bounded positive (meaning $\langle Bx,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x\in H$) self-adjoint injection with $\|B\|\le1$ and dense range $D(A)$. For a bounded operator, its spectrum $\sigma(B)$ is the set of complex $z$ for which $B-zI$ has no bounded two-sided inverse. Let $E_B$ be the regular spectral PVM on the Borel subsets of the nonempty compact set $\sigma(B)$ satisfying $B=\int_{\sigma(B)}b\,dE_B(b)$. Then $\sigma(B)\subseteq[0,1]$ and $E_B(\{0\})=0$. Define $\phi(b)=b^{-1}-1$ for $b\in\sigma(B)\setminus\{0\}$ and, for every Borel $S\subseteq[0,\infty)$, define

$$E_A(S):=E_B(\{b\in\sigma(B)\setminus\{0\}:\phi(b)\in S\}).$$

This is a PVM on the Borel subsets of $[0,\infty)$. For each $u\in H$ put $\mu_u(S):=\langle E_A(S)u,u\rangle$. The unbounded integral $\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)$ denotes the operator $T_A$ with domain

$$D(T_A):=\left\{u\in H:\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda^2\,d\mu_u(\lambda)<\infty\right\}$$

and action

$$T_Au:=\lim_{N\to\infty}\Phi_{E_A}(\lambda\mathbf1_{[0,N]})(u),$$

where $\Phi_{E_A}(g)$ is the bounded Borel PVM integral of $g$. Then $A=T_A$ and hence

$$A=\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda),\qquad D(A)=\left\{u\in H:\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda^2\,d\langle E_A(\lambda)u,u\rangle<\infty\right\}.$$

For every bounded Borel function $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$, $f(A):=\Phi_{E_A}(f)$ is bounded, satisfies $\|f(A)\|\le\sup_{\lambda\ge0}|f(\lambda)|$, and obeys $\|f(A)u\|^2=\int|f|^2\,d\mu_u$. The condition $E_B(\{0\})=0$ does not assert that $0\notin\sigma(B)$.

Fix a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a finite index set $A$ with real basis $\{t^a\}_{a\in A}$, and a finite species index set $I$. Let $\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}:=\mathfrak g\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ be the complexification of [[def-complexification-of-a-real-lie-algebra]], with complex scalar multiplication on the second tensor factor and the complex-bilinear bracket specified on pure tensors by $[X\otimes z,Y\otimes w]=[X,Y]\otimes zw$ for $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$ and $z,w\in\mathbb C$. Identify $X\in\mathfrak g$ with its canonical real embedding $X\otimes1$; in particular $t^a$ in a representation argument means $t^a\otimes1$. For each $i\in I$, let $V_i$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let $\rho_i:\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_i)$ be a complex-linear Lie-algebra representation, so $\rho_i([U,V])=\rho_i(U)\rho_i(V)-\rho_i(V)\rho_i(U)$. Attach the bookkeeping label $\chi_i=L$ to each species. In this interface, a “left-handed Weyl species” means exactly the data $(V_i,\rho_i,\chi_i=L)$; the label is not a spinor field or a chirality operator. No spacetime manifold, spinor bundle or field, kinetic operator or action, integration of $\rho_i$ to a gauge group, regulator, effective action, or gauge-variation map is constructed or assumed.

Set $T^a_{R_i}:=\rho_i(t^a)$ and define $\{A,B\}:=AB+BA$ for endomorphisms of $V_i$. The algebraic cubic representation coefficient is
$$d^{abc}=\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{tr}_{V_i}\!\left(T^a_{R_i}\{T^b_{R_i},T^c_{R_i}\}\right)\in\mathbb C.$$
The basis and generator normalization are fixed as part of the data. No factor $1/2$ is included in the anticommutator. If $T^{(b}T^{c)}=(T^bT^c+T^cT^b)/2$, then $d^{abc}$ is twice $\sum_i\operatorname{tr}_{V_i}(T^a_{R_i}T^{(b}_{R_i}T^{c)}_{R_i})$. Cancellation of this coefficient means $d^{abc}=0$ for every basis triple in this convention. These are representation traces only; calling them anomaly coefficients in a physical model requires an additional theorem.

Define the separate linear representation coefficient by
$$\ell^a=\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{tr}_{V_i}(T^a_{R_i})\in\mathbb C.$$
For one-dimensional representation spaces of a one-dimensional Abelian Lie algebra with fixed generator $t$ and $\rho_i(t)=q_i\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C}$, this gives $\ell=\sum_iq_i$. The coefficient $\ell^a$ is recorded separately because a later mixed gauge-gravitational analysis needs its own representation data. Such an analysis must specify its spacetime and gauge connections, curvature conventions, and index polynomial; no mixed-anomaly formula is asserted by this interface.

The only local BRST obstruction statement recorded here is a separate formal result for the specific Abelian jet complex used by the mathematical supplier, not a BRST construction for the general Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ above. In the convention of `def-qftx-brst-relative-local-cohomology`, a compactly supported local horizontal $p$-form is a finite sum of $f_{i_1\ldots i_p}(x,z)\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_p}$, with each coefficient smooth and compactly supported in $x\in\mathbb R^4$ and polynomial in finitely many field-jet coordinates $z^i_\alpha$; $i$ indexes the field and ghost generators and $\alpha$ their derivative multi-indices. Its total derivative is $D_\mu=\partial/\partial x^\mu+\sum_{i,\alpha}z^i_{\alpha+e_\mu}\partial_L/\partial z^i_\alpha$, where $e_\mu$ is the unit multi-index and $\partial_L$ is the left graded derivative; $d_H=dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu$. The differential $s$ is the odd ghost-number-one Abelian derivation fixed by `def-qftx-abelian-local-brst`, with $sa_\mu=\partial_\mu c_{\mathrm{gh}}$, $sc_{\mathrm{gh}}=0$, $s\bar c=B$, $sB=0$, and $s\psi=igc_{\mathrm{gh}}\psi$, extended by the graded Leibniz rule and commutation with spacetime derivatives; $a_\mu,\psi,B$ are even, $c_{\mathrm{gh}},\bar c$ are odd, and their ghost numbers are $0,0,0,1,-1$, respectively. This source also fixes $s^2=d_H^2=0$ and $sd_H+d_Hs=0$, with nilpotence of $s$ established by `lem-qftx-brst-nilpotence-doublets`. For each $n$, $\mathcal K_n^{r,p}$ is an $s,d_H$-stable subcomplex of these forms, and the relative class is the quotient
$$H^{1,4}(s|d_H;\mathcal K_n)=\frac{\{a_4\in\mathcal K_n^{1,4}:s a_4+d_Ha_3=0\text{ for some }a_3\in\mathcal K_n^{2,3}\}}{\{s b_4+d_Hc_3:b_4\in\mathcal K_n^{0,4},\ c_3\in\mathcal K_n^{1,3}\}}.$$
The direct supplier `prop-qftx-anomaly-obstruction` is a draft proposition with a supplied conditional proof. Its scalar construction premise is the draft theorem `thm-qftx-scalar-eg-induction`: under the Axiom of Choice (every family of nonempty sets has a choice function) and Countable Choice (every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function), and for admissible flat scalar free data and a local scalar polynomial class as defined by `def-qftx-local-time-ordered-system`, that theorem asserts existence of symmetric multilinear time-ordered maps satisfying its contract at every finite order, with finite graph scaling bounds and local extension ambiguities. It asserts no convergence, adiabatic limit, positivity, or Ward identity. The exact statement of `prop-qftx-anomaly-obstruction` assumes those data and a time-ordering scheme satisfying that theorem. For each ghost number $r$, define the local-functional quotient $\mathscr F_n^r:=\mathcal K_n^{r,4}/d_H\mathcal K_n^{r,3}$ and its formal series module $\mathscr F_n^r\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, where $\hbar$ is a formal indeterminate. For some $n\ge1$, it further assumes an odd formal ghost-number-one operator $\mathcal W_\hbar=s+\sum_{j\ge1}\hbar^j\mathcal W_j$ on this module, $\mathcal W_\hbar^2=0$, and an element $X\in\mathscr F_n^0\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ with $\mathcal W_\hbar X=\hbar^n\mathcal A+O(\hbar^{n+1})$, where $O(\hbar^{n+1})$ denotes terms of formal degree at least $n+1$, all lower coefficients vanish, and $\mathcal A=[a_4]_{\mathscr F_n}$ for compactly supported $a_4\in\mathcal K_n^{1,4}$. It requires $\mathcal K_n^{0,4}$ to be exactly the admissible local counterterm densities. Under these hypotheses, that proposition states that $s a_4$ is $d_H$-exact and that shifting $X$ by $-\hbar^n[b_4]_{\mathscr F_n}$, for $b_4\in\mathcal K_n^{0,4}$, cancels the order-$n$ breaking exactly when $[a_4]_{s|d_H}=0$. This is used only in the stated conditional form: it does not establish that the hypotheses hold for the representation data above or construct a physical effective action, and it does not prove a quantum action principle.

Accordingly, this interface asserts no physical anomaly-cancellation criterion from $d^{abc}$. A later physical theorem must specify its spacetime, field space, action, regulator and renormalized effective-action map, and the map that assigns a local gauge-variation density to that data. It must then prove the relation of that density to an explicitly specified local BRST cohomology class and invariant six-form polynomial, with mixed gauge-gravitational coefficients and loop-order hypotheses stated separately. No conclusion about transformations outside the identity component of a separately specified full gauge-transformation group follows from this infinitesimal representation tensor. Vanishing $d^{abc}$ alone proves neither a nonperturbative gauge theory nor the absence of failures under such transformations.

Assume the hypotheses and notation of [[def-qftx-heavy-gaussian-data]]. Let $E\ge0$ be an energy and let $P_E:=E_A([0,E^2])$ be the spectral projection of $A$. For $J=P_EJ\in H$ and an integer $N\ge0$, define
$$S_NJ:=M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-A/M^2)^rJ,$$
which is well-defined since $J$ has bounded spectral support. Put $R_NJ:=K^{-1}J-S_NJ$. Then
$$\|R_NJ\|\le M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}\|J\|,$$
and
$$\left|\Delta S_{\mathrm{eff}}(J)+\tfrac12\langle J,S_NJ\rangle\right| =\tfrac12|\langle J,R_NJ\rangle| \le \frac{\|J\|^2}{2M^2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}.$$
Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$: $A$ has units of mass squared, $E,M$ have mass units, and $E^2/M^2$ is dimensionless. Under the source normalization of [[def-qftx-heavy-gaussian-data]], $\|J\|^2/M^2$ and the action remainder are dimensionless. These are exact conditional bounds for every $E\ge0$; the truncation is small/useful when $E<M$. No claim is made for unrestricted sources or arbitrary interacting matching.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, let $C_1,C_2$ be real symmetric positive-semidefinite $d\times d$ covariance matrices, and let $f:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty]$ be Borel. With $T_C$ as in [[def-qftx-finite-gaussian-shell-transform]],
$$T_{C_2}(T_{C_1}f)(x)=T_{C_1+C_2}f(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d),$$
as an equality in $[0,\infty]$. In particular, for every finite nonnegative Borel potential $V$,
$$\exp[-(V_{C_1})_{C_2}(x)]=\exp[-V_{C_1+C_2}(x)].$$
The Gaussian measures are normalized probabilities, so no determinant/vacuum constant appears; changing to unnormalized Gaussian weights requires carrying their normalization factors. This is an exact finite-regulator semigroup identity. Differentiating it to obtain a Polchinski-type flow is not asserted and would require a differentiable covariance path and separate differentiability/integrability hypotheses.

Assume AC. Let $H=L^2(\mathbb R,dp;\mathbb C)$ with pairing $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_\mathbb R u(p)\overline{v(p)}\,dp$, let
$$A=M_{p^2},\qquad D(A)=\{u\in H:p^2u\in H\},$$
and fix $M>0$, $0\le E<M$, and $N\in\mathbb N_0$. This is the no-band case for the estimate in [[thm-qftx-heavy-derivative-bound]]: the polynomial approximation to $(M^2+p^2)^{-1}$ has multiplier remainder
$$r_N(p^2)=M^{-2}\frac{(-p^2/M^2)^{N+1}}{1+p^2/M^2}.$$
Let $r_N(A)$ denote multiplication by $r_N(p^2)$ on its maximal $L^2$ domain. There is a unit vector $u\in\bigcap_{r=0}^{N+1}D(A^r)$ for which
$$\|r_N(A)u\|>M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}.$$
Thus the derivative estimate's low-energy factor cannot hold uniformly on the full momentum spectrum. Here $p,M,E$ have mass units, $dp$ has mass units, $A$ has mass-squared units, and $\hbar=c=1$. This is a mathematical counterexample to removing the spectral-band hypothesis; it is not a measured physical failure.
statement.proposed:
Assume AC. Let $dp$ denote Lebesgue measure on the momentum line $\mathbb R$, and let $H=L^2(\mathbb R,dp;\mathbb C)$ be the space of equivalence classes modulo Lebesgue-a.e. equality of complex measurable functions $u$ satisfying $\int_\mathbb R|u(p)|^2\,dp<\infty$, with pairing $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_\mathbb R u(p)\overline{v(p)}\,dp$, linear in its first variable, and induced norm $\|u\|_2=(\int_\mathbb R|u(p)|^2\,dp)^{1/2}$. Define the multiplication operator $A$ by
$$A=M_{p^2},\qquad D(A)=\{u\in H:p^2u\in H\},$$
with $(Au)(p)=p^2u(p)$ almost everywhere. For each integer $r\ge1$, let $A^r$ be multiplication by $p^{2r}$ on $D(A^r):=\{u\in H:p^{2r}u\in H\}$; set $A^0=I$ with $D(A^0)=H$. Fix $M>0$, $0\le E<M$, and let $N$ be a nonnegative integer. This is the no-band case for the low-energy remainder estimate: the polynomial approximation to $(M^2+p^2)^{-1}$ has multiplier remainder
$$r_N(p^2)=M^{-2}\frac{(-p^2/M^2)^{N+1}}{1+p^2/M^2}.$$
Let $r_N(A)$ denote multiplication by $r_N(p^2)$ on the maximal domain $D(r_N(A)):=\{u\in H:r_N(p^2)u\in H\}$. There is a unit vector $u\in\bigcap_{r=0}^{N+1}D(A^r)$ for which
$$\|r_N(A)u\|>M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}.$$
Thus the low-energy factor in the remainder estimate cannot hold uniformly on the full momentum spectrum. Here $p,M,E$ have mass units, $dp$ has mass units, $A$ has mass-squared units, and $\hbar=c=1$. This is a mathematical counterexample to removing the spectral-band hypothesis; it is not a measured physical failure.

$Q_i\in\mathbb R$ (physical charge $eQ_i$ in C), and an orientation
$\eta_i\in\{-1,1\}$, where $-1$
denotes an incoming leg and $+1$ an outgoing leg. Assume charge balance
$\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i=0$. Write $h=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ and
$h(a,b)=a^0b^0-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$.

$$p_i=E_i(1,v_i),\qquad q=\hbar\nu(1,n),\qquad J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{p_i}{h(p_i,q)},\qquad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}.$$
Here $\nu>0$ is angular frequency in s$^{-1}$ and $\hbar\nu$ is photon
energy in J. The data make $h(p_i,q)=E_i\hbar\nu(1-v_i\cdot n)>0$ and
$J(q)=K(n)/(\hbar\nu)$. The balance condition gives
$h(J(q),q)=0$; this is the conservation convention for this prescribed
eikonal current in the model.

Let $A\subseteq S^2$ be a Borel angular acceptance region and let $d\Omega$
be Euclidean chart surface measure. Write $K(n)=(K^0(n),\mathbf K(n))$ and
define $K_\perp(n)=(I_3-nn^T)\mathbf K(n)$, where $I_3$ is the $3\times3$
identity matrix, and
$$b(n)=\mathbf1_A(n)\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad C=\int_{S^2}|b(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\ge0.$$
Thus $b$ and $C$ are dimensionless.

$\nu(\mathbf k)=c|\mathbf k|$ in s$^{-1}$. The one-particle coherent
displacement is the transverse mode function
$$f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}(\mathbf k)= \mathbf1_{\{\varepsilon<\nu(\mathbf k)<\Lambda\}}|\mathbf k|^{-3/2} {}\times b\!\left(\frac{\mathbf k}{|\mathbf k|}\right) \quad(\mathbf k\ne0), \qquad f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}(0)=0.$$

$L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$; the associated free one-photon
energy is $\hbar\nu(\mathbf k)=\hbar c|\mathbf k|$ in J. Define its
exponential vector and normalized coherent vector by
$$\epsilon(f)=\bigoplus_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{\otimes_s m}}{\sqrt{m!}}, \qquad \Psi_{\varepsilon,\Lambda} =\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}\|^2}{2}\right) \epsilon(f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}),$$

$B_1,\ldots,B_r$ of $(\varepsilon,\Lambda)$ into disjoint Borel intervals,

$H_j=\{u\in\mathcal H_T:u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ a.e. unless }\nu(\mathbf k)\in B_j\}$.

$(\varepsilon,\Delta)$ and the resolved band $[\Delta,\Lambda)$. The
threshold frequency is assigned to the resolved band; its exact assignment
does not change any $L^2$ vector or probability because a single frequency
has zero one-particle measure.

with signature $(+,-,-,-)$ used in this model.

For $n\in S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and angular frequency
$\nu>0$ in s$^{-1}$, with associated model photon energy $\hbar\nu$ in J,
put $p_i=E_i(1,v_i)$ and $q=\hbar\nu(1,n)$ in $\mathbb R^4$. On
$$\mathscr Q=\{\hbar\nu(1,n):\nu>0,\ n\in S^2\}\subset\mathbb R^4,$$
define the prescribed current $J:\mathscr Q\to\mathbb R^4$ and angular

$$J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{p_i}{h(p_i,q)},\qquad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}.$$

scattering-amplitude factorization or approximation is asserted.

$S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ is a compact embedded smooth hypersurface, and

injective $C^1$ chart cover $X_j:V_j\to S^2$, where each $V_j$ is open in
$\mathbb R^2$, with $C^1$ coordinate
transitions and a subordinate ambient partition of unity $\chi_j$ whose supports are compactly
contained in the chart neighborhoods, its integral on a nonnegative Borel

$$\int_{S^2}F\,d\Omega=\sum_j\int_{V_j}(\chi_jF)(X_j(y))\sqrt{\det(DX_j(y)^TDX_j(y))}\,dy.$$
This is the chart-independent induced surface integral. Write
$K(n)=(K^0(n),\mathbf K(n))$ and define
$K_\perp(n)=(I_3-nn^T)\mathbf K(n)$, where $I_3$ is the $3\times3$
identity matrix. Put
$$b_0(n)=\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad b(n)=\mathbf1_A(n)b_0(n),\qquad C=\int_{S^2}|b(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$

$$x\cdot y=\sum_{j=1}^3x_jy_j\quad(x,y\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^3a_jb_j\quad(a,b\in\mathbb C^3),$$

put $\widehat{\mathbf k}=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$
and $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\widehat{\mathbf k}\widehat{\mathbf k}^{T}$, the

$\mathbf k$; assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$. Its multiplier is an
orthogonal projection on $\mathcal H$, so its range is closed. The transverse

$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}=\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for a.e. }\mathbf k\ne0\},$$

$P_{s,m}(f^{\otimes m})=f^{\otimes m}$ for $m\ge1$; write this tensor as

$$g_K^{(2)}(0)=\frac{\mathbb E[K(K-1)]}{(\mathbb E K)^2}=\frac{F_2}{\mu^2}=g_N^{(2)}(0).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with boundary, $\mathfrak g$ a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra with invariant nondegenerate symmetric pairing, and $A\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak g)$ a smooth connection in a fixed trivialization. For an arbitrary smooth variation $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak g)$, the Chern–Simons first variation is

$$\delta\operatorname{CS}_A(\alpha)=2\int_M\langle\alpha\wedge F_A\rangle-\int_{\partial M}\langle A\wedge\alpha\rangle,$$

where $\partial M$ has the outward-normal-first orientation. Thus the boundary term is part of the variation; the bulk Euler equation is $F_A=0$ when variations are compactly supported in $\operatorname{int}M$ (or when boundary data make the boundary variation vanish). For $B\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak g)$ the BF action has first variation

$$\delta\operatorname{BF}_{(B,A)}(\beta,\alpha)=\int_M\langle\beta\wedge F_A\rangle+\int_M\langle\alpha\wedge D_AB\rangle-\int_{\partial M}\langle B\wedge\alpha\rangle,$$

so interior-compact variations give the equations $F_A=0$ and $D_AB=0$. No boundary condition is imposed by these bulk equations.

For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ fixed, the boundary potential current of $\lambda\operatorname{CS}$ is $\theta_A(\alpha)=-\lambda\langle A\wedge\alpha\rangle$. On a compact oriented smooth surface $\Sigma$ (with smooth boundary allowed), put $\mathcal A_\Sigma=\Omega^1(\Sigma;\mathfrak g)$ and identify each tangent space with $\Omega^1(\Sigma;\mathfrak g)$. For $a\in\mathcal A_\Sigma$ define $\Theta_\Sigma|_a(\alpha)=\int_\Sigma\theta_a(\alpha)$, and let $\Omega_\Sigma=d_{\mathcal A_\Sigma}\Theta_\Sigma$. The restriction to the flat-connection solution space, wherever it is smooth, is the possibly degenerate presymplectic form. Explicitly, on tangent vectors $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ it is the constant closed form

$$\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=-2\lambda\int_\Sigma\langle\alpha_1\wedge\alpha_2\rangle.$$

At a flat connection $a$ ($F_a=0$), tangent variations $\alpha$ to the flat-connection equations satisfy $D_a\alpha=0$. For an infinitesimal gauge parameter $\epsilon\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\mathfrak g)$, the gauge direction is $D_a\epsilon$ and

$$\Omega_\Sigma(D_a\epsilon,\alpha)=-2\lambda\int_{\partial\Sigma}\langle\epsilon,\alpha\rangle.$$

Consequently gauge parameters vanishing on $\partial\Sigma$ generate null directions on the linearized flat locus. If $\epsilon$ is field-independent, the displayed boundary variation is $\delta Q_\epsilon$ for $Q_\epsilon(a)=-2\lambda\int_{\partial\Sigma}\langle\epsilon,a\rangle$. Nonzero boundary parameters need not be null and can carry such charges when the boundary conditions permit them; no charge algebra or integrability assertion for field-dependent parameters is made.

Fix $d\ge1$. A locally finite counting measure on $\mathbb R^d$ is a measure of the form $\xi=\sum_{r\in I}\delta_{x_r}$, where $I$ is finite or countable, repetitions among the points $x_r\in\mathbb R^d$ are allowed, and every compact set contains only finitely many listed points, counting repetitions. The empty sum is allowed and is the zero measure. For a Borel set $B$, $\xi(B)$ is the number of listed points in $B$, with multiplicity. Write $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$ for the set of these measures. For $x\in\mathbb R^d$, the point mass $\delta_x$ assigns mass $1$ to a Borel set containing $x$ and mass $0$ otherwise.

The vague topology on $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lf}}(\mathbb R^d)$ is the coarsest topology for which $\xi\mapsto\int f\,d\xi$ is continuous for every nonnegative continuous compactly supported function $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$. Thus $\xi_n\to_{\mathrm v}\xi$ exactly when $\int f\,d\xi_n\to\int f\,d\xi$ for every such $f$.

Here a random locally finite counting measure means a measurable random element for which $\Xi_n(B)$ is a random variable for every bounded Borel set $B$. If $(\Xi_n)$ is a sequence of such measures on a common probability space and $K$ is compact, its local counts are uniformly integrable on $K$ when

$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_n\mathbb E\!\left[\Xi_n(K)\mathbf1_{\{\Xi_n(K)>R\}}\right]=0.$$

This is the count-tail condition used when an argument needs control of unbounded observables supported in $K$. The definition asserts no convergence of expectations without the exact test-function, support, and tail hypotheses of the result being applied.

A locally finite counting measure on $\mathbb R^d$ is a measure of the form $\xi=\sum_{r\in I}\delta_{x_r}$, where $I$ is finite or countable, repetitions among the points $x_r\in\mathbb R^d$ are allowed, and every compact set contains only finitely many listed points, counting repetitions. statement.proposed:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T\ge0$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, and let $(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be an increasing family of sub-$\sigma$-algebras of $\mathcal F$. Let $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a family of real random variables such that each $M_t$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable, $\mathbb E[M_t^2]<\infty$, $M_0=0$, and $\mathbb E[M_t\mid\mathcal F_s]=M_s$ almost surely for every $0\le s\le t\le T$. Suppose it has càdlàg paths almost surely, meaning there is a measurable event $\Omega_0\in\mathcal F$ with $\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1$ such that, for every $\omega\in\Omega_0$, the path $t\mapsto M_t(\omega)$ is right-continuous on $[0,T)$ and has a finite left limit at every $t\in(0,T]$. Define
$$
D_T=\bigcup_{n\ge0}\{kT/2^n:0\le k\le2^n\},\qquad S_T=\sup_{t\in D_T}|M_t|.
$$
Then $S_T$ is measurable and agrees with the pathwise supremum $\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t|$ on $\Omega_0$, and
$$
\mathbb E[S_T^2]\le4\,\mathbb E[|M_T|^2].
$$

statement.before:
An abstract polymer model consists of a countable set $\Gamma$, a reflexive symmetric relation $\sim$ on $\Gamma$, and an activity function $z:\Gamma\to\mathbb C$. Its elements are called polymers, and $\gamma\sim\eta$ means that the two polymers are incompatible. A subset $X\subseteq\Gamma$ is compatible when no two distinct elements of $X$ are related by $\sim$. For each finite $V\subseteq\Gamma$, define the finite-volume partition polynomial

$$Z_V(z):=\sum_{\substack{X\subseteq V\\X\text{ compatible}}}\ \prod_{\gamma\in X}z_\gamma,$$

where the empty subset contributes $1$.

For $n\geq1$ and an ordered tuple $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n)\in\Gamma^n$, let $\mathcal C_n$ be the finite set of connected simple graphs with vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, put $f_{ij}:=-\mathbf 1_{\{\gamma_i\sim\gamma_j\}}$, and define the connected coefficient

$$U_n(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_{ij}.$$

For $n=1$, $\mathcal C_1$ contains the one-vertex graph and the empty edge product equals $1$. These are finite polynomial and coefficient definitions; they assert no convergence.
statement.proposed:
An abstract polymer model consists of an at most countable set $\Gamma$ (finite or in bijection with $\mathbb N$), a reflexive symmetric relation $\sim$ on $\Gamma$ (so $\gamma\sim\gamma$ and $\gamma\sim\eta$ implies $\eta\sim\gamma$), and an activity function $z:\Gamma\to\mathbb C$. Its elements are called polymers, and $\gamma\sim\eta$ means that the two polymers are incompatible. A subset $X\subseteq\Gamma$ is compatible when no two distinct elements of $X$ are related by $\sim$. For real and natural summands, finite-index sums and products are enumeration-independent. For complex summands, define a finite sum or product by any enumeration and repeated addition or multiplication in $\mathbb C$; associativity and commutativity make the result independent of the enumeration. The empty sum is $0$ and the empty product is $1$. For each finite $V\subseteq\Gamma$, define the finite-volume partition polynomial

$$Z_V(z):=\sum_{\substack{X\subseteq V\\X\text{ compatible}}}\ \prod_{\gamma\in X}z_\gamma,$$

where the empty subset contributes $1$.

Write $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $\binom{[n]}2:=\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in[n],\ i\ne j\}$. A simple graph on $[n]$ is a pair $([n],E)$ with $E\subseteq\binom{[n]}2$; a path is a finite vertex list with distinct vertices and each consecutive pair an edge. A graph is connected when every two vertices are joined by a path. A cycle is a vertex list $(v_0,\ldots,v_k)$ with $k\geq3$, $v_k=v_0$, $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$ distinct, and each consecutive pair an edge; a tree is a connected simple graph with no cycle. For $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\geq1$, let $\mathcal C_n$ be the set of connected simple graphs on $[n]$ and let $\mathcal T_n$ be the set of trees on $[n]$. The set $[n]$ is finite; its power set is finite, so its subset $\binom{[n]}2$ is finite; the power set of that edge set is finite as well. Each simple graph on $[n]$ is determined by an edge set in this last power set, so $\mathcal C_n$ and $\mathcal T_n$ are finite.

For an ordered tuple $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n)\in\Gamma^n$, put $f_{ij}:=-\mathbf 1_{\{\gamma_i\sim\gamma_j\}}$ and define the connected coefficient

$$U_n(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_{ij}.$$

For $n=1$, $\mathcal C_1$ contains the one-vertex graph and the empty edge product equals $1$. These are finite polynomial and coefficient definitions; they assert no convergence.

statement.before:
Let $(\Gamma,\sim,z)$ be an abstract polymer model. Suppose $a:\Gamma\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies

$$\sum_{\eta\sim\gamma}|z_\eta|e^{a_\eta}\leq a_\gamma\qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma).$$

For each fixed root $\gamma\in\Gamma$, the nonnegative rooted connected-cluster sum

$$R_\gamma:=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(n-1)!}\sum_{\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_n\in\Gamma}|U_n(\gamma,\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_n)|\prod_{j=2}^n|z_{\gamma_j}|$$

is well-defined as a possibly extended nonnegative series and satisfies $R_\gamma\leq e^{a_\gamma}$.
statement.proposed:
Let $(\Gamma,\sim,z)$ be an abstract polymer model, and let $a:\Gamma\to[0,\infty)$. Interpret each countable sum over polymer labels of nonnegative terms as the supremum of its finite subsums in $[0,+\infty]$, and interpret a nonnegative series as the supremum of its increasing partial sums in $[0,+\infty]$. Suppose

$$\sum_{\eta\sim\gamma}|z_\eta|e^{a_\eta}\leq a_\gamma\qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma).$$

For each fixed root $\gamma\in\Gamma$, define the nonnegative rooted connected-cluster sum

$$R_\gamma:=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(n-1)!}\sum_{\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_n\in\Gamma}|U_n(\gamma,\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_n)|\prod_{j=2}^n|z_{\gamma_j}|$$

Then $R_\gamma$ is well-defined as a possibly extended nonnegative series and satisfies $R_\gamma\leq e^{a_\gamma}$.

statement.before:
Let $\Gamma$ be countable with a reflexive symmetric incompatibility relation $\sim$. Let $V\subseteq\Gamma$ be finite, and fix weights $w_\gamma\in\mathbb C$, numbers $a_\gamma\geq0$, and a radius $r>0$. Call $X\subseteq V$ compatible when no two distinct elements of $X$ are related by $\sim$. Suppose there is $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ such that

$$\sum_{\substack{\eta\in V\\\eta\sim\gamma}}r|w_\eta|e^{a_\eta}\leq(1-\varepsilon)a_\gamma\qquad(\gamma\in V).$$

For $t\in\mathbb C$, define $Z_V(t):=\sum_{\substack{X\subseteq V\ X\text{ compatible}}}\prod_{\gamma\in X}(tw_\gamma)$. Define the connected series

$$L_V(t):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{t^n}{n!}\sum_{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\in V}U_n(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n)\prod_{i=1}^nw_{\gamma_i}.$$

Then $L_V$ converges absolutely and uniformly on every closed subdisc strictly inside $|t|<r$, may be differentiated there term by term, and satisfies $Z_V(t)=\exp(L_V(t))$ for $|t|<r$. Thus $Z_V$ has no zero in this disc and $L_V$ is its analytic logarithm normalized by $L_V(0)=0$.
statement.proposed:
Let $\Gamma$ be an at most countable set (finite or in bijection with $\mathbb N$) and let $\sim$ be a reflexive symmetric relation on $\Gamma$ ($\gamma\sim\gamma$ and $\gamma\sim\eta$ implies $\eta\sim\gamma$). Let $V\subseteq\Gamma$ be finite, and fix maps $w:V\to\mathbb C$ and $a:V\to[0,\infty)$ and a radius $r>0$. Call $X\subseteq V$ compatible when no two distinct elements of $X$ are related by $\sim$. Suppose there is $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ such that

$$\sum_{\substack{\eta\in V\\\eta\sim\gamma}}r|w_\eta|e^{a_\eta}\leq(1-\varepsilon)a_\gamma\qquad(\gamma\in V).$$

For $t\in\mathbb C$, define $Z_V(t):=\sum_{\substack{X\subseteq V\\\text{and }X\text{ is compatible}}}\prod_{\gamma\in X}(tw_\gamma)$. Define the connected series

$$L_V(t):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{t^n}{n!}\sum_{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\in V}U_n(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n)\prod_{i=1}^nw_{\gamma_i}.$$

Then $L_V$ converges absolutely and uniformly on every closed subdisc strictly inside $|t|<r$, may be differentiated there term by term, and satisfies $Z_V(t)=\exp(L_V(t))$ for $|t|<r$. Thus $Z_V$ has no zero in this disc. Here an analytic logarithm of $Z_V$ on the disc means a holomorphic function $L$ with $\exp(L(t))=Z_V(t)$ there; the logarithm $L_V$ is normalized by $L_V(0)=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. All displayed integrals use Lebesgue measure. Let $d\geq1$, let $v:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be an even Borel pair potential with no $-\infty$ values, and suppose it is stable with constant $B\geq0$. Fix $\beta>0$, set $e^{-c(+\infty)}:=0$ for every $c>0$, define the Mayer function $f_\beta(x):=e^{-\beta v(x)}-1$, and suppose

$$C_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f_\beta(x)|\,dx<\infty.$$

For $n\geq2$, let $\mathcal C_n$ be the connected simple graphs on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and put

$$U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_\beta(x_i-x_j).$$

For every configuration $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n$,

$$|U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)|\leq e^{2\beta Bn}\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(T)}|f_\beta(x_i-x_j)|,$$

where $\mathcal T_n$ is the set of labelled trees on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. In particular,

$$\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^{n-1}}|U_n(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)|\,dx_2\cdots dx_n\leq e^{2\beta Bn}n^{n-2}C_\beta^{\,n-1}.$$
statement.proposed:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. All displayed integrals use Lebesgue measure. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\geq2$ and write $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. A simple graph on $[n]$ is $([n],E)$ with $E$ a set of unordered two-element subsets of $[n]$; a path is a finite vertex list with distinct vertices and consecutive pairs in $E$; connected means every two vertices are joined by a path; a cycle is a vertex list $(v_0,\ldots,v_k)$ with $k\geq3$, $v_k=v_0$, $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$ distinct, and consecutive pairs in $E$; a tree is a connected graph with no cycle; a forest is a graph with no cycle. Finite sums and products over graph, edge, vertex, and subset sets below are enumeration-independent; the empty sum is $0$ and the empty product is $1$. Fix $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d\geq1$, let $v:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be an even Borel pair potential with no $-\infty$ values, and suppose it is stable with constant $B\in\mathbb R$, $B\geq0$. Fix $\beta\in\mathbb R$ with $\beta>0$, set $e^{-c(+\infty)}:=0$ for every $c>0$, define the Mayer function $f_\beta(x):=e^{-\beta v(x)}-1$, and suppose

$$C_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f_\beta(x)|\,dx<\infty.$$

Let $\mathcal C_n$ be the connected simple graphs on $[n]$ and let $\mathcal T_n$ be the trees on $[n]$. These families are finite because $[n]$ has finitely many unordered two-element subsets and each graph is determined by a subset of those edges. A spanning tree of a finite graph is a tree with the same vertex set and a subset of its edges. A leaf is a vertex incident to exactly one edge. Put

$$U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_\beta(x_i-x_j).$$

For every configuration $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n$,

$$|U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)|\leq e^{2\beta Bn}\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(T)}|f_\beta(x_i-x_j)|,$$

where $\mathcal T_n$ is the set of labelled trees on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. In particular,

$$\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^{n-1}}|U_n(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)|\,dx_2\cdots dx_n\leq e^{2\beta Bn}n^{n-2}C_\beta^{\,n-1}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. All displayed integrals use Lebesgue measure. Fix $d\geq1$, an even Borel pair potential $v:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ with no $-\infty$ values, stable with constant $B\geq0$, and $\beta>0$. Put $e^{-c(+\infty)}=0$ for every $c>0$, $f_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta v(x)}-1$, and $C_\beta=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f_\beta(x)|\,dx<\infty$. For $n\geq2$, use

$$U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_\beta(x_i-x_j),$$

where $\mathcal C_n$ is the set of connected simple graphs on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$; set $U_1=1$. For $L>0$, let $\Lambda_L=[-L,L]^d$ and write $|\Lambda_L|:=\lambda_d(\Lambda_L)=(2L)^d$; define

$$\Xi_L(z):=\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^N}{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}\exp\!\left(-\beta\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}v(x_i-x_j)\right)\,dx_1\cdots dx_N,$$

with the $N=0$ term equal to $1$. Set $b_1(L)=1$ and, for $n\geq2$,

$$b_n(L):=\frac1{n!|\Lambda_L|}\int_{\Lambda_L^n}U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\,dx_1\cdots dx_n.$$

Also set $b_1=1$ and, for $n\geq2$,

$$b_n:=\frac1{n!}\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^{n-1}}U_n(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)\,dx_2\cdots dx_n.$$

Let $\mathcal D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|e^{2\beta B+1}C_\beta<1\}$ when $C_\beta>0$, and let $\mathcal D=\mathbb C$ when $C_\beta=0$. On $\mathcal D$, the finite-volume connected pressure series $p_L(z):=\sum_{n\geq1}b_n(L)z^n$ and the limiting Mayer pressure series $p(z):=\sum_{n\geq1}b_nz^n$ converge absolutely and locally uniformly, are differentiable term by term, and satisfy

$$\Xi_L(z)=\exp\!\bigl(|\Lambda_L|p_L(z)\bigr),\qquad \lim_{L\to\infty}p_L(z)=p(z).$$

The convergence and derivative limits are uniform on every compact subdisc of $\mathcal D$. The pressure limit here is along centered cubes only.

Fix $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d\geq1$, an even Borel pair potential $v:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ with no $-\infty$ values, stable with constant $B\in\mathbb R$, $B\geq0$, and inverse parameter $\beta\in\mathbb R$ with $\beta>0$. Put $e^{-c(+\infty)}=0$ for every $c>0$, $f_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta v(x)}-1$, and $C_\beta=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f_\beta(x)|\,dx<\infty$. For each $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\geq2$, use

$$U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_\beta(x_i-x_j),$$

where $\mathcal C_n$ is the set of connected simple graphs on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$; set $U_1=1$. For $L\in\mathbb R$ with $L>0$, let $\Lambda_L=[-L,L]^d$ and write $|\Lambda_L|:=\lambda_d(\Lambda_L)=(2L)^d$; define

$$\Xi_L(z):=\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^N}{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}\exp\!\left(-\beta\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}v(x_i-x_j)\right)\,dx_1\cdots dx_N,$$

with the $N=0$ term equal to $1$. Set $b_1(L)=1$ and, for $n\geq2$,

$$b_n(L):=\frac1{n!|\Lambda_L|}\int_{\Lambda_L^n}U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\,dx_1\cdots dx_n.$$

Also set $b_1=1$ and, for $n\geq2$,

$$b_n:=\frac1{n!}\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^{n-1}}U_n(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)\,dx_2\cdots dx_n.$$

Let $\mathcal D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|e^{2\beta B+1}C_\beta<1\}$ when $C_\beta>0$, and let $\mathcal D=\mathbb C$ when $C_\beta=0$. $$\Xi_L(z)=\exp\!\bigl(|\Lambda_L|p_L(z)\bigr),\qquad \lim_{L\to\infty}p_L(z)=p(z).$$

Its stability constant may be chosen as $B=0$, the function $x\mapsto e^{-\beta v_a(x)}-1$ is $-1$ on the open ball $B(0,a):=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:|x|<a\}$ and $0$ elsewhere, and its absolute integral is $C_\beta=|B(0,a)|$. statement.proposed: Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d\geq1$, a hard-core diameter $a\in\mathbb R$ with $a>0$, and $\beta\in\mathbb R$ with $\beta>0$. For $x=(x_j)_{j<d}\in\mathbb R^d$, write $\|x\|_2:=\sqrt{\sum_{j<d}x_j^2}$, and let $B(0,a):=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2<a\}$. Let $\lambda_d$ denote Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^d$. Define the hard-core pair potential $v_a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ by $v_a(x)=+\infty$ when $\|x\|_2<a$ and $v_a(x)=0$ when $\|x\|_2\geq a$. statement.before:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of values of a scalar control parameter $\theta$, expressed in one fixed unit if it is dimensional. Let $(N_n)_{n\ge1}$ be positive integers with $N_n\to\infty$, interpreted as finite system sizes such as site counts. A finite-volume partition-function sequence on $I$ is a sequence of real-analytic functions $Z_n:I\to(0,\infty)$. For each $n$, define its dimensionless log partition density per site by $p_n(\theta):=N_n^{-1}\log Z_n(\theta)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. If the pointwise limit $p(\theta):=\lim_{n\to\infty}p_n(\theta)$ exists as a finite real number for every $\theta\in I$, call $p$ the infinite-volume pressure associated with this sequence. A point $\theta_c\in I$ is critical under the nonanalytic-pressure criterion exactly when there do not exist $\epsilon>0$ with $(\theta_c-\epsilon,\theta_c+\epsilon)\subseteq I$ and real coefficients $(a_k)_{k\ge0}$ such that $p(\theta)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k(\theta-\theta_c)^k$ throughout that interval. Finite-volume analyticity and a finite-size maximum of a derivative do not, by themselves, establish criticality under this definition.

This is one precise thermodynamic criticality criterion; it makes no claim that a particular interacting model satisfies it. A divergent correlation length is a separate criterion and is not identified with pressure nonanalyticity without an additional theorem.
statement.proposed:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of values of a scalar control parameter $\theta$, expressed in one fixed unit if it is dimensional. A function $g:I\to\mathbb R$ is **real analytic** if for every $\theta_0\in I$ there are $\epsilon>0$ and real coefficients $(a_k)_{k\ge0}$ such that $(\theta_0-\epsilon,\theta_0+\epsilon)\subseteq I$, the series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k(\theta-\theta_0)^k$ converges there, and its sum equals $g(\theta)$ throughout that interval. Let $(N_n)_{n\ge1}$ be positive integers with $N_n\to\infty$, interpreted as finite system sizes such as site counts. A finite-volume partition-function sequence on $I$ is a sequence of real-analytic functions $Z_n:I\to(0,\infty)$. For each $n$, define its dimensionless log partition density per site by $p_n(\theta):=N_n^{-1}\log Z_n(\theta)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. If the pointwise limit $p(\theta):=\lim_{n\to\infty}p_n(\theta)$ exists as a finite real number for every $\theta\in I$, call $p$ the infinite-volume pressure associated with this sequence. A point $\theta_c\in I$ is critical under the nonanalytic-pressure criterion exactly when there do not exist $\epsilon>0$ with $(\theta_c-\epsilon,\theta_c+\epsilon)\subseteq I$ and real coefficients $(a_k)_{k\ge0}$ such that $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k(\theta-\theta_c)^k$ converges and equals $p(\theta)$ throughout that interval.

This definition specifies only the nonanalytic-pressure criterion and makes no claim that a particular model satisfies it.

statement.before:
Let $d\ge1$ and $L\ge1$ be integers, let $\Lambda_{d,L}:=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$, and represent every residue coordinate by its unique value in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Write $e_j$ for the $j$th coordinate class, and count the two terms $x+e_j$ and $x-e_j$ separately even when they coincide for $L=1$ or $L=2$. For a real function $f$ on $\Lambda_{d,L}$, define

$$(-\Delta f)(x):=\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(2f(x)-f(x+e_j)-f(x-e_j)\bigr).$$

Extend $-\Delta$ complex-linearly. For $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_d)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$, define $\chi_r(x):=\exp(2\pi i\,r\cdot x/L)$. With inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=L^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_{d,L}}f(x)\overline{g(x)}$, the $L^d$ characters $\chi_r$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb C^{\Lambda_{d,L}}$ and satisfy

$$-\Delta\chi_r=\lambda_r\chi_r,\qquad \lambda_r=4\sum_{j=1}^d\sin^2(\pi r_j/L).$$

Consequently $-\Delta$ is real symmetric positive semidefinite, and for $m^2>0$ and $\kappa>0$ the matrix $m^2I_{\Lambda_{d,L}}+\kappa(-\Delta)$ is real symmetric positive definite with eigenvalues $m^2+4\kappa\sum_j\sin^2(\pi r_j/L)>0$.
statement.proposed:
Let $d,L\ge1$ be integers and let $\Lambda_{d,L}:=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$, where $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$ is the quotient set of integers modulo $L$. Use the quotient addition $[a]_L+[b]_L=[a+b]_L$ and additive inverse $-[a]_L=[-a]_L$, and define these operations coordinatewise on $\Lambda_{d,L}$. For $x\in\Lambda_{d,L}$, write $\widetilde x=(\widetilde x_1,\ldots,\widetilde x_d)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ for its unique coordinate representatives. For $1\le j\le d$, let $e_j\in\Lambda_{d,L}$ have coordinate $[1]_L$ in position $j$ and $[0]_L$ elsewhere. Count the two terms $x+e_j$ and $x-e_j$ separately even when they coincide for $L=1$ or $L=2$.

For a real-valued function $f:\Lambda_{d,L}\to\mathbb R$, define

$$(-\Delta f)(x):=\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(2f(x)-f(x+e_j)-f(x-e_j)\bigr).$$

For a complex-valued function, use the same formula for $-\Delta$, which is its complex-linear extension. Write $\mathbb C^{\Lambda_{d,L}}$ for the complex-valued functions on $\Lambda_{d,L}$ with pointwise vector operations. For $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_d)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$, define the function $\chi_r:\Lambda_{d,L}\to\mathbb C$ by

$$\chi_r(x):=\exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi i}{L}\sum_{j=1}^d r_j\widetilde x_j\right).$$

Use the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle:=L^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_{d,L}}f(x)\overline{g(x)}$. Identify real functions with coordinate vectors using the lexicographic order on the representatives $\widetilde x$, and let $I_{\Lambda_{d,L}}$ be the identity operator on those functions. A real matrix $A$ is symmetric when $A^{\mathsf T}=A$; a real symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite when $v^{\mathsf T}Av\ge0$ for every real vector $v$, and positive definite when $v^{\mathsf T}Av>0$ for every nonzero real vector $v$. For all $r,s\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$, the inner products satisfy $\langle\chi_r,\chi_s\rangle=1$ if $r=s$ and $0$ otherwise; every complex-valued function on $\Lambda_{d,L}$ is a unique linear combination of the functions $\chi_r$.

The exact Gaussian block-elimination algorithm has input:

- an integer $N\ge1$ and a real symmetric positive-definite precision matrix $K_0\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$;
- an integer $q\ge0$ and nested retained coordinate sets
  $$R_0=\{1,\ldots,N\}\supseteq R_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq R_q,$$
  each given in increasing coordinate order.

It starts at stage $0$ with the ordered coordinates $R_0$ and matrix $K_0$. For each $j=1,\ldots,q$, let $E_j=R_{j-1}\setminus R_j$ be the coordinates to eliminate at that stage.

1. If $E_j=\varnothing$, set $K_j=K_{j-1}$ and $\ell_j=0$.
2. If $E_j\ne\varnothing$, reorder the current coordinates as $R_j$ followed by $E_j$ and write the correspondingly permuted matrix
   $$K_{j-1}=\begin{pmatrix}A_j&B_j\\B_j^{\mathsf T}&C_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
   Solve the nonsingular system $C_jX_j=B_j^{\mathsf T}$, set
   $$K_j:=A_j-B_jX_j,\qquad \ell_j:=\frac{|E_j|}{2}\ln(2\pi)-\frac12\ln(\det C_j).$$

The output is $(K_q,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_q)$, with the accumulated log normalization $\sum_{j=1}^q\ell_j$. When $R_j=\varnothing$, $K_j$ is the unique empty $0\times0$ matrix and its determinant is defined to be $1$. This is an exact-arithmetic procedure on finite matrices. When $K_0$ is a precision of [[def-csm-frontier-gaussian-lattice]], the log increments are intended to record the normalization changes from eliminating the stated coordinates; a separate correctness theorem proves that finite-dimensional Gaussian identity.

$$\varphi_b(x):=b^{-(d-2)/2}\varphi'(x/b),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$

For a real smooth compactly supported field $\psi$, define its Gaussian gradient action and quartic integral by

$$S_2[\psi]:=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\nabla\psi(x)|^2\,d\lambda_d(x),\qquad Q_4[\psi]:=\frac1{4!}\int_{\mathbb R^d}\psi(x)^4\,d\lambda_d(x),$$

$$S_2[\varphi_b]=S_2[\varphi'],\qquad Q_4[\varphi_b]=b^{4-d}Q_4[\varphi'].$$

Define a continuous-time Markov chain as follows: the left reservoir changes $\eta_1$ from $0$ to $1$ at rate $\alpha$ and from $1$ to $0$ at rate $1-\alpha$; the right reservoir changes $\eta_2$ from $0$ to $1$ at rate $\beta$ and from $1$ to $0$ at rate $1-\beta$; and the bond swaps the two occupations at rate $1$. Its unique stationary law $\pi$ has

$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi}(\eta_1,\eta_2)=-\frac{(\alpha-\beta)^2}{18}.$$

Consequently, the stationary law is not a product when $\alpha\ne\beta$. This is an exact finite-chain correlation example, not a derivation of the continuum quasi-potential.
statement.proposed:
Fix $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1)$ and set $\Omega=\{0,1\}^2$. For $\eta=(\eta_1,\eta_2)\in\Omega$, let $\eta_i$ denote its $i$th coordinate. $$
(Lg)(\eta):=\alpha(1-\eta_1)\bigl(g(1,\eta_2)-g(\eta)\bigr)+(1-\alpha)\eta_1\bigl(g(0,\eta_2)-g(\eta)\bigr)+\beta(1-\eta_2)\bigl(g(\eta_1,1)-g(\eta)\bigr)+(1-\beta)\eta_2\bigl(g(\eta_1,0)-g(\eta)\bigr)+\mathbf 1_{\{\eta_1\ne\eta_2\}}\bigl(g(\eta_2,\eta_1)-g(\eta)\bigr).
$$

Here $\mathbf 1_A$ is $1$ when the condition $A$ holds and $0$ otherwise. This rate formula specifies the two reservoir flips and the bond swap of the finite-state continuous-time chain. Let $\mathcal P(\Omega)$ be the set of probability mass functions $\pi:\Omega\to[0,1]$, so $\sum_{\eta\in\Omega}\pi(\eta)=1$. A law $\pi\in\mathcal P(\Omega)$ is stationary when $\sum_{\eta\in\Omega}\pi(\eta)(Lg)(\eta)=0$ for every real $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $\mathbb E_\pi[g]:=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega}\pi(\eta)g(\eta)$, $m_i:=\mathbb E_\pi[\eta_i]$, and

$$\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(\eta_1,\eta_2):=\mathbb E_\pi[\eta_1\eta_2]-m_1m_2.$$

For $i=1,2$, the marginal is $\pi_i(a):=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega:\,\eta_i=a}\pi(\eta)$ for $a\in\{0,1\}$; $\pi$ is a product law when $\pi(a,b)=\pi_1(a)\pi_2(b)$ for all $a,b\in\{0,1\}$. The unique stationary law of this chain has

$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi}(\eta_1,\eta_2)=-\frac{(\alpha-\beta)^2}{18}.$$

Consequently, the stationary law is not a product when $\alpha\ne\beta$. This is an exact finite-chain correlation example, not a derivation of the continuum quasi-potential.
